# Caligrafy - Describe it. Approve it. Ship it.

**Your idea turned into a complete app.** Describe it to [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), approve the
plan, and Caligrafy ships it: the database, sign-in, web pages, a phone and tablet app, a REST API and tools for AI
agents, online at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`, with the code in your own GitHub repository.
## Get started quickly

With Claude Code, three steps take your idea to a complete app online:

| | You | Claude and Caligrafy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Describe it** | your idea, in a sentence: `/caligrafy-quill:idea A reading list where I rate the books I read` | turn it into a plan: a name, the tables, every feature, who may do what, the pages |
| **2. Approve it** | read the plan, change it, say OK | build every feature once, then check it from a page, REST and an AI agent |
| **3. Ship it** | approve the sign-ins in your browser | create your GitHub repository, deploy it, check it online |

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
claude
```
```
/caligrafy-quill:idea A reading list: I add books I want to read, mark them as read, and rate them from 1 to 5.
```
You say OK once, at the plan; after that you only approve sign-ins on GitHub's and Caligrafy Cloud's own pages,
which Claude opens for you. It never asks for a password or a key, and asks before spending credits. See
[Quickstart with Claude](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude).

**Start from a proven prompt.** The [marketplace of caligrafy.com](https://caligrafy.com/marketplace) offers apps that
already shipped, three ways: the prompt that recreates one with Caligrafy, its code, or the app managed for you. And
once yours is online, `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace` offers it there: you earn 25% of every sale. No time to build it?
[Submit your idea](https://caligrafy.com/ideas/new) and Caligrafy builds it for you.
## A complete app: build once, experience everywhere

What makes the app complete is how Caligrafy builds it. A feature (add a task, list the books, place an order) is
written once, as a **capability**: its inputs, its rules, who may use it, and what it does. Caligrafy then serves
that same capability to every way people and machines reach your application:

| Experience | How it uses the capability |
| --- | --- |
| **Web pages** | a page calls it and shows the result |
| **Vue apps** on desktop, tablet and phone | a generated JavaScript function: `await createTask({ title })` |
| **REST API** for other applications | `POST /api/tasks` |
| **AI agents** such as Claude or Cursor | an MCP tool: `create_task` |
| **Snap Cards and the assistant** | a card a person uses, and an assistant that answers with it: `Route::snap();` ([more](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant)) |

The same validation messages, the same permissions and the same audit log, whichever way it is called. You never
write a feature twice, and the experiences never drift apart.
## By hand: the same three steps

Everything Claude does is plain Caligrafy you can write yourself, with the same files Claude writes:

| Step | What you do | With |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Describe it** | a running project, your tables, and each feature written once with its rules | `.bin/caligrafer quickstart`, `create_db.sql` and a model, a capability (`php caligrafer.php service`) |
| **2. Approve it** | every experience and every permission, checked | `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::auth`, `Route::capabilities`, `Route::mcp`, `scope` and `level`, tests, the reviewer, `php caligrafer.php doctor` |
| **3. Ship it** | your application at a public address | the production `Dockerfile`, `php caligrafer.php cloud deploy` |

The [course](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course) teaches both ways: with Claude, and by hand, every
file typed by you.
## Quickstart by hand: 5 minutes

You need [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
(running). PHP, MySQL and Composer run in Docker.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --docker --example
```
`quickstart` installs the libraries, starts the server, creates the database and the framework tables, and adds a
**Tasks** example (the first start builds the PHP image: a few minutes). When it asks to delete the `.git` folder,
answer `y`: your project starts its own history. To use your own Apache and MySQL (MAMP, XAMPP, LAMP) instead, see
[Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart#composer).

**1. Use it on the web.** Open **http://localhost:8080/tasks**, add a task, tick it, rename it.

**2. Use it from another application.** The same tasks, over REST:
```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/tasks
```

**3. Use it from an AI agent.** Create a token and give it to Claude Code (or Cursor, below):
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "my agent" --scopes "*"
claude mcp add --transport http myapp http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <the token>"
```
Ask Claude "add a task to buy milk": it calls `create_task`, and the task appears on the web page.
In Cursor, add to `.cursor/mcp.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "myapp": { "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <the token>" } } } }
```

**4. Ship it.** Push the project to a GitHub repository (`git init`, commit, push), then:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud login                 # open the address it prints, approve the code
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud create myapp --repo https://github.com/<you>/myapp
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy myapp          # https://myapp.caligrafy.com
```
`cloud login` opens [deploy.caligrafy.com](https://deploy.caligrafy.com), where you sign in (or sign up) and approve.
Every new app is free for its first 30 minutes online. The Tasks example is open to everyone, online too: see
[Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online) before you share the address.
## Your first capability

A feature, by hand, is a table, a model, a capability and its routes. The list of a book catalog:

**`application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php`** (created by
`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListBooks --scope books:read`)
```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_books', description: 'Lists the books, 20 per page, each with its author.', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true)]
class ListBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer', 'page' => 'integer');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
        if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
            $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);
        }
        return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
    }
}
```
**`application/config/routing/web.php`**
```php
Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);   // a web page
Route::capabilities();                                                               // REST: POST /capabilities/list_books
Route::mcp();                                                                        // AI agents: the list_books tool
```
The same capability is also a function of the generated JavaScript client (`php caligrafer.php client`). The tutorial
[Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability) builds a complete
feature step by step: the table, the model, the page, a form and sign-in.
## What comes in the box

+ **Every experience:** server-rendered pages (Pug), Vue apps and a Vite single page application, installable mobile
  web apps, REST, and an MCP server for AI agents.
+ **One rule:** only capabilities touch your data. Pages get their data from capabilities in one line
  (`Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']])`), so a page, the API and an agent
  never follow different rules. Forms, sign-in, webhooks, downloads and anything else a browser asks are one line each too
  ([declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes): `Route::form`,
  `Route::auth`, `Route::webhook`, `Route::download`, `Route::action`): an application needs no controller.
+ **One look, or yours:** Caligrafy's look on every page: a light top bar with the Caligrafy mark, title bands, forms,
  rows and tiles, Caligrafy black for the main action, full-screen camera apps, the same on every device. Or pick one of 85 [design styles](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles)
  (`DESIGN_STYLE` in `.env`, or your own `DESIGN.md`) and let `/caligrafy-quill:design` restyle every page.
+ **Secure by design:** sign-in, passkeys and face login for people; scoped, revocable tokens for programs and
  agents; CSRF protection; an audit log of every change; server files never served.
+ **What large apps need:** [queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) with filters, paging,
  related rows in one query and transactions, [migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations), [background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs), [a cache](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caching),
  [tests for your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App), [dependency injection](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection), scheduled jobs and notifications.
+ **Fast:** in the same benchmark, Caligrafy 2.19 beats Symfony and Laravel on all 16 measures (requests per second,
  median and slowest response, memory, for plain text, JSON, a database query and an HTML page): an HTML page at
  2,887 requests per second, against 1,789 for Symfony and 324 for Laravel
  ([release notes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-2.19.0)).
+ **Batteries included:** card, ACH and crypto payments, OpenAI and open-model AI (Llama on Groq, OpenRouter,
  Ollama...), chatbots, face detection and machine learning in the browser, search and social metadata.
+ **Made for AI-assisted development:** a [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/10.-Claude-Code-Plugin)
  that knows the framework, builds features the Caligrafy way or a whole application from your idea, and puts it
  online, and `AGENTS.md` for other coding agents.
+ **Online in a few commands:** a production `Dockerfile` in every project, the database prepared at every start,
  and [Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#cloud):
  `php caligrafer.php cloud deploy` puts it at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`, every new app free for its first 30
  minutes, and `/caligrafy-quill:ship` does it all for you, from the GitHub repository to the check online.
+ **Sell what you built:** offer an app online on the [marketplace of caligrafy.com](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#marketplace):
  Caligrafy sells a prompt that recreates it and you earn 25% of every sale. `/caligrafy-quill:marketplace` reads
  your code, screenshots its key features and submits the listing (`php caligrafer.php cloud submit`).
+ **Tools:** `php caligrafer.php doctor` checks your setup and services, `call` tries a capability in one line,
  `migrate` changes the database, `test` runs your tests, `queue work` runs background jobs,
  `update` moves a project to the latest release in one command (keeping what you changed), `upgrade` updates its
  `application/` templates and tells you what to check, `version` tells you which release you run.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude -->

**Describe it. Approve it. Ship it.** You describe an application to [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) in a sentence, approve the plan Claude proposes, and Claude builds it the Caligrafy way (every feature written once, as a capability), checks it from every side, and puts it online at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`. You then use the same application from a web page, your phone, other programs over REST and AI agents.

It usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, most of it Claude working. The [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) does the setup by hand, with a ready-made example, in 5 minutes.

**Start from a proven prompt.** The [marketplace of caligrafy.com](https://caligrafy.com/marketplace) sells the prompts behind apps that already shipped: give one to `/caligrafy-quill:idea` instead of your own sentence.
## <a name="need"></a>What you need

+ [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), running
+ [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
+ A [GitHub](https://github.com/) account. An SSH key on GitHub, or the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) signed in, saves one step; without them, Claude installs the GitHub CLI (with Homebrew) and signs it in with a code you approve in your browser
+ An account on [Caligrafy Cloud](https://deploy.caligrafy.com/signup), or create it when Claude opens the page. Every new app is free for its first 30 minutes online
## <a name="start"></a>Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
claude
```
Trust the folder when Claude Code asks: that turns on the Caligrafy plugin that ships in the project (`.claude/settings.json`). Then give it your idea:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:idea A reading list: I add books I want to read with their author, mark them as read, and rate them from 1 to 5.
```
## <a name="steps"></a>Describe it. Approve it. Ship it.

You approve **once**, at the plan. Your OK covers the rest: setting the project up (the framework's `.git` makes way for your app's own history), building it, creating a private GitHub repository and putting it online. After that Claude does not ask you to run a command or copy a key: it opens your browser when only you can approve something, and asks before spending credits.

| | What Claude does | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Describe it** | | |
| The plan | turns the idea into a name, the tables, the capabilities (`list_`, `get_`, `create_`, `update_`, `delete_` per table, plus the actions the idea needs), who may do what (by default anyone reads and people who signed up change), the pages and some sample data; says what your OK lets it do | your idea, in a sentence |
| **2. Approve it** | | |
| Your OK | | read the plan, change it, say OK. Say "stop before putting it online" to review it locally first |
| Start | checks Docker and the ports, then `.bin/caligrafer quickstart`: the Docker server, the database, the framework tables, the `/capabilities` and `/mcp` routes | nothing |
| Build once | for each table a `create_db.sql` and a model; each feature as a capability (`php caligrafer.php service ...`); sign-in with `Route::auth`; the pages with `Route::page` and `Route::form`; the REST routes; the JavaScript client; a page where signed-in people create a token for their AI agents; tests | nothing |
| Check | `capabilities`, `call` on every capability, REST with and without sign-in, the page at desktop and phone width, MCP `tools/list` and `tools/call`, `test`, `doctor`, a review by the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent | nothing |
| Everywhere, locally | shows you the page at `http://localhost:8080`, a `curl` line and the line that connects an agent | try it if you like |
| **3. Ship it** (the `ship` skill) | | |
| GitHub | commits, creates the private repository and pushes: with your SSH key when GitHub knows it, else over HTTPS with the GitHub CLI, else after a browser approval | only if needed: enter the code GitHub shows in the page Claude opens |
| Online | signs in to Caligrafy Cloud (`cloud login`), creates the app, adds its read-only deploy key to the repository, deploys and checks the address | approve the code on the Caligrafy Cloud page Claude opens (sign up and confirm your email the first time) |

Claude never asks you for a password, a token or a key, and never prints one: approvals happen on GitHub's and Caligrafy Cloud's own pages. `/caligrafy-quill:ship <name>` puts any Caligrafy project online the same way, and puts it online again after a change.

### Check

Before you say OK to the plan:
+ the name is the one you want: it becomes `https://<name>.caligrafy.com` and the GitHub repository;
+ each table and capability is one you need, and nothing that changes data is open to everyone unless you want that.

Before you call it done:
+ the address Claude reports opens, you can sign up and sign in, and the main page adds and changes your data;
+ the `curl` line answers with your data;
+ `doctor` and the tests passed in Claude's report.
## <a name="result"></a>What you get

| Experience | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **Web page** | `https://<name>.caligrafy.com/`: sign up, then add and change your data |
| **Phone and tablet** | the same address, *Add to Home Screen*: it opens like an app |
| **REST API** for other programs | `curl -H "Accept: application/json" https://<name>.caligrafy.com/api/<things>` |
| **AI agents** (Claude, Cursor...) | sign in, create a token on the page, then paste the `claude mcp add ...` line it shows |
| **The code** | your GitHub repository: a Caligrafy project you can read, change and keep building, by hand or with Claude |

Every experience calls the same capabilities: the same rules, the same permissions, the same error messages.
## By hand

Every step Claude takes is a step you can take yourself: the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) sets the project up, [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability) builds a feature with its page, REST API, agent tools, sign-in and test, and [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online) ships it. The [course](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki) builds a whole application step by step.
## <a name="next"></a>Next

+ **Change it:** ask Claude for a new feature (`/caligrafy-quill:new-capability`), or edit the code yourself. A change to a table that already has data goes in a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations), which the deploy runs. Then `/caligrafy-quill:ship <name>`.
+ **Keep it online:** `php caligrafer.php cloud status <name>` shows the time left; `php caligrafer.php cloud extend <name> week` (2 credits) keeps it online a week. See [Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#cloud).
+ **Your own server instead:** `/caligrafy-quill:deploy <name> --own-server` prepares it for Coolify or Docker ([your own server](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#ownserver)).
+ **Learn what Claude did:** [How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works) in 5 minutes. Every skill is on the [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/10.-Claude-Code-Plugin) page.
## <a name="trouble"></a>Troubleshooting

| You see | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| `/caligrafy-quill:idea` is not a command | in `myapp`, run `php caligrafer.php plugin` (with PHP on your computer) or `.bin/caligrafer quickstart` (with Docker): it registers the project's plugin with Claude Code. Then restart `claude` there |
| Docker is not running | start Docker Desktop, then tell Claude to go on |
| A port is already in use (8080, 8077, 3306) | Claude gives this project other ports with a `docker-compose.override.yml` and uses them in every address |
| Your app's sign-up refuses an email address | by default usernames are letters and digits, for example `sam42` (Caligrafy Cloud's own accounts use your email). To sign in with an email, say so in the idea, or ask Claude: *"people sign in with their email, kept in the username column"* ([Signing in with an email](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#emailsignin)) |
| The name is taken on Caligrafy Cloud or GitHub | Claude proposes another name |
| The browser page did not open | Claude prints its address: open it, approve the code, and Claude goes on |
| Caligrafy Cloud says *Confirm your email first* | open the link of the email from Caligrafy (look in spam), then sign in on the same page; it can send the link again |
| You forgot your Caligrafy password | *Forgot your password?* on the sign-in page emails a 6-digit code, then you choose a new password |
| The free 30 minutes of the app are used | say yes when Claude asks to spend credits; to buy some, Claude opens the Stripe page (`cloud credits 5`) |
| The page works locally but its calls are refused online (`[ERROR 1004] Access Denied: the legacy API key is turned off`) | the page sends the shared API key, which Caligrafy Cloud turns off: ask Claude to call the routes with the JavaScript client or `apiHeaders()` |

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart -->

The Quickstart creates a Caligrafy project on your computer and shows one feature, a list of tasks, used three ways: from a web page, from another program over REST, and from an AI agent such as Claude or Cursor. It takes about 5 minutes. Every other page of this wiki starts from the project it creates.
## <a name="claude"></a>With Claude

To build your own idea instead of the Tasks example, with Claude Code doing the work, follow the [Quickstart with Claude](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude):

```text
/caligrafy-quill:idea A reading list: I add books with their author, mark them as read and rate them from 1 to 5.
```

Claude sets the project up with the same command as step 2 below (without the example), then builds, checks and ships the app.
## By hand

### <a name="need"></a>What you need

+ [Git](https://git-scm.com/)
+ [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), running
+ The ports `8080` (the site), `8077` (phpMyAdmin) and `3306` (MySQL) free on your computer. If one is taken, see [Troubleshooting](#trouble) first.

PHP 8.5, Apache, MySQL 8.4 and phpMyAdmin run in Docker: you do not install them. Without Docker, see [Other ways](#composer).

### <a name="start"></a>1. Get the framework

```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
```

`myapp` is the folder of your project. Choose any name.

### 2. Set the project up

```bash
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --docker --example
```

It asks first:
```text
quickstart initializes the project, which deletes the .git folder of the framework (your project starts its own history).
Continue? [y/N]
```
Answer `y`. The `.git` folder is the history of the framework; your project starts its own in [Put it online](#online).

The command installs the PHP libraries (with your Composer, or Composer in Docker), builds and starts the Docker server (the first build takes from under a minute to a few minutes), then sets the project up inside it. It ends with:
```text
Caligrafy quickstart (Docker server)
  OK    Project: application/ and .env created, keys generated
  OK    .env: the database of the Docker server (caligrafy)
  OK    Database: caligrafy ready on mysql
  OK    Framework tables: tokens, audit log, job runs, jobs, cache, migrations
  OK    Routes: /capabilities (JS client), /mcp (AI agents), /notify (notification emails)
  OK    Example: 9 file(s) added (application/services/Tasks, models/Tasks, views/Tasks, public/js/tasks.js)
  OK    Example table: tasks
  OK    Example client: public/js/capabilities.js generated

Ready. Next:
  - open http://localhost:8080/tasks: the same tasks over REST (http://localhost:8080/api/tasks) and MCP (http://localhost:8080/mcp)
  - write a capability: php caligrafer.php service Books/CreateBook --scope books:write
  - let an AI agent use it: php caligrafer.php token create "my agent" --scopes "*"
    claude mcp add --transport http myapp http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
  - check everything: php caligrafer.php doctor
```

| Line | What it did |
| --- | --- |
| Project | ran `php caligrafer.php initialize`: copied the templates to `application/`, created `.env` with a new `APP_KEY` and `API_KEY`, deleted `.git` |
| .env | set `DB_ACTIVATE=true`, `DB_HOST=mysql` and `DB_DATABASE=caligrafy` |
| Database, Framework tables | created the database and the tables of personal access tokens, the audit log, jobs, the cache and migrations (`php caligrafer.php platform install`) |
| Routes | added `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')`, `Route::mcp('/mcp')` and `Route::notifications()` to `application/config/routing/web.php` |
| Example | added the Tasks example (`--example`): five capabilities, a model, a page, the `tasks` table, its routes and the JavaScript client |

Leave out `--example` for an empty project. Every step can be run again: `quickstart` only does what is missing and never overwrites your files.

When Claude Code is installed on your computer, the command also registers the project's Claude Code plugin and prints `Claude Code plugin: caligrafy-quill@caligrafy-<name>, read from this folder`.

### <a name="use"></a>3. Use the feature on a web page

Open **http://localhost:8080/tasks**. Add a task, tick it done, rename it, delete it. Submit an empty task: the page shows `The Title field is required`.

### 4. Use it from another program, over REST

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"title": "Try the quickstart"}' http://localhost:8080/api/tasks
```
```json
{"data":{"id":1,"title":"Try the quickstart","notes":"","done":0,"created_at":"2026-11-07 23:14:07","modified_at":"2026-11-07 23:14:07"}}
```
```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8080/api/tasks
```
```json
{"data":[{"id":1,"title":"Try the quickstart","notes":"","done":0,"created_at":"2026-11-07 23:14:07","modified_at":"2026-11-07 23:14:07"}]}
```
A task without a title gets `422` and the same message as the page:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' http://localhost:8080/api/tasks
```
```json
{"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"Some of the inputs are invalid","fields":{"title":"The Title field is required"}}}
```
Always send `Accept: application/json`: without it, a `POST` is treated as a form and refused with `[ERROR 3000] Security Error - Cross Site Forgery` (403).

### 5. Use it from an AI agent

Agents sign in with a **personal access token**. Create one that may read and change tasks:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "my agent" --scopes tasks:read,tasks:write
```
```text
 Token #1 "my agent" created with tasks:read tasks:write

 cq_1_...

 It is shown only now: store it as a secret (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
```
Copy the `cq_...` value. Give it to **Claude Code**:
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http myapp http://localhost:8080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer cq_1_..."
```
or to **Cursor**, in `.cursor/mcp.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "myapp": { "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer cq_1_..." } } } }
```
Ask the agent "add a task to buy milk". It calls the `create_task` tool. The open `/tasks` page shows the new task within 3 seconds, without a reload.

To check the endpoint without an agent:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_1_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' http://localhost:8080/mcp
```
The answer lists the tools this token may use: `create_task`, `delete_task`, `get_task`, `list_tasks`, `register_user`, `update_task` (`register_user` is the public sign-up of the project).

### 6. Check the project

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor
```
The last line is:
```text
 15 OK, 0 WARN, 0 FAIL, 6 SKIP
```
The `SKIP` lines are the services you have not configured yet (OpenAI, Groq, Stripe, Coinbase, Watson, mail).

### Check

+ `http://localhost:8080/tasks` opens, and a task added there is listed by `curl http://localhost:8080/api/tasks`.
+ An empty title gets `The Title field is required` on the page, over REST and from the agent.
+ `doctor` ends with `0 FAIL`.
## <a name="what"></a>What you just used

The Tasks feature is written once, as five **capabilities** (one class per action) in `application/services/Tasks/`: `list_tasks`, `get_task`, `create_task`, `update_task` and `delete_task`. The page, the REST API and the agent all call them, so the rules are the same everywhere. These lines of `application/config/routing/web.php` serve them:

```php
    // BUILD ONCE: every capability, for the JS client and AI agents
    Route::capabilities('/capabilities');   // the capabilities for the JS client of the Vue apps
    Route::mcp('/mcp');                     // the capabilities as tools for AI agents (personal access tokens)
    Route::notifications();                 // the pages notification emails link to (confirm, unsubscribe)

    // TASKS EXAMPLE: one set of capabilities (application/services/Tasks) served to every channel
    Route::page('/tasks', 'Tasks/index');   // the web page (public/js/tasks.js)
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/tasks', 'list_tasks');                // REST
    Route::capability('GET', '/api/tasks/{id}', 'get_task');
    Route::capability('POST', '/api/tasks', 'create_task');
    Route::capability('PUT', '/api/tasks/{id}', 'update_task');
    Route::capability('DELETE', '/api/tasks/{id}', 'delete_task');
```

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `application/services/Tasks/*.php` | the five capabilities |
| `application/models/Tasks/Task.php`, `create_db.sql` | the model of the `tasks` table, and the script that created it |
| `application/views/Tasks/index.pug` | the page |
| `public/js/tasks.js` | the page's script: it calls the capabilities through `public/js/capabilities.js`, the generated JavaScript client |

[How Caligrafy works](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works) explains the idea in a few minutes. [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability) builds a feature of your own.

> **The example is open to everyone.** Its capabilities are `public: true`: anyone who reaches the site can add and delete tasks, without signing in. Before you put an application online, remove `public: true` from the capabilities that change data and turn on sign-in: [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability#secure) shows how.
## <a name="everyday"></a>Every day

| To | Run (in the project folder) |
| --- | --- |
| start the server | `.bin/caligrafer server start` (or `docker compose up -d dev-box`) |
| stop it | `.bin/caligrafer server stop` (or `docker compose stop`) |
| run a Caligrafer command | `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php <command>` ([every command](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer)) |
| look at the database | phpMyAdmin at http://localhost:8077, user `root`, password `root` |

`server start` prints:
```text
Caligrafy Server successfully started.

 Hostname: http://localhost:8080
 phpmyadmin: http://localhost:8077
 mysql: localhost:3306 (from your computer; mysql:3306 from the containers)
 mysql username: root 
 mysql password: root 
```
Stop the server with `stop`, never `docker compose down`: the MySQL container keeps its data only until it is removed.
## <a name="online"></a>Put it online

The same project runs online with [Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#cloud) at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`, built from its GitHub repository. Every new app is free for its first 30 minutes online.

1. **Your code on GitHub.** `quickstart` removed the framework's history, so start yours, then create a repository on GitHub (private works too) and push to it:
    ```bash
    git init -b main
    git add -A
    git commit -m "My app"
    git remote add origin https://github.com/<you>/myapp.git
    git push -u origin main
    ```
2. **Sign in to Caligrafy Cloud.** Create an account at [deploy.caligrafy.com](https://deploy.caligrafy.com/signup) and confirm your email. Then:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud login
    ```
    It prints a code and an address: open the address, check the code and approve it. In Docker it does not open the browser for you.
3. **Create the app and deploy it:**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud create myapp --repo https://github.com/<you>/myapp
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy myapp
    ```
    For a private repository, `cloud create` prints a read-only deploy key (also saved in `.caligrafy/myapp-deploy-key.pub`): add it to the repository on GitHub (*Settings > Deploy keys*) before `cloud deploy`. `cloud deploy` follows the build, which takes a few minutes, and ends with the address.

Open `https://myapp.caligrafy.com/tasks`: the production image ran `php caligrafer.php deploy`, which created the tables, when it started. `/caligrafy-quill:ship` in Claude Code does all three steps for you.

> **Online, the Tasks example is open to everyone too.** That is fine for a 30-minute try; for longer, remove `public: true` first. When the free time ends the app is paused; `php caligrafer.php cloud extend myapp week` (2 credits) brings it back.
## <a name="next"></a>Next

+ **Build your own feature:** [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability) adds a Bookshelf: its table, its capabilities, a page with a form, a REST API, agent tools, sign-in and a test.
+ **Remove the example:** delete `application/services/Tasks`, `application/models/Tasks`, `application/views/Tasks` and `public/js/tasks.js`, the `TASKS EXAMPLE` lines of `application/config/routing/web.php`, then run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php client` again.
+ **Every command:** the [Caligrafer](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer) page.
## <a name="trouble"></a>Troubleshooting

| You see | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| `Docker is not running: start Docker Desktop, then run .bin/caligrafer quickstart again.` | Start Docker Desktop, wait until it says it is running, run the command again |
| `port is already allocated` (8080, 8077 or 3306) | Another server uses the port. Stop it, or give this project other ports with a `docker-compose.override.yml` next to `docker-compose.yaml` (below), and use those ports in every address. `quickstart` still prints `8080` |
| The PHP image build fails or stops (`Killed`) | A slow or filtered network, or too little memory for Docker: run the command again, or give Docker more memory |
| `FAIL  Database: could not reach mysql` | MySQL takes a few seconds on its first start: run `.bin/caligrafer quickstart --docker --example` again |
| `STOP  initialize deletes the .git folder of the framework` | You answered no: run the command again and answer `y` |
| The page is empty or shows an error | `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor` lists what is wrong, with a fix for each line |

**Other ports.** The site, phpMyAdmin and MySQL on 8081, 8078 and 3307 (Docker Compose 2.24 or later reads `!override`):
```yaml
# docker-compose.override.yml
services:
  dev-box:
    ports: !override
      - "8081:80"
  phpmyadmin:
    ports: !override
      - "8078:80"
  mysql:
    ports: !override
      - "3307:3306"
```
## Other ways

### <a name="composer"></a><a name="nodocker"></a>With Composer, on MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP

Use this when you already run a local Apache and MySQL (MAMP, XAMPP, or Apache and MySQL on Linux) and have PHP 8.3+ and [Composer](https://getcomposer.org). Create the project **in the web folder** of that server (MAMP: the folder of its Apache settings, `htdocs` by default; XAMPP: `htdocs`; LAMP: `/var/www/html`):
```bash
composer create-project caligrafy/caligrafy-quill myapp
cd myapp
.bin/caligrafer quickstart --local --example
```
`composer create-project` downloads the latest release and its libraries, then prints where the project will be served and the next command. `quickstart --local`:

1. initializes the project (there is no `.git` to delete in a release);
2. gives the project its address (`APP_ROOT`, its path in the web folder). With MAMP it reads MAMP's own settings: its web folder, its Apache port and its MySQL port;
3. asks for the MySQL settings, with the server's defaults (MAMP: `127.0.0.1`, port `8889`, `root` / `root`; XAMPP: `127.0.0.1`, `3306`, `root` and no password; LAMP: `localhost`, `3306`, `root` and no password) and a database named after the folder;
4. creates the database, the framework tables, the routes and the example, like the Docker quickstart.

Then open the address it prints, for example `http://localhost:8888/myapp/tasks` with a default MAMP.

+ The project is elsewhere: add `--url http://localhost/<folder>` to give its address.
+ No terminal to answer the questions (a script): it skips the database. `--db-defaults` takes the server's defaults; `--no-db` skips the database on purpose.
+ The MySQL settings do not work: it sets `DB_ACTIVATE=false` again, so that the pages still open, and says what to fix in `.env`.
+ On **Windows** (XAMPP, MAMP for Windows): `php caligrafer.php quickstart --example`.
+ Without `--local` or `--docker`, `.bin/caligrafer quickstart` uses the local server when Apache (`httpd` or `apache2`) is running and PHP is installed, else Docker.

### <a name="ownmysql"></a>Your own PHP and MySQL, settings first

When you know the MySQL settings, write them before `quickstart` and nothing is asked:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git myapp
cd myapp
composer install
cp framework/settings/.env.example .env
```
In `.env`, set `DB_ACTIVATE=true`, `DB_HOST` (`127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, to use `DB_PORT`), `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME` and `DB_PASSWORD`. Then:
```bash
php caligrafer.php quickstart --example --yes --url http://localhost/myapp
```
`--yes` deletes the framework's `.git` without asking; `--url` is the address your Apache serves the folder at. The output is the one of step 2, with `OK    Local server: your server, http://localhost/myapp (APP_ROOT=myapp)` and `OK    Database: <DB_DATABASE> ready on 127.0.0.1` in place of the Docker lines. Apache must allow the project's `.htaccess` (`AllowOverride All`) with `mod_rewrite` and `mod_headers`: see [Getting Started](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/1.-Getting-Started#protecting-your-server-files).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/How-Caligrafy-Works -->

Caligrafy is a PHP framework built on one idea: **build once, experience everywhere**. You write each feature of your application once, as a **capability**, and every way people and programs reach the application (web pages, Vue apps, a REST API, AI agents) calls that same capability. This page explains the few ideas behind it in about 5 minutes. To try it first, follow the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart).

You can build with Claude Code, which follows these ideas for you (`/caligrafy-quill:idea`, see the [Quickstart with Claude](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart-with-Claude)), or by hand, following [Your first capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability). Both produce the same project.
## <a name="capability"></a>A capability is a feature, written once

A **capability** is one thing your application can do: list the books, add a book, lend a book. It is a small PHP class in `application/services/` that says four things:

| What | Where in the class | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| its name and what it does | the `#[Capability]` attribute | `name: 'create_book'`, `description: 'Adds a book...'` |
| the inputs it accepts and their rules | `$rules` | `'title' => 'required\|max_len,200'` |
| who may use it | the `#[Capability]` attribute | `scope: 'books:write'`, `level: 1`, or `public: true` |
| the work | `handle()` | save the book, return it |

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;

#[Capability(
    name: 'create_book',
    description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author.',
    scope: 'books:write'
)]
class CreateBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'title' => 'required|max_len,200',
        'published_year' => 'required|integer|min_numeric,1450|max_numeric,current_year',
        'author_id' => 'required|integer|exists,authors.id'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $id = Book::insert($input);   // one INSERT, every value bound
        return Book::with('author')->find($id);
    }
}
```

A capability returns data, or refuses with a `ServiceError` (`invalid`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`). It does not draw a page, redirect or answer HTTP itself. That is what lets every experience use it. (A few requests only make sense in a browser, such as a sign-in between two sites: those are [web-only capabilities](#webonly).) Inside it, the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) reads the data: `Book::with('author')->where('author_id', 2)->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)`.
## <a name="experiences"></a>Experiences call the capabilities

An **experience** is a way to reach your application. Each one is shaped for its audience, and each one calls the same capabilities. One line of `application/config/routing/web.php` connects each:

| Experience | Who uses it | How it reaches `create_book` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web pages (Pug) | people in a browser | the page gets its data from a read-only capability (`Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Bookshelf/book', ['data' => ['book' => 'get_book']])`), and its form posts to `Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' => '/books/{id}'])` |
| Vue apps and page scripts | people on desktop, tablet and phone | `await createBook({ title, published_year, author_id })` from the generated JavaScript client (`php caligrafer.php client`, served by `Route::capabilities('/capabilities')`) |
| REST API | other programs | `POST /api/books` (`Route::capability('POST', '/api/books', 'create_book')`), or `POST /capabilities/create_book` |
| AI agents (MCP) | Claude, Cursor and other agents | the `create_book` tool (`Route::mcp('/mcp')`) |
| The command line and tests | you | `php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Kindred published_year=1979 author_id=2`, `$this->call('create_book', [...])` in a test |

The other needs of a web application are one line each, and call capabilities too ([Declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes)): `Route::auth()` for sign-in, sign-out and sign-up, `Route::webhook()` for the events a payment provider posts, `Route::download()` for a CSV export or many files as one ZIP, `Route::redirect()` for an address that moved, and `Route::action()` for whatever a page or a form cannot say. Every request of the application is declared this way: there is no controller to write. Work that runs later or on a timer is a capability too, pushed as a [background job](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) or named in a [schedule](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs).

### <a name="webonly"></a>Web-only capabilities

Most features belong on every experience. A few belong to the browser: a sign-in between two sites, a face sign-in, a page that chooses where to go, a gate, a page that creates a payment. They need the session, or they answer with a page or a redirect. Such a capability is declared `webOnly: true`, and returns a `Caligrafy\Web`:

```php
#[Capability(name: 'open_author_books', description: 'Opens the books of an author.', readOnly: true, public: true, webOnly: true)]
class OpenAuthorBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'required|integer');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $books = $this->capability('list_books', array('author_id' => $input['author_id']), $context);
        return $books['total'] == 1 ? Web::redirect('/books/' . $books['data'][0]['id']) : Web::view('Bookshelf/books', array('books' => $books));
    }
}
```

`Route::action('/authors/{author_id}/books', 'open_author_books');` serves it, and **nothing else reaches it**: REST, MCP, the JavaScript client, the command line, `Route::page` and `Route::form` answer "There is no capability". It keeps the rules of every capability (who may call it, its inputs, its audit log). It may also read the session, sign people in, and change data on a `GET`, which is why it stays on the web. What other experiences need stays in plain capabilities, which it calls with `$this->capability()`.
## <a name="identity"></a>Who is calling

Every call knows who makes it, in its `Context`:

+ **People** sign in (password, passkey). A capability can ask for a minimum permission level, `level: 1`, read from the `permissions` column of `users`.
+ **Programs and AI agents** use a **personal access token** (`php caligrafer.php token create "my agent" --scopes books:read,books:write`). A token reaches only the capabilities its scopes allow, can expire, and can be revoked on its own.
+ **Public** capabilities (`public: true`) need neither: use it for data anyone may read.
## <a name="call"></a>What happens on every call

Whatever the experience, every call goes through the same steps:

1. **Find** the capability (unknown: `404`).
2. **Check who calls**: signed in or a token (`401`), with the scope and the level (`403`), unless the capability is public.
3. **Check the inputs** against `$rules`, keeping only the declared inputs (`422`, with a message per field).
4. **Run** `handle()`.
5. **Record** it in the audit log: every change and every refusal (`php caligrafer.php audit`). Reads that succeed are not recorded.

So a book without an author gets `The Author Id field is required` on the web page, over REST and for an agent, and a token without `books:write` is refused everywhere.
## <a name="online"></a>From your computer to the internet

The project you build is the project you put online, unchanged:

+ a production `Dockerfile` at its root builds it (PHP, Apache, your libraries, no development tools);
+ when the container starts, `php caligrafer.php deploy` creates the framework tables, runs every new or changed `create_db.sql`, then the [migrations](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations) that never ran, and Apache starts;
+ `php caligrafer.php cloud deploy <name>` puts it at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com` with [Caligrafy Cloud](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#cloud), or you run the same image on [your own server](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online#ownserver).

Online, every experience calls the same capabilities with the same rules. With Claude, the whole path is three steps: **describe it** (the idea becomes a plan), **approve it** (your OK; Claude builds once and checks every experience) and **ship it** (GitHub and Caligrafy Cloud).
## <a name="where"></a>Where things live

```text
application/
├── services/      the capabilities: each feature, once (Users/: the people who sign in)
├── models/        one class per table, with the create_db.sql that creates it
├── migrations/    changes to tables that hold data: numbered SQL files, each run once (php caligrafer.php migrate)
├── views/         the web pages (Pug), on the layout default/master/site
├── controllers/   the example controllers of a new project (core/); a new request never needs one
└── config/        routing/web.php: the routes; config.php: the site's settings;
                   schedule.php (scheduled jobs) and container.php (constructor bindings) when you add them
tests/             your tests (php caligrafer.php test)
Dockerfile         the production image (php caligrafer.php deploy runs when it starts)
public/
├── js/capabilities.js       the generated JavaScript client
├── css/                     Caligrafy's look: tokens.css (design tokens), layout.css, look.css, camera.css
└── <app>/                   Vue apps and single page applications
```

**One rule keeps every experience the same: only capabilities touch models.** Pages get their data from capabilities (`Route::page` with `data`, or the JavaScript client), forms post to capabilities (`Route::form`), custom requests are capabilities too (`Route::action`), REST and AI agents call capabilities. `Route::page` also gives every view who is signed in (`$authorized`, `$user`).

Caligrafy is also a classic MVC framework (routes, controllers, models, views). Existing controllers keep working: they call capabilities with `$this->call()`, and the [Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers) page shows how to move one. New code does not need them: start with capabilities and the declarative routes, and use `Route::action` for what a page or a form cannot say.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Your-First-Capability -->

In this tutorial you add a **Bookshelf** to the project of the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart): an `authors` and a `books` table, four capabilities (list the books, get one, list the authors, add a book), a page with a form, a REST API, tools for AI agents, sign-in, a test and a migration. It is the Bookshelf of the [course](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course), with the same tables and the same code. About 30 minutes. Every command runs in the project folder, with the Docker server of the Quickstart running.

A **capability** is one feature of the application, written once as a PHP class: its inputs and their rules, who may use it, and the work. Pages, REST, the JavaScript client and AI agents all call the same capability.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Author name:string bio:text
/caligrafy-quill:new-resource Book title:string published_year:int summary:text author:fk
```

For each entity, the `new-resource` skill writes the table script (`application/models/Book/create_db.sql`, the parent table first, with the foreign key `author_id`), the model, the five capabilities `list_books`, `get_book`, `create_book`, `update_book` and `delete_book` in `application/services/Books/` (scopes `books:read` and `books:write`), their REST routes, the pages with `Route::page` and the forms with `Route::form`. It then offers to run the SQL (`/caligrafy-quill:db`), calls each capability and asks the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent to review the files. The skill keeps one folder per entity (`models/Book/`, `services/Books/`, `views/Books/`); the steps below keep the whole Bookshelf in `Bookshelf/` folders, as the course does: both work. For one feature at a time, `/caligrafy-quill:new-capability create_book books:write` does the same for one capability and checks that every channel answers and refuses the same way.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities` lists the new capabilities with the scopes you expect (`books:read`, `books:write`) and `read` only on the reads.
+ `author_id` has the rule `exists,authors.id`: a book with an unknown author is refused with a message, not a database error.
+ No capability that changes data is `public: true`, unless you asked for it.
+ `web.php` has no controller: the forms are `Route::form` lines.
+ The page opens, and an empty form shows a message under each required field.
## By hand

In Docker, every `php caligrafer.php` command runs as `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`. On your own PHP, run `php caligrafer.php ...` in the project folder.

### <a name="table"></a>1. The tables and their models

A **model** is a PHP class for one table, with one public property per column. Create the folder `application/models/Bookshelf` and three files in it.

**`application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql`**
```sql
/* Bookshelf: the first version of its tables, and sample books.
 * Run it with: docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql
 * Safe to run again: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips a table that exists, INSERT IGNORE a row whose id exists.
 * Never edit it once it ran on a database with data: change a table with a migration (step 9).
 */

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS authors (
    id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
    bio TEXT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (
    id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    published_year SMALLINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    summary TEXT NULL,
    author_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    KEY idx_books_author_id (author_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_books_author_id FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES authors (id)
        ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;

-- Sample data, with fixed ids so that book 3 is Kindred everywhere
INSERT IGNORE INTO authors (id, name, bio) VALUES
    (1, 'Ursula K. Le Guin', 'American author of science fiction and fantasy, known for the Earthsea books.'),
    (2, 'Octavia E. Butler', 'American science fiction author, the first to receive a MacArthur fellowship.'),
    (3, 'Italo Calvino', 'Italian writer of playful, inventive novels and short stories.');

INSERT IGNORE INTO books (id, title, published_year, summary, author_id) VALUES
    (1, 'A Wizard of Earthsea', 1968, 'A gifted boy learns magic and must face the shadow he set loose.', 1),
    (2, 'The Left Hand of Darkness', 1969, 'An envoy visits a planet whose people have no fixed sex.', 1),
    (3, 'Kindred', 1979, 'A young woman is pulled back in time to a plantation in Maryland.', 2),
    (4, 'Parable of the Sower', 1993, 'In a collapsing California, a teenager starts a new belief system.', 2),
    (5, 'Invisible Cities', 1972, 'Marco Polo describes imaginary cities to the emperor Kublai Khan.', 3);
```

**`application/models/Bookshelf/Author.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Model;

// One Author = one row of the authors table (Author::query() reads authors: the class name in lower case, plus s)
class Author extends Model {

    // one public property per column of the table
    public $id;
    public $name;
    public $bio;
    public $created_at;
    public $modified_at;
}
```

**`application/models/Bookshelf/Book.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Model;

// One Book = one row of the books table. Book::with('author') adds the row of authors whose id is author_id
class Book extends Model {

    // one public property per column of the table
    public $id;
    public $title;
    public $published_year;
    public $summary;
    public $author_id;
    public $created_at;
    public $modified_at;
}
```

Run the script:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql
```
```text
 application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql run on caligrafy
```
The primary key is always `id`. `Book::query()` reads the table `books` and `Author::query()` the table `authors`: the class name in lower case plus `s`. The foreign key `author_id` links a book to its author, and `Book::with('author')` reads that author with the book. Online, `php caligrafer.php deploy` runs every new or changed `create_db.sql` when the app starts. A later change to a table that holds data is a migration: see [step 9](#migration).

### <a name="capabilities"></a>2. Four capabilities

Caligrafer writes each class, ready to fill:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListBooks --scope books:read --read-only
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/GetBook --scope books:read --read-only
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ListAuthors --scope books:read --read-only
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/CreateBook --scope books:write
```
Each prints:
```text
 Created application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php: capability 'list_books' (scope books:read)
 Fill in $rules and handle(), then serve it: a page (Route::page data), a form (Route::form), REST (Route::capability or Route::capabilities), MCP (Route::mcp)
```
The capability's name is the snake_case of the class name. Replace the content of the four files.

**`application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;

// list_books: the catalog, sorted by title, 20 books per page, each with its author. Anyone may read it
#[Capability(
    name: 'list_books',
    description: 'Lists the books of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page, each with its author (id, name, bio). Give author_id to list only the books of one author, and page for the next pages. Returns data (the books), total, page, per_page and pages.',
    scope: 'books:read',
    readOnly: true,
    public: true
)]
class ListBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer', 'page' => 'integer');
    public $descriptions = array(
        'author_id' => 'Optional: only the books of this author',
        'page' => 'Optional: the page, 1 by default (20 books per page)'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        // two queries for the page (the count, then the books) and one for all their authors
        $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
        if (!empty($input['author_id'])) {
            $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']);   // the value is bound, never pasted into the SQL
        }
        return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
    }
}
```

**`application/services/Bookshelf/GetBook.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

// get_book: one book with its author, or "not found"
#[Capability(
    name: 'get_book',
    description: 'Returns one book of the catalog with its author (id, name, bio), by the id of the book.',
    scope: 'books:read',
    readOnly: true,
    public: true
)]
class GetBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('id' => 'required|integer');
    public $descriptions = array('id' => 'The id of the book');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $book = Book::with('author')->find($input['id']);
        if (!$book) {
            throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no book #{$input['id']}");
        }
        return $book;
    }
}
```

**`application/services/Bookshelf/ListAuthors.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;

// list_authors: every author, sorted by name. Anyone may read it
#[Capability(
    name: 'list_authors',
    description: 'Lists the authors of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by name: id, name and bio.',
    scope: 'books:read',
    readOnly: true,
    public: true
)]
class ListAuthors extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        return Author::query()->orderBy('name')->get();
    }
}
```

**`application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php`**
```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Service;

// create_book: adds a book, with the same rules whoever calls it
#[Capability(
    name: 'create_book',
    description: 'Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.',
    scope: 'books:write',
    public: true   // for now: step 7 closes it
)]
class CreateBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array(
        'title' => 'required|max_len,200',
        'published_year' => 'required|integer|min_numeric,1450|max_numeric,current_year',
        'summary' => 'max_len,2000',
        'author_id' => 'required|integer|exists,authors.id'
    );
    public $filters = array('title' => 'trim', 'summary' => 'trim');
    public $descriptions = array(
        'title' => 'The title of the book',
        'published_year' => 'The year it was first published, for example 1969 (not after this year)',
        'summary' => 'Optional: one or two sentences about the book',
        'author_id' => 'The id of its author (list_authors)'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $id = Book::insert($input);   // one INSERT, every value bound; returns the id of the new book
        return Book::with('author')->find($id);
    }
}
```

What each part does:
+ `description` is what an AI agent reads to choose the tool: say what it does and what it returns.
+ `$rules` lists every input the capability accepts, with its [validation rules](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/6.-Validation). Only these inputs reach `handle()`. `exists,authors.id` refuses an author that is not in `authors`; `max_numeric,current_year` refuses a year after this one. `$filters` clean the inputs first; `$descriptions` describe them to clients and agents.
+ `scope` is what a token needs. `readOnly: true` marks a capability that changes nothing (only those can feed a page). `public: true` lets anyone call it without signing in: right for the reads, and for `create_book` only until [step 7](#secure).
+ `handle()` reads and writes with the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) (`Book::with('author')`, `Book::find()`, `Book::insert()`), every value bound, and returns data. It never draws a page, redirects or prints. It refuses with a `ServiceError` (`notFound`, `invalid`, `forbidden`, `conflict`).
+ `paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1)` returns `data` (the rows), `total`, `page`, `per_page` and `pages`. Always pass the page: REST, MCP and the command line have no query string.

Try them before any route:
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php capabilities
```
```text
 create_book                  public         writes    Adds a book to the Bookshelf catalog and returns it with its id and its author. The author must already exist: use list_authors to find author_id.
 get_book                     public         read      Returns one book of the catalog with its author (id, name, bio), by the id of the book.
 list_authors                 public         read      Lists the authors of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by name: id, name and bio.
 list_books                   public         read      Lists the books of the Bookshelf catalog, sorted by title, 20 per page, each with its author (id, name, bio). Give author_id to list only the books of one author, and page for the next pages. Returns data (the books), total, page, per_page and pages.
```
(with the Tasks, Users and notification capabilities around them).
```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call create_book title=Dawn published_year=1987 author_id=2
```
```json

```


```json
        "code": "invalid",
        "message": "Some of the inputs are invalid",
```
