<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications -->

**Notifications** reach your users when none of your pages are open: a book due tomorrow, a reservation ready, an
order shipped. One call, `Caligrafy\Notify::user()`, sends the message on every channel the user turned on: **web push**
(a notification on their phone or computer, browser closed) and **email** (an address they confirmed). Since 2.15.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability Every morning at 8, tell the administrators how many books are due today or late, and add a "Turn on alerts" button to the loans page
```

Claude writes the capability that calls `Notify::user()`, the job in `application/config/schedule.php`, the button
with `public/js/notify.js`, and adds `Route::capabilities()` and `Route::notifications()` to `web.php`. It runs
`php caligrafer.php platform install` and `php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject mailto:<you>` on your computer
(Caligrafy Cloud makes its own keys).

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php notify status <your user id>` shows `push` `configured: true`.
+ After *Turn on alerts* in your browser, `php caligrafer.php notify test <your user id>` answers `"push": 1` and a
  notification appears.
+ `php caligrafer.php schedule run <job>` prints `ok`.
## <a name="example"></a>By hand: tell the administrators what is late, every morning

Every morning at 8 in New York, each administrator of **Bookshelf** hears how many loans are due today or late. Start
from [Scheduled jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Scheduled-Jobs#example) (the `loans` table) and
an administrator (`permissions` 1, [Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication)).
The commands run in the Docker server of the Quickstart; without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`.
The whole lesson, with a page and Caligrafy Cloud, is
[course lesson 15](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/15-Reminders).

**1. Turn notifications on, once.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify keys --subject mailto:you@example.com
```

`notify keys` prints ` Web push keys written to .env (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VAPID_SUBJECT=mailto:you@example.com).
Keep them: new keys cut off every subscribed browser`. Run again, it keeps them.

**2. The routes.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, below `Route::auth(...)`:

```php
    Route::capabilities();      // what notify.js calls (/capabilities)
    Route::notifications();     // the pages the emails link to: /notify/confirm/{token}, /notify/unsubscribe
```

**3. The capability.** Write `application/services/Loans/RemindLoans.php` (the course's, lesson 15):

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Database;
use Caligrafy\Notify;
use Caligrafy\Service;

// remind_loans: tells the administrators which books are due today or late; a scheduled job runs it every morning
#[Capability(
    name: 'remind_loans',
    description: 'Notifies every administrator of the loans due today or late, by push and email. Returns how many loans are due today, how many are late, and how many administrators got the message.',
    scope: 'loans:write',
    level: 1
)]
class RemindLoans extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $today = date('Y-m-d');
        $due = Loan::whereNull('returned_at')->where('due_on', $today)->count();         // SELECT COUNT(*)
        $late = Loan::whereNull('returned_at')->where('due_on', '<', $today)->count();
        if ($due + $late === 0) {
            return array('due' => 0, 'late' => 0, 'notified' => 0);
        }
        $books = $due + $late;
        $message = array(
            'title' => $books === 1 ? '1 book to bring back' : "$books books to bring back",
            'body' => "$due due today, $late late. Open the loans to see who has them.",
            'url' => '/loans',
            'tag' => 'loans-due'
        );
        $notified = 0;
        foreach (Database::table('users')->where('permissions', '>=', 1)->pluck('id') as $admin) {
            $sent = Notify::user($admin, $message);
            if ($sent['push'] > 0 || $sent['email']) {
                $notified++;
            }
        }
        return array('due' => $due, 'late' => $late, 'notified' => $notified);
    }
}
```

A job has nobody signed in, so the capability finds the people it notifies itself.

**4. The schedule.** Add the job to `application/config/schedule.php`:

```php
<?php
return array(
    array('name' => 'clear-returned-loans', 'capability' => 'clear_returned_loans', 'input' => array('days' => 365),
        'cron' => '0 3 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
    array('name' => 'remind-loans', 'capability' => 'remind_loans', 'cron' => '0 8 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
);
```

**5. <a name="page"></a>The button.** Push needs the user's permission, asked from a click. Add to the loans page of
the course, `application/views/Loans/index.pug`, at the end of `block content`:

```pug
    button.btn.btn-primary#alerts(type='button') Turn on alerts
    script(src=$home . 'public/js/notify.js')
    script.
      document.getElementById('alerts').addEventListener('click', async () => {
        const status = await Notify.enable()
        if (status === 'install-needed') alert('On iPhone and iPad, add the app to your Home Screen first')
      })
```

**6. Try it.** Sign in as the administrator, open `http://localhost:8080/loans`, press *Turn on alerts* and allow notifications. Then:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify test 1          # 1: the administrator's user id
```
```json
{
    "push": 1,
    "email": false,
    "skipped": null
}
```

A *Notifications work* message appears. With a loan due today or late:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php schedule run remind-loans     # remind-loans: ok
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call remind_loans             # {"data": {"due": 0, "late": 1, "notified": 1}}
```

Before any browser turned push on, the same calls answer `"push": 0` and `"notified": 0`: nothing is sent, nothing
fails.

**Check**

+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php notify status 1` lists `"browsers": 1` under `push`.
+ The *1 book to bring back* notification opens `/loans` on a tap.
+ The table `caligrafy_notifications` has one line per message (never its body).
## <a name="send"></a>Reference: `Notify::user`

```php
$result = Caligrafy\Notify::user($userId, array(
    'title'   => 'Kindred is due tomorrow', // required, at most 80 characters
    'body'    => 'Bring it back by Friday.', // required, at most 300 characters
    'url'     => '/books/3',               // opened on a tap: a path of the app, or an https:// address
    'tag'     => 'loan-17',                // optional: a new message with the same tag replaces the old one
    'urgency' => 'high',                   // optional: low, normal (default) or high
));
// array('push' => 1, 'email' => true, 'skipped' => null)
```

+ `$userId` is the id `$context->userId()` gives (in a job, the id of each user it works for).
+ `push` is how many browsers got it; `email` whether an email was sent.
+ A delivery failure never throws. A bad message throws `ServiceError::invalid` with the fields.
+ At most `NOTIFY_RATE_PER_HOUR` messages per user and hour (30): above it nothing is sent (`'skipped' => 'rate'`).
+ Every call is logged in `caligrafy_notifications` (who, the title, the tag, what each channel did; never the body),
  kept 30 days.
+ Without the tables (`platform install`) nothing is sent and nothing fails.
+ When you delete a user, call `Caligrafy\Notify::forget($userId)`: their browsers, address, choices and log go.

### <a name="setup"></a>Settings

| `.env` | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `NOTIFY_CHANNELS` | `push,email` | The channels the app offers |
| `NOTIFY_RATE_PER_HOUR` | `30` | Messages per user and hour |
| `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`, `VAPID_SUBJECT` | empty | Written by `notify keys`; never replaced (new keys cut off every subscribed browser) |
| `APP_URL` | empty | The app's address, for the links of emails sent by jobs and the command line (Caligrafy Cloud sets it) |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_USERNAME`, `MAIL_PASSWORD`, `MAIL_FROM` | | The emails' server and sender; without them email reports `not-configured` and push still works |

On **Caligrafy Cloud** each app gets its web push keys at its first deploy, kept across deploys.

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `php caligrafer.php notify keys [--subject mailto:you@example.com]` | writes the web push keys to `.env`, once |
| `php caligrafer.php notify test <user id>` | sends that user a test message on every channel they turned on |
| `php caligrafer.php notify status <user id>` | the channels, the browsers, the email address and whether it is confirmed |

### `notify.js`

| | |
|---|---|
| `Notify.status()` | `unsupported`, `install-needed` (iPhone and iPad outside the Home Screen app), `denied`, `off` or `on` |
| `Notify.enable()` | asks permission, subscribes this browser, saves it; returns the new status. Call it from a click |
| `Notify.disable()` | unsubscribes this browser |
| `Notify.test()` | sends a test message to the signed-in user |
| `Notify.email(address)` | sets the address and emails a link to confirm it (24 hours) |
| `Notify.channel('email', false)` | turns a channel off (or on) |
| `Notify.info()` | what `notify_status` answers |

It registers `public/sw.js`, which shows the message with the browser closed and, on a tap, focuses a tab of its
address or opens one. Keep an in-page banner for when a page is open: notifications are for when it is not.

### <a name="email"></a>Email

+ **Only to a confirmed address.** `Notify.email()` (the `notify_email_set` capability) sends a link valid 24 hours,
  used once. Nothing else is sent there before.
+ **Unsubscribe in one click:** every email has a signed link and the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`
  headers that mail apps show as a button (`Route::notifications()` answers them).
+ **In your app's look:** the emails take the colors, font and corners of your
  [design style](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles) (`DESIGN_STYLE`), else Caligrafy's.

### <a name="capabilities"></a>Built-in capabilities

They ship with the framework, so pages, REST and the JS client use them with no code of yours. Each acts only on the
signed-in user's own data; none is an MCP tool (only a browser can subscribe or open a link).

| Capability | Input |
|---|---|
| `notify_status` | none: the channels and their state |
| `notify_subscribe` | the browser's `PushSubscription` JSON |
| `notify_unsubscribe` | `endpoint` |
| `notify_email_set` | `email` (sends the confirmation) |
| `notify_email_confirm` | `token` (public: the email's link) |
| `notify_preferences` | `channel`, `enabled` |
| `notify_test` | none |

### <a name="devices"></a>Where push works

Chrome, Edge and Firefox on computers and Android; Safari on Mac; Safari on iPhone and iPad once the app is added to
the Home Screen ([install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)). A
device that is off gets the message when it comes back, within 24 hours. Push needs HTTPS (or `localhost`).
## Common mistakes

+ **`Notify.enable()` does nothing.** It was called on page load: browsers ask permission only from a click.
+ **`"push": 0` for everyone.** No browser turned push on yet, or the VAPID keys changed (`notify keys` was run on a new
  `.env`): every browser must turn it on again.
+ **Emails from a job have no links.** `APP_URL` is empty: set it to the app's address.
+ **`"email": false`.** The user has no confirmed address, or `MAIL_*` is not set.
+ **Nothing on iPhone.** The app must be added to the Home Screen, and served over HTTPS.

+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs)
+ [Views: install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs -->

A **background job** runs one of your capabilities later, outside the request: the page answers at once, and the slow
part (an email, an AI call, a report, resizing images) happens a moment after, with retries when it fails. A job is a
capability's name and its input, pushed with `Caligrafy\Queue::push()` and run by a worker. Since 2.18.0.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability When a book is lent, notify the person who lent it of its due date, in the background
```

Claude writes two capabilities, the one the page calls (it checks who asks, saves, then pushes the job) and the one that
does the work, and adds the worker job on `queue_work` to `application/config/schedule.php`.

**Check**

+ The capability that pushes checks who may ask, and pushes ids, not data to trust later.
+ The work capability refuses callers other than the queue (it runs with full access).
+ `php caligrafer.php queue work --once` prints `done` for the job.
## By hand: a receipt for each loan

When the front desk of **Bookshelf** lends a book, the call answers at once, and a job tells the person who lent it who
has the book and until when. Start from the loans of the course
([lesson 13](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/13-Capstone-Loans): the `loans` table, the `Loan`
model, `lend_book`) and from [Notifications](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Notifications#example)
(`platform install`, `notify keys`). The commands run in the Docker server of the Quickstart; without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`.

**1. <a name="push"></a>Push the job from the capability that takes the request.** Replace
`application/services/Loans/LendBook.php` with (the course's, plus `use Caligrafy\Queue;` and the `Queue::push` line):

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Queue;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

// lend_book: records that someone borrowed a book, for a number of days
#[Capability(
    name: 'lend_book',
    description: 'Lends a book of the catalog to someone for a number of days (14 by default) and returns the loan. Refused when the book is already lent.',
    scope: 'loans:write'
)]
class LendBook extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('book_id' => 'required|integer', 'borrower' => 'required|max_len,100', 'days' => 'integer|min_numeric,1|max_numeric,60');
    public $filters = array('borrower' => 'trim');
    public $descriptions = array(
        'book_id' => 'The id of the book (list_books, search_books)',
        'borrower' => 'The name of the person who borrows it',
        'days' => 'For how many days: 1 to 60, 14 by default'
    );

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if (!Book::find($input['book_id'])) {
            throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no book #{$input['book_id']}");
        }
        $open = Loan::where('book_id', $input['book_id'])->whereNull('returned_at')->first();
        if ($open) {
            throw ServiceError::conflict("This book is already lent to {$open->borrower}");
        }
        $days = (int) ($input['days'] ?? 14);
        $id = Loan::insert(array(
            'book_id' => $input['book_id'],
            'borrower' => $input['borrower'],
            'due_on' => date('Y-m-d', strtotime("+$days days"))
        ));
        if ($context->userId() !== null) {
            // later, outside the request: tell the person who lent it
            Queue::push('send_loan_receipt', array('loan_id' => (int) $id, 'user_id' => (int) $context->userId()));
        }
        return Loan::find($id);
    }
}
```

The job gets ids, not names or dates to trust later, and only when someone is behind the call.

**2. The capability that does the work.** Write `application/services/Loans/SendLoanReceipt.php`:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Notify;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

// send_loan_receipt: run by the queue after lend_book, tells the person who lent the book when it comes back
#[Capability(
    name: 'send_loan_receipt',
    description: 'Tells the person who lent a book who has it and when it is due. Run by the queue after lend_book.',
    mcp: false
)]
class SendLoanReceipt extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('loan_id' => 'required|integer', 'user_id' => 'required|integer');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if (!in_array($context->actorType(), array('queue', 'cli'), true)) {
            throw ServiceError::forbidden('The queue sends the loan receipts');
        }
        $loan = Loan::find($input['loan_id']);
        if (!$loan) {
            throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no loan #{$input['loan_id']}");
        }
        $book = Book::find($loan->book_id);
        $sent = Notify::user($input['user_id'], array(
            'title' => $book->title . ' is lent',
            'body' => $loan->borrower . ' has it until ' . $loan->due_on . '.',
            'url' => '/loans',
            'tag' => 'loan-' . $loan->id,
        ));
        return array('loan_id' => (int) $loan->id, 'push' => $sent['push'], 'email' => $sent['email']);
    }
}
```

The job runs with full access: the `actorType()` check keeps people from calling it through the REST API.

**3. The worker.** Add the queue to `application/config/schedule.php`:

```php
<?php
return array(
    array('name' => 'clear-returned-loans', 'capability' => 'clear_returned_loans', 'input' => array('days' => 365),
        'cron' => '0 3 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
    array('name' => 'remind-loans', 'capability' => 'remind_loans', 'cron' => '0 8 * * *', 'timezone' => 'America/New_York'),
    array('name' => 'queue', 'capability' => 'queue_work', 'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 55),
);
```

Every minute it runs the jobs that are due for up to 50 seconds: the `scheduler` container of the Docker server and
Caligrafy Cloud run it.

**4. Try it.** Lend a book as the front desk, with a token that acts for the administrator (user 1), through the REST
API (`Route::capabilities()` in `web.php`):

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php token create "Front desk" --scopes loans:write --user 1
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer cq_<id>_<secret>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"book_id": 1, "borrower": "Sam"}' http://localhost:8080/capabilities/lend_book
```

It answers at once: `201 {"data":{"id":1,"book_id":1,"borrower":"Sam","due_on":"<in 14 days>",...}}`. The same call again
answers `409 {"error":{"code":"conflict","message":"This book is already lent to Sam"}}`. The job waits:

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php queue list
```
```text
 #1      default  send_loan_receipt        pending  0/3  from 2026-11-07 23:40:15
```

Run it now (the scheduler's `queue` job does the same within a minute):

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php queue work --once
```
```text
 Working the queue default until it is empty
 #1 send_loan_receipt: done
 1 done, 0 to try again, 0 failed
```

The notification *A Wizard of Earthsea is lent* reaches the administrator's browsers if they turned alerts on.

**Check**

+ `queue status` reads `0 pending, 0 running, 1 done, 0 failed`.
+ `audit` has `queue send_loan_receipt #1 send_loan_receipt ok`.
+ The `lend_book` call answered before the job ran.
## Reference: `Queue::push`

```php
use Caligrafy\Queue;

Queue::push('send_loan_receipt', ['loan_id' => $id, 'user_id' => $userId]);
Queue::push('build_report', ['month' => '2026-11'], ['delay' => 600, 'attempts' => 5, 'timeout' => 120]);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `delay` | `0` | seconds before the job may start |
| `attempts` | `3` | how many times it is tried (1 to 20) |
| `timeout` | `60` | seconds a run may take before it is stopped (900 at most) |
| `queue` | `default` | the queue's name (lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`), for a worker of its own |

+ It returns the job's id. The capability must exist when you push (`InvalidArgumentException` otherwise), and the
  input must encode to JSON.
+ Jobs are kept in `caligrafy_jobs` (made by `php caligrafer.php platform install` and the deploy step).
+ **Who it runs as.** A job runs with full access, like a scheduled job (`Context::system`: the audit log records
  `queue` and `<capability> #<id>`). Check who may ask for the work before you push it, and pass ids rather than data
  to trust later.

### Workers

| Way | When |
|---|---|
| a job on `queue_work` in `schedule.php` (`'every' => '1m', 'timeout' => 55`) | Caligrafy Cloud, and `server start` on your computer; a job starts within a minute and has what is left of it |
| `php caligrafer.php queue work` | your own server, longer jobs: a loop that runs jobs as they come (Ctrl+C stops it) |

```bash
php caligrafer.php queue work                 # runs jobs as they come
php caligrafer.php queue work --once          # runs what is due, then stops
php caligrafer.php queue work --for 300       # for 5 minutes
php caligrafer.php queue work --queue reports --sleep 3   # another queue; seconds between looks when empty
```

Each job runs in its own process, stopped at its timeout. Run one way or the other, not both. `queue_work` takes
`queue` and `seconds` (1 to 290, default 50) inputs, and refuses every caller but the scheduler and the command line.

### <a name="failures"></a>Failures and retries

+ A run that throws or times out is tried again after 30 seconds, then 1 minute, 2 minutes... until its attempts are
  used; then the job is `failed`.
+ A refusal of the capability (`invalid`, `not_found`, `forbidden`, `unauthenticated`) fails at once: it would fail
  again. `queue work` prints `#2 send_loan_receipt: failed (There is no loan #999)`.
+ A worker that stopped in the middle of a job (a restart) leaves it `running`; the next worker puts it back once its
  timeout and one more minute have passed.
+ Finished jobs are kept 7 days.

```bash
php caligrafer.php queue status              # pending, running, done, failed
php caligrafer.php queue list                # the latest jobs, with their last error (--status failed, --limit 50)
php caligrafer.php queue failed              # only the failed ones
php caligrafer.php queue retry 42            # or: queue retry all
```

### <a name="test"></a>Testing

In a test, `$this->assertQueued('send_loan_receipt')` checks that a job was pushed and returns its input
([Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App)). Run the job itself with
`$this->call('send_loan_receipt', $input)`.
## Common mistakes

+ **Jobs stay `pending`.** No worker: add the `queue` job to `schedule.php`, or run `queue work`.
+ **Two workers for one queue.** A `queue_work` job and a `queue work` container side by side: keep one.
+ **A job reads the signed-in user.** Nobody is signed in when it runs: pass the ids it needs in its input.
+ **Anyone can trigger the work.** The work capability is also a REST capability: refuse callers whose
  `$context->actorType()` is not `queue` (or `cli`).
+ **A long job is stopped at 50 seconds** with the scheduler's worker: give it a worker of its own (`queue work`,
  timeouts up to 900 seconds).

+ [Snap Cards: a capability declared `async: true` runs in the queue as a Track card: Task](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant#tasks)
+ [Authentication: tokens](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#agents)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations -->

A **migration** is one change to a table that already holds data, written as a numbered SQL file that runs once. Every
computer and every server runs the same files in the same order, so they all end up with the same tables. Since 2.18.0.

**Which file to write:**

| You want to... | Write | Run it with |
|---|---|---|
| create a new table (its first version) | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in `application/models/<Folder>/create_db.sql` ([Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models)) | `php caligrafer.php sql application/models/<Folder>/create_db.sql` |
| change a table that holds data: add a column or an index, rename, fix rows | a migration in `application/migrations/` (this page) | `php caligrafer.php migrate` |

A `create_db.sql` that already ran is never edited: once a table has rows, every change to it goes in a new migration.
## With Claude

Ask for the change with the `db` skill of the Claude Code plugin:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:db add an isbn column (20 characters, optional, unique) to the books table
```

Claude writes `application/migrations/<number>_<name>.sql` with `php caligrafer.php migrate make <name>`, puts the SQL
in it, runs `php caligrafer.php migrate` (in the Docker container when the project uses the Docker server) and checks
`php caligrafer.php migrate status`. It never edits a migration that already ran.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the new file is in `application/migrations/` and holds one change;
+ `php caligrafer.php migrate status` shows every file as `ran`;
+ the model of the table has a property for each new column (`public $isbn;`).
## <a name="write"></a>By hand

The Bookshelf `books` table exists and holds rows ([Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models)).
Add an `isbn` column to it. With the Docker server of the
[Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart), run every command in the container:
`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...` (without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **Create the file.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate make add_books_isbn
    ```
    It prints the file it wrote (the number is the date and time):
    ```text
     application/migrations/20261107120200_add_books_isbn.sql written: add its SQL, then php caligrafer.php migrate
    ```
2. **Write the change.** Open that file and make it read:
    ```sql
    -- add_books_isbn
    -- Runs once (php caligrafer.php migrate, and at every deploy). Never edit it after it ran: write a new one.
    -- One statement: the column and its unique index are added together, or not at all.

    ALTER TABLE books
        ADD COLUMN isbn VARCHAR(20) NULL AFTER summary,
        ADD UNIQUE KEY uq_books_isbn (isbn);
    ```
    Two books never share an ISBN, and a book without one has `NULL`, which the unique index allows on many rows.
3. **See what will run.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate status
    ```
    ```text
     pending  20261107120200_add_books_isbn.sql
    ```
4. **Run it.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate
    ```
    ```text
     OK   20261107120200_add_books_isbn.sql

     1 migration(s) run on caligrafy
    ```
    Run it again and it says ` Nothing to migrate: caligrafy is up to date`.
5. **Give the model the new column.** In `application/models/Bookshelf/Book.php`, add `public $isbn;` after
   `public $summary;` (the whole model is on the [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models) page).
6. **Commit the file.** It runs online on its own: the deploy step (`php caligrafer.php deploy`, which the production
   image runs at every start, and so Caligrafy Cloud) runs the pending migrations after the `create_db.sql` scripts.

**Check:**
+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate status` shows ` ran      20261107120200_add_books_isbn.sql  (<date and time>)`;
+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor --only database` shows `OK    Migrations: 1 ran, none pending`;
+ the column is there: `docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot caligrafy -e "DESCRIBE books"` lists
  `isbn  varchar(20)  YES  UNI  NULL`.
## <a name="run"></a>Reference

**Commands**

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `php caligrafer.php migrate make <name>` | writes `application/migrations/<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_<name>.sql` with a comment header (the name becomes lower case, letters, digits and `_`). Needs no database |
| `php caligrafer.php migrate` | runs, in number order, every file that never ran on this database, and records each one |
| `php caligrafer.php migrate status` | each file with its state: `pending`, `ran` (with when) or `changed` |
| `php caligrafer.php migrate --env .env.testing` | the same on the database of another `.env` file, here the test database; `--env` goes with `migrate` and `migrate status` (2.19.1; before, write `migrate "" --env .env.testing`) |
| `php caligrafer.php doctor` | `WARN Migrations: 1 pending: ...` or `... changed after it ran: it will not run again`; `OK Migrations: N ran, none pending` |
| `php caligrafer.php deploy` | (production start) runs the `create_db.sql` scripts, then the pending migrations: `OK Migrations: 1 run: <name>` or `up to date`. A failing migration stops it with exit 1 |

**Files**

+ Named `<number>_<name>.sql`: the number is 1 to 14 digits, the name letters, digits and `_`. Another `.sql` name in
  the folder stops every command: `notes.sql: a migration is named <number>_<name>.sql, e.g. 20261107120000_add_books_isbn.sql`.
+ Two files with the same number (as a number: `5_a.sql` and `005_b.sql`) are refused.
+ The statements are split on `;` outside quotes (`'...'`, `"..."`, `` `...` ``) and comments (`-- `, `#`, `/* */`),
  so text such as `'a;b'` is safe. `DELIMITER` is not supported: write triggers and procedures in a script you run
  with `php caligrafer.php sql <file>`.
+ An empty file runs and is recorded: write its SQL before you run `migrate`.

**The table `caligrafy_migrations`** (made by `php caligrafer.php platform install`, or by the first `migrate`): `name`
(the file name), `sha256` (of its content when it ran) and `ran_at`. A file whose content no longer matches its
`sha256` is `changed`: it is never run again.
## <a name="rules"></a>Three rules

1. **Never edit a migration that ran.** It will not run again: `status` shows `changed`, and `migrate` prints
   ` WARN <name>: changed after it ran, not run again (write a new migration for the change)`. Put the file back as it
   was and write a new one.
2. **Forward only.** There is no "down": to undo a change, write a migration that undoes it.
3. **One change per file, or files that can run twice.** MySQL saves a `CREATE` or an `ALTER` at once. When the second
   statement of a file fails, the first one stays applied and the file is not recorded:
   ```text
    migrate: 20261107120300_add_more.sql, statement 2: SQLSTATE[42S21]: Column already exists: 1060 Duplicate column name 'isbn'
   ```
   Keep one change per file, or write it so that it can run again (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`).
## <a name="createdb"></a>Migrations and create_db.sql

`create_db.sql` gives a new database its tables: `php caligrafer.php sql <file>` runs it by hand, and the deploy step
runs it when it is new or changed (a changed script that drops or deletes data is not run again: it says so in a `WARN`
line). A migration runs exactly once on each database, in order, after the scripts. So:

+ a new table: `create_db.sql` (its first version, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`);
+ any change to a table that holds data: a migration;
+ sample rows for your computer: a `seed.sql` you run with `php caligrafer.php sql` (the deploy step never runs it).
## Common mistakes

+ **Editing the file after it ran** (G120): nothing happens on any database. Restore it and write a new migration.
+ **Changing `create_db.sql` instead of writing a migration**: a database that already has the table keeps the old
  one (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it).
+ **A table change inside a transaction or a test**: MySQL ends the transaction at the first `CREATE` or `ALTER`.
  Keep table changes in migrations.
+ **Forgetting the model**: the new column is still read and written (the rows carry it), but the model no longer
  says what the table holds. Add its property in the same change.
## Related pages

+ [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models): the first version of a table, and its model
+ [Caligrafer: migrate](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#migrate)
+ [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App): migrations on a test database
+ [Putting it online](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Putting-it-Online): the deploy step


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caching -->

The **cache** keeps a value for a while, so that slow work (a call to another service, a heavy count, a report) is done
once and read many times. A capability reads through the cache, and the capabilities that change the data forget the
value, so nobody reads an old copy for long. Since 2.18.0.
## With Claude

Say what is slow, how old the answer may be, and what changes it:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability shelf_stats books:read read-only public: the numbers of books, authors and open loans, at most 10 minutes old; forget them when a book is added
```

Claude reads the value with `Caligrafy\Cache::remember('<key>', <seconds>, fn () => ...)` in the capability, and calls
`Cache::forget('<key>')` in the capabilities that change the data.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ the key says what the value is (`bookshelf:stats`), and holds the user's id when the value is someone's;
+ every capability that changes the data forgets the key;
+ the value is plain data (numbers, strings, arrays), not a model object.
## <a name="use"></a>By hand

Run the commands in the Docker container (`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`; without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **The framework tables.** The cache is kept in the `caligrafy_cache` table by default.
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install` creates it (the deploy step does too).
2. **Read through the cache.** Run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Bookshelf/ShelfStats --scope books:read --read-only`, then
   make `application/services/Bookshelf/ShelfStats.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Cache;
    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Database;
    use Caligrafy\Service;

    #[Capability(
        name: 'shelf_stats',
        description: 'Returns the numbers of the Bookshelf: books, authors, and books out on loan now. Up to 10 minutes old.',
        scope: 'books:read',
        readOnly: true,
        public: true
    )]
    class ShelfStats extends Service
    {
        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            return Cache::remember('bookshelf:stats', 600, function () {
                return array(
                    'books' => Database::table('books')->count(),
                    'authors' => Database::table('authors')->count(),
                    'out' => Database::table('loans')->whereNull('returned_at')->count()
                );
            });
        }
    }
    ```
    `remember()` returns the kept value when there is one, otherwise runs the function, keeps its result for 600
    seconds and returns it.
3. **Forget it where the data changes.** In `application/services/Bookshelf/CreateBook.php` (from
   [Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service)),
   add `use Caligrafy\Cache;` under `<?php` and make `handle()` read:
    ```php
        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            $id = Book::insert($input);
            Cache::forget('bookshelf:stats');   // the number of books changed
            return Book::with('author')->find($id);
        }
    ```
    Do the same in `delete_book` and `lend_book`.
4. **Run it.** With the sample rows of [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models):
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call shelf_stats
    ```
    ```json
    {
        "data": {
            "books": 5,
            "authors": 3,
            "out": 2
        }
    }
    ```
    The value is now in the table: `docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot caligrafy -e "SELECT cache_key, value FROM caligrafy_cache"`
    shows `bookshelf:stats  {"books":5,"authors":3,"out":2}`. Add a book with `call create_book`: the row is gone,
    and the next `call shelf_stats` says `"books": 6`.

**Check:**
+ two `call shelf_stats` in a row give the same answer, and the second one runs no count;
+ after `create_book`, `shelf_stats` has the new number;
+ `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cache clear` prints
  ` Cache (database) emptied; <n> compiled view and class map file(s) removed`.
## Reference

```php
use Caligrafy\Cache;

Cache::remember('bookshelf:stats', 600, fn () => $this->count());   // the kept value, or the function's, kept 600 s
Cache::put('report:2026-11', $rows, 3600);    // for an hour (null: until forgotten; 0 or less: forgets it)
Cache::get('report:2026-11', []);             // the value, or [] when it is not there or too old
Cache::has('report:2026-11');                 // true or false
Cache::forever('settings', $settings);        // until it is forgotten
Cache::forget('report:2026-11');              // gone
Cache::flush();                               // the whole store
```

+ Values are stored as JSON: strings, numbers, booleans, `null` and arrays. An object (a model) comes back as an array,
  and `remember()` returns what a later read returns. A value that cannot be encoded is refused.
+ A key is any text but empty. Put whose it is in the key when it is someone's: `"loans:user:$id"`.
+ In one request, a value read once is read from memory after that.

### <a name="stores"></a>Where values are kept: `CACHE_STORE`

| `CACHE_STORE` in `.env` | Used when empty | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `database` | with `DB_ACTIVATE=true` | the `caligrafy_cache` table: one store for the web server, the queue, the scheduled jobs and every server of the app |
| `file` | without a database | a private folder of the temporary directory: one server, one system user |
| `off` | | nothing is kept; `remember()` always runs its function |

Another value stops with `CACHE_STORE=<value>: use file, database or off`. Until the `caligrafy_cache` table exists,
the database store uses the file store and writes `Caligrafy cache: the caligrafy_cache table is missing (php
caligrafer.php platform install): using the file store` in the PHP error log. One write in a hundred removes the
expired rows.

**Why the database by default:** the web server and the command line (the queue, scheduled jobs) run as different
system users, and each one has its own file store. A job that forgets a value in the file store would leave the web
server's copy in place. The database is one store for all of them.

`php caligrafer.php cache clear` empties the store, and the compiled views and the class map of the system user that
runs it. The web server keeps its own: run it as that user, or restart the container.
## Common mistakes

+ **Not forgetting** a value where the data changes: people read the old copy until it expires.
+ **`CACHE_STORE=file` with a queue or scheduled jobs** (G119): the job's `forget()` does not reach the page's copy.
  Keep the database store.
+ **Caching someone's data under a shared key**: one person sees another's. Put the user's id in the key.
+ **Expecting a model back**: it comes back as an array (`$stats['books']`).
## Related pages

+ [Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP): capabilities
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs): slow work done later
+ [Caligrafer: cache](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#cache)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App -->

Your app's **tests** check what it does through its capabilities, the way its pages, REST API, Vue apps and AI agents
reach them: with the permission checks, the validation and the audit. Each test runs in a database transaction that
is rolled back at its end, so tests leave the database as they found it. Since 2.18.0.
## With Claude

The `new-capability` skill writes a test with each capability. To test what exists, ask:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability write the tests of create_book, get_book and lend_book: the rule cases as a user, the refusals as a guest
```

Claude runs `php caligrafer.php test make <Name>`, fills `tests/<Name>Test.php` (extends `Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase`)
with `$this->call(...)` and `$this->assertCapabilityFails(...)`, and runs `php caligrafer.php test <Name>`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ every refusal kind the capability can give has its assertion (`invalid`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`);
+ the tests create their own rows: they do not count on the rows of your development database;
+ `php caligrafer.php test` ends with `OK (...)`.
## <a name="first"></a>By hand

The tests of the Bookshelf capabilities (`create_book`, `list_books`, `get_book`, `delete_book` of
[Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service)
and `lend_book` of [Dependency injection](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection), on
the `loans` table of [Models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/4.-Models)). `create_book` is closed
there (signed in or a token) and `delete_book` has `level: 1`.
PHPUnit comes with the development packages of every project (`composer install`). Run the commands in the Docker
container (`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`; without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **A database for the tests.** Copy the settings: `cp .env .env.testing`. In `.env.testing`, change one line:
    ```text
    DB_DATABASE=caligrafy_test
    ```
    `.env.testing` holds the same secrets as `.env`: the project's `.gitignore` already leaves it out of git (every
    `.env.*` file but `.env.example`, 2.19.1). Then create the database and its tables:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS caligrafy_test"
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install --env .env.testing
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql --env .env.testing
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php migrate --env .env.testing
    ```
    `--env .env.testing` runs the command on the test database (` application/models/Bookshelf/create_db.sql run on
    caligrafy_test`, ` 1 migration(s) run on caligrafy_test`). The tests
    read `.env`, then `.env.testing`, whose settings win.
2. **Create the test file.** Run:
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test make Bookshelf
    ```
    ```text
     tests/BookshelfTest.php written: php caligrafer.php test Bookshelf
    ```
3. **Write the tests.** Make `tests/BookshelfTest.php` read:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Database;
    use Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase;

    /**
     * php caligrafer.php test Bookshelf
     */
    final class BookshelfTest extends TestCase
    {
        private function author(): int
        {
            // a row for this test only: the transaction of the test is rolled back at its end
            return (int) Database::table('authors')->insert(array('name' => 'Ursula K. Le Guin'));
        }

        public function testAReaderAddsABookAndEveryoneSeesIt(): void
        {
            $authorId = $this->author();
            $book = $this->call('create_book', array('title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => $authorId), $this->user(7));

            $this->assertSame('Tehanu', $book['title']);
            $this->assertSame('Ursula K. Le Guin', $book['author']['name']);
            $page = $this->call('list_books', array('author_id' => $authorId), 'guest');
            $this->assertSame(1, $page['total']);
            $this->assertSame('Tehanu', $page['data'][0]['title']);
        }

        public function testRefusals(): void
        {
            $error = $this->assertCapabilityFails('invalid', 'create_book', array('title' => 'Tehanu'), $this->user(7));
            $this->assertArrayHasKey('published_year', $error->fields);

            $this->assertCapabilityFails('unauthenticated', 'create_book', array('title' => 'Tehanu'), 'guest');
            $this->assertCapabilityFails('forbidden', 'delete_book', array('id' => 1), $this->user(7, 0));
            $this->assertCapabilityFails('not_found', 'get_book', array('id' => 999999), 'guest');
        }

        public function testALoanIsDueIn14Days(): void
        {
            $this->fake(Clock::class, new class implements Clock {
                public function today(): DateTimeImmutable
                {
                    return new DateTimeImmutable('2026-11-01');
                }
            });
            $book = $this->call('create_book', array('title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'author_id' => $this->author()));

            $loan = $this->call('lend_book', array('book_id' => $book['id'], 'borrower' => 'Ana'), $this->user(7));

            $this->assertSame('2026-11-15', $loan['due_on']);   // 14 days after the fixed today
            $this->assertCapabilityFails('conflict', 'lend_book', array('book_id' => $book['id'], 'borrower' => 'Ben'), $this->user(7));
        }

        public function testTheBookPage(): void
        {
            // the data Route::page gives application/views/Bookshelf/book.pug: get_book and list_authors
            $html = $this->render('Bookshelf/book', array(
                'book' => array('id' => 1, 'title' => 'Tehanu', 'published_year' => 1990, 'summary' => 'The fourth Earthsea book.',
                    'isbn' => null, 'author_id' => 1, 'author' => array('name' => 'Ursula K. Le Guin')),
                'authors' => array(array('id' => 1, 'name' => 'Ursula K. Le Guin'))
            ));

            $this->assertStringContainsString('Tehanu', $html);
            $this->assertStringContainsString('by Ursula K. Le Guin, 1990', $html);
        }
    }
    ```
    `$this->user(7)` is a signed-in user of id 7 and level 0: `delete_book` (level 1) refuses them.
    `$this->call(..., null)` (no third argument) is the command line, with full access.
4. **Run them.**
    ```bash
    docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test
    ```
    ```text
    PHPUnit 12.5.44 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.

    ....                                                                4 / 4 (100%)

    OK (4 tests, 13 assertions)
    ```
    (between them, the PHP version and the time it took). `php caligrafer.php test Loan` runs only the tests whose name matches `Loan` (`testALoanIsDueIn14Days`).

**Check:**
+ `OK (4 tests, 13 assertions)`;
+ the test database has no `Tehanu` afterwards:
  `docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot caligrafy_test -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books WHERE title = 'Tehanu'"`
  gives `0` (the five sample books of `create_db.sql` stay);
+ break a rule on purpose (remove `required` from `published_year` in `CreateBook`): `testRefusals` fails. Put it back.
## <a name="helpers"></a>Reference

| Helper | What it does |
|---|---|
| `$this->call($capability, $input, $as)` | calls the capability with its checks, validation and audit; returns its answer as plain data |
| `$this->user($id = 1, $level = 0, $attributes = [])` | a signed-in user for `$as`: an id, a permission level (`permissions`), other attributes the capability reads |
| `$this->action($capability, $input, $as)` | calls a capability declared `webOnly: true` as `Route::action` does (2.21.0); returns its answer: a `Caligrafy\Web`, whose `->describe()` gives `type`, `target`, `data`, `status` and `headers`, or plain data |
| `$this->assertCapabilityFails($kind, $capability, $input, $as)` | the capability refuses with `$kind` (`invalid`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`); returns the `ServiceError` (`->fields`, `->getMessage()`) |
| `$this->render($view, $data)` | the HTML of a Pug view of `application/views`, as a page shows it |
| `$this->fake($class, $object)` | the [container](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection) gives `$object` for `$class` in this test |
| `$this->assertQueued($capability, $where = null)` | a [background job](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs) of that capability was pushed in this test (whose input passes the function `$where`); returns its input |

**Who calls (`$as`)**

| `$as` | The test calls as |
|---|---|
| `null` (or nothing) | the command line: full access |
| `'guest'` | a visitor: only public capabilities |
| `$this->user(7)`, an object or an array | that user, over REST |
| a `Caligrafy\Context` | that context (a token: `Context::forToken($row, 'mcp')`) |

**Commands**

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `php caligrafer.php test make <Name>` | writes `tests/<Name>Test.php` (refuses an existing file) |
| `php caligrafer.php test` | runs every `tests/*Test.php` and `tests/*/*Test.php` with PHPUnit; exit 0 when they pass |
| `php caligrafer.php test <filter>` | only the tests whose class or method name matches |

Without PHPUnit it says ` PHPUnit is not installed: composer install (with the development packages), then php caligrafer.php test`.
A warning fails the run (`--fail-on-warning`).
## <a name="database"></a>The database

+ With `DB_ACTIVATE=true`, each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back at its end: the rows a test writes are
  gone after it, and tests never see each other's rows.
+ The settings are those of `.env`, then of `.env.testing` (whose settings win). `DB_TEST_DATABASE=caligrafy_test` in
  `.env` also works: it replaces `DB_DATABASE` for the tests only; the commands that prepare that database still need
  a settings file (`--env`).
+ A test that must not run in a transaction sets `protected $transactions = false;` (and cleans up after itself).
+ Between tests, the container's bindings, the cache's in-memory copies and the counts of the N+1 warning are reset.
## <a name="where"></a>Where tests live

`tests/` at the top of the project, one class per file named `*Test.php`, extending `Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase`.
The production image leaves `tests/` out, and the framework never loads it on a page.
## Common mistakes

+ **A `CREATE`, `ALTER` or `DROP` in a test** (G121): MySQL commits it and ends the test's transaction, so the rows
  of the test stay. Create tables in `create_db.sql` and migrations, before the tests.
+ **Tests on your development database**: they pass or fail with the rows you have. Give them `.env.testing`.
+ **`.env.testing` in git**: it holds your secrets. The project's `.gitignore` leaves out every `.env.*` but
  `.env.example` (2.19.1); a project made before 2.19.1 adds `/.env.*` and `!/.env.example` to its `.gitignore`.
+ **`migrate "" --env .env.testing`**: the empty `""` was needed before 2.19.1. Since 2.19.1, write
  `migrate --env .env.testing`.
+ **A test that reads `$_SESSION` or the request**: a plain capability never does; give the user with `$this->user()`.
+ **`$this->call()` on a web-only capability**: it answers `not_found`, as every other channel. Use `$this->action()`. It
  runs `handle()` without a request: a capability that calls `request()` or signs someone in is tested through its parts, and
  in the browser.
## Related pages

+ [Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#test): capabilities
+ [Dependency injection](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection#test): fakes
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs#test): `assertQueued()`
+ [Testing Caligrafy](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Caligrafy): the framework's own QA suite
+ [Caligrafer: test](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#test)


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Dependency-Injection -->

**Dependency injection** means a class asks for what it uses in its constructor instead of creating it, and
Caligrafy's **container** gives it. A capability then stays short, the real thing (a clock, a mailer, a payment
gateway) is chosen in one file, and a test can swap it for a fake. Since 2.18.0.
## With Claude

Say what the capability uses from outside, and that a test must be able to replace it:

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability lend_book loans:write: lend a book for a number of days (14 by default) from today; take the date from a Clock so a test can fix it
```

Claude gives the capability a constructor (`public function __construct(private Clock $clock) {}`), binds the
interface in `application/config/container.php`, and writes a test that replaces it with `$this->fake()`.

**Check** before you say OK:
+ `handle()` never writes `new SystemClock()` (or `new` of anything with settings): it uses what the constructor got;
+ every interface the constructor asks for is bound in `application/config/container.php`;
+ `php caligrafer.php call lend_book book_id=2 borrower=Dan` works, and `php caligrafer.php test` passes.
## <a name="ask"></a>By hand

A loan is due a number of days after today, 14 by default (`lend_book` of the course, with a clock). "Today" comes
from a `Clock`, so a test can choose the date. Run the commands in
the Docker container (`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php ...`; without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`).

1. **The interface.** Create `application/support/Clock.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    // What time it is: the capabilities ask for a Clock, so a test can give them a fixed one
    interface Clock
    {
        public function today(): DateTimeImmutable;
    }
    ```
2. **The real one.** Create `application/support/SystemClock.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    // The real clock: today, in the time zone of the application (SERVER_TIMEZONE)
    class SystemClock implements Clock
    {
        public function today(): DateTimeImmutable
        {
            return new DateTimeImmutable('today');
        }
    }
    ```
    Any folder of `application/` but `config/` and `views/` is found by the class map: no `require` to write.
3. **<a name="bind"></a>The binding.** Create `application/config/container.php`:
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Container;

    // What the container gives a class that asks for an interface (or for a class that needs settings)
    Container::bind(Clock::class, SystemClock::class);
    ```
4. **The capability asks for it.** `lend_book` is the capability of the course's loans
   ([lesson 13](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course/wiki/13-Capstone-Loans): the `loans` table and the
   `Loan` model). Without it, run
   `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php service Loans/LendBook --scope loans:write`. Then make
   `application/services/Loans/LendBook.php` read (the course's, with the date from the clock):
    ```php
    <?php

    use Caligrafy\Capability;
    use Caligrafy\Context;
    use Caligrafy\Service;
    use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

    // lend_book: records that someone borrowed a book, for a number of days counted from the Clock's today
    #[Capability(
        name: 'lend_book',
        description: 'Lends a book of the catalog to someone for a number of days (14 by default) and returns the loan. Refused when the book is already lent.',
        scope: 'loans:write'
    )]
    class LendBook extends Service
    {
        public $rules = array('book_id' => 'required|integer', 'borrower' => 'required|max_len,100', 'days' => 'integer|min_numeric,1|max_numeric,60');
        public $filters = array('borrower' => 'trim');
        public $descriptions = array(
            'book_id' => 'The id of the book (list_books)',
            'borrower' => 'The name of the person who borrows it',
            'days' => 'For how many days: 1 to 60, 14 by default'
        );

        // the container gives the Clock bound in application/config/container.php
        public function __construct(private Clock $clock)
        {
        }

        public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
        {
            if (!Book::find($input['book_id'])) {
                throw ServiceError::notFound("There is no book #{$input['book_id']}");
            }
            $open = Loan::where('book_id', $input['book_id'])->whereNull('returned_at')->first();
            if ($open) {
                throw ServiceError::conflict("This book is already lent to {$open->borrower}");
            }
            $days = (int) ($input['days'] ?? 14);
            $id = Loan::insert(array(
                'book_id' => $input['book_id'],
                'borrower' => $input['borrower'],
                'due_on' => $this->clock->today()->modify("+$days days")->format('Y-m-d')
            ));
            return Loan::find($id);
        }
    }
    ```
5. **Run it.** `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call lend_book book_id=2 borrower=Dan` returns the loan
   with `"due_on"` 14 days from today (`"2026-11-21"` on 7 November 2026). Run it again: the book is out,
   `{"error": {"code": "conflict", "message": "This book is already lent to Dan"}}`.
6. **In a test, a fixed clock.** See step 3 of [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App#first):
    ```php
    $this->fake(Clock::class, new class implements Clock {
        public function today(): DateTimeImmutable
        {
            return new DateTimeImmutable('2026-11-01');
        }
    });
    $loan = $this->call('lend_book', ['book_id' => $bookId, 'borrower' => 'Ana'], $this->user(7));
    $this->assertSame('2026-11-15', $loan['due_on']);   // 14 days after the fixed today
    ```

**Check:**
+ `call lend_book` works with the binding;
+ remove `application/config/container.php` for a moment: `call lend_book ...` then says
  `The container cannot build Clock: it is an interface. Bind it to a class in application/config/container.php`.
  Put it back.
## Reference

Every capability is built by the container, with what its constructor asks for. A class type in a constructor is
built the same way, with what its own constructor asks for; a parameter with a default keeps it.

| Method (in `application/config/container.php`) | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Container::bind($id, $factory)` | a new object each time; `$factory` is a class name or a function that returns the object |
| `Container::singleton($id, $factory)` | one object for the whole request, made the first time it is asked for |
| `Container::instance($id, $object)` | this object |

```php
Container::bind(Clock::class, SystemClock::class);                                               // an interface -> a class
Container::singleton(PaymentGateway::class, fn () => new StripeGateway(getenv('PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_TEST')));   // your own class, with settings
```

| Method (anywhere) | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Container::get($id)` | the object for `$id`: its instance, its binding, or the class built with what it asks for |
| `Container::make($class, ['name' => $value])` | a new `$class` (never a shared one), some constructor parameters given by name |
| `Container::has($id)` | whether `$id` has a binding or an instance |
| `Container::reset()` | forgets every binding and instance (the tests do it between tests) |

How a constructor parameter is given: by name from `make()`'s parameters, else by its class or interface type, else
its default, else `null` when it accepts `null`. The file `application/config/container.php` is read once: by the web
front controller after `config.php`, by the command line and the tests the first time the container is used.

**What it says when it cannot build a class:**

| Cause | Message |
|---|---|
| an interface with no binding | `The container cannot build Clock: it is an interface. Bind it to a class in application/config/container.php` |
| a parameter with no type and no default | `The container cannot build NeedsName: nothing gives its parameter $name. Give it a default, a class type, or bind it in application/config/container.php` |
| a class that needs itself | `The container cannot build A: it needs itself (A -> B -> A)` |
| an abstract class, or a constructor that is not public | `The container cannot build X: it is abstract or its constructor is not public` |

Over REST the call answers 500, over MCP a JSON-RPC `Internal error` (-32603); the audit log records `error  LogicException`.
## <a name="test"></a>In tests

`$this->fake(Clock::class, $object)` gives `$object` to every class that asks for `Clock`, for this test only: the
container is reset before and after each test, and the bindings of `application/config/container.php` are read
again first, so the fake replaces them. See [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App#helpers).
## Common mistakes

+ **`new` in `handle()`** for something with settings or side effects (a mailer, a payment client): a test cannot
  replace it. Ask for it in the constructor.
+ **An interface with no binding**: the capability fails at its first call. Bind it in `application/config/container.php`.
+ **A binding written in `web.php`**: the command line, the queue and the tests never read `web.php`. Write bindings in
  `application/config/container.php`.
## Related pages

+ [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App): `$this->fake()`
+ [Build once](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/11.-Build-Once:-Services,-Capabilities-and-MCP#service): capabilities
+ [Background jobs](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Background-Jobs): jobs are capabilities too, built the same way
