<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.2-Stripe-%26-Cryptocurrency-Payment -->

Caligrafy takes card payments with **Stripe** (stripe-php 23: Stripe Checkout, payment intents and the Payment
Element, Stripe Connect for marketplaces) and crypto payments with the **Coinbase Business Checkouts API**. The
recommended way is a Stripe Checkout started by a capability, and a webhook (`Route::webhook`, 2.19.0) that records the
payment when Stripe says it went through.
> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Accepting online payments](https://youtu.be/OqHfnKtM5VY)
>
> In this video you will learn how to accept online payments with Caligrafy using Stripe.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-capability Readers pay 5 USD for a membership with Stripe Checkout; record each paid session from Stripe's webhook
```

Claude writes a capability that starts the checkout, a `Route::form` that sends the reader to Stripe, a capability
that records the payment and `Route::webhook('/stripe/events', '<capability>', ['verify' => 'stripe'])` in
`application/config/routing/web.php`, with the table of the payments. It never writes your keys: you put them in `.env`.

**Check**

+ `.env` has your test keys (`PAY_PUBLIC_KEY_TEST`, `PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_TEST`) and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and they are
  not in git.
+ The capability that records payments refuses every caller but the webhook, and records a session once even when
  Stripe sends the event twice.
+ A payment with the test card `4242 4242 4242 4242` shows up in the table.
## By hand

**Bookshelf** sells a 5 USD membership. The commands run in the Docker server of the
[Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart) (`http://localhost:8080`); without Docker, drop
`docker compose exec dev-box`. Before you start: the sign-in pages of
[Authentication](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication) (`Route::auth`), and a
[Stripe](https://stripe.com/) account.

**1. The keys.** In the [Stripe dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys), copy the test keys into `.env`:

```text
PAY_PUBLIC_KEY_TEST=pk_test_...
PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_TEST=sk_test_...
PAY_PUBLIC_KEY_PRODUCTION=pk_live_...
PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_PRODUCTION=sk_live_...
```

`APP_ENV=local` uses the test keys; `APP_ENV=production` the live ones.

**2. The payments table.** Write `application/models/Payments/create_db.sql`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS payments (
    id int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    stripe_session varchar(255) NOT NULL,
    amount int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    created_at datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    UNIQUE KEY payments_stripe_session_unique (stripe_session)
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8mb4;
```

Run `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/Payments/create_db.sql`.

**3. The capability that starts the checkout.** Write `application/services/Payments/StartCheckout.php`:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Payment;
use Caligrafy\Service;

#[Capability(
    name: 'start_checkout',
    description: 'Starts a Stripe checkout for a 5 USD membership and returns the address of the Stripe payment page.',
    scope: 'payments:write'
)]
class StartCheckout extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('site' => '');
    public $descriptions = array('site' => 'The address of this site, for the way back from Stripe. APP_URL wins over it');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $site = rtrim((string) (getenv('APP_URL') ?: ($input['site'] ?? '')), '/');
        $result = (new Payment())->createCheckout(
            500,                                    // the amount in cents: 5.00
            'usd',
            1,                                      // the quantity
            array('name' => 'Bookshelf membership'),
            $site . '/membership/done?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}',
            $site . '/membership'
        );
        if (!$result['action_success']) {
            throw new \RuntimeException('Stripe refused the checkout: ' . $result['error']);
        }
        return array('url' => $result['url']);
    }
}
```

The two addresses are where Stripe sends the reader back: after paying, and with its back link. `APP_URL` (the app's
address, set by Caligrafy Cloud) wins over `site`. A capability does not read the session: the route gives it `site` in
step 5.

**4. The capability that records the payment.** Write `application/services/Payments/RecordPayment.php`:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Database;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\ServiceError;

#[Capability(
    name: 'record_payment',
    description: 'Records a paid Stripe checkout session. Called by the Stripe webhook.',
    mcp: false
)]
class RecordPayment extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('event' => 'required');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        if ($context->actorType() !== 'webhook') {
            throw ServiceError::forbidden('Payments are recorded by the Stripe webhook only');
        }
        $event = $input['event'];
        if (($event['type'] ?? '') !== 'checkout.session.completed') {
            return array('ignored' => true);
        }
        $session = $event['data']['object'];
        if (($session['payment_status'] ?? '') !== 'paid') {
            return array('ignored' => true);
        }
        if (Database::table('payments')->where('stripe_session', $session['id'])->exists()) {
            return array('duplicate' => true);
        }
        Database::table('payments')->insert(array(
            'stripe_session' => $session['id'],
            'amount' => (int) $session['amount_total'],
            'status' => 'paid',
        ));
        return array('recorded' => true);
    }
}
```

+ The `actorType()` check matters: without it any signed-in person could call `record_payment` through the REST API
  with an event they made up.
+ Stripe sends an event again until it gets a `2xx`: the `exists()` check records a session once.

**5. The routes.** In `application/config/routing/web.php`, below `Route::auth(...)`:

```php
    Route::page('/membership', 'Bookshelf/membership', ['signedIn' => true, 'comeBack' => true]);
    Route::form('/membership/checkout', 'start_checkout', [
        'inputs' => fn () => ['site' => session('home')],             // only the server sets it, whatever the form sends
        'success' => fn ($result) => $result['url'],                  // a full address: the payment page of Stripe
        'back' => '/membership',
    ]);
    Route::page('/membership/done', 'Bookshelf/membership-done', ['signedIn' => true]);
    Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_payment', ['verify' => 'stripe']);
```

`success` is a function here because the address comes from Stripe: the form sends the reader to it.

**6. The pages.** Write `application/views/Bookshelf/membership.pug`:

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block title
  | Membership

block content
  main
    h1 Membership
    p A year of Bookshelf for 5 USD.
    form(method='POST', action=$home . 'membership/checkout')
      =csrf()
      button.btn.btn-primary(type='submit') Pay with Stripe
```

and `application/views/Bookshelf/membership-done.pug`:

```pug
extends ../default/master/site

block title
  | Thank you

block content
  main
    h1 Thank you
    p Your payment is being confirmed. It appears in your account within a minute.
```

**7. The webhook secret.** Stripe signs each event with the secret of its endpoint, `whsec_...`:

+ **On your computer**, the [Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/stripe-cli) forwards the test events:
  `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8080/stripe/events` prints a `whsec_...` secret.
+ **Online**, in the dashboard (Developers, Webhooks), add the endpoint `https://<your app>/stripe/events` with the
  event `checkout.session.completed`, and copy its signing secret.

Put it in `.env`:

```text
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...
```

**8. Try it.** Sign in, open `/membership`, press *Pay with Stripe*: Stripe's page opens. Pay with the test card
`4242 4242 4242 4242`, any future date, any CVC. Stripe brings you back to `/membership/done`, and its event adds a row
to `payments` (`status` `paid`, `amount` `500`).

To try the webhook with no Stripe at all, sign an event yourself. Write `tests/sign.php` (`tests/` is never served):

```php
<?php
// php tests/sign.php <secret> <file>: the Stripe-Signature header of the file's body
$time = time();
$body = file_get_contents($argv[2]);
echo 't=' . $time . ',v1=' . hash_hmac('sha256', $time . '.' . $body, $argv[1]);
```

and `tests/event.json`:

```json
{"id":"evt_test_1","type":"checkout.session.completed","data":{"object":{"id":"cs_test_a1","payment_status":"paid","amount_total":500}}}
```

then, with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_test_docs` in `.env`:

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Stripe-Signature: $(docker compose exec -T dev-box php tests/sign.php whsec_test_docs tests/event.json)" \
  --data-binary @tests/event.json http://localhost:8080/stripe/events
```

| You send | You get |
|---|---|
| the event, signed | `200 {"received":true}` and a row in `payments` |
| the same event again | `200 {"received":true}`, still one row |
| `Stripe-Signature: t=1,v1=bad`, or no header | `400 {"error":{"code":"invalid_signature","message":"The Stripe signature is not valid"}}` |
| any event with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` empty | `500 {"error":{"code":"error","message":"The webhook is not set up"}}` |
| `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php call record_payment '{"event":{"type":"x"}}'` | `{"error":{"code":"forbidden","message":"Payments are recorded by the Stripe webhook only"}}` |

`docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php audit` shows each event as `webhook /stripe/events record_payment ok`.

**Check**

+ `payments` has one row per paid session, whatever the number of times Stripe sent it.
+ A bad signature gets `400`; no one but the webhook can record a payment.
+ `.env` (keys and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) is not committed.
## <a name="going-live"></a>Going live

With `APP_ENV=production`, payments use the `PAY_*_PRODUCTION` (live) keys: real cards, real money. Try one real
payment of a small amount, then refund it from the Stripe dashboard.

Stripe keeps **one list of webhook endpoints per mode, each with its own secret**:

+ Create the endpoint again in **live mode** and give the server its live signing secret (`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; on
  Caligrafy Cloud, `php caligrafer.php cloud secret set <app> STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...`, then deploy).
+ A **test-mode** endpoint left on the production address fails: the server checks the test events with the live secret
  and answers `400`. Stripe retries, emails you, and stops sending to the endpoint after about nine days. Disable it
  (Developers, Webhooks, in test mode), or point it at a test server.

`php caligrafer.php doctor --only stripe,coinbase` checks the keys without creating anything: it reads the Stripe
balance (and says test or live mode) and lists one Coinbase checkout.
## <a name="webhook"></a>Reference: `Route::webhook`

```php
Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_payment', ['verify' => 'stripe']);
Route::webhook('/hooks/github', 'record_push', ['verify' => function ($rawBody, $headers) {
    return hash_equals('sha256=' . hash_hmac('sha256', $rawBody, getenv('GITHUB_SECRET')), $headers['x-hub-signature-256'] ?? '');
}]);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `verify` | required | `'stripe'`, or a function `($rawBody, $headers): bool` (header names in lower case); anything else stops `web.php` with an error |
| `secret_env` | `'STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET'` | the `.env` setting that holds the Stripe secret |
| `secret` | | the secret itself, instead of `secret_env` |
| `tolerance` | `300` | seconds a Stripe signature stays valid |

| The event | The answer |
|---|---|
| signature checked, capability done | `200 {"received": true}` |
| bad or missing signature, a body that is not JSON | `400` |
| the capability refuses (`ServiceError`) | its status and error |
| no secret set, no such capability, an error in the capability | `500` (the reason goes to the PHP error log) |

+ `POST` only. No session and no CSRF token: the signature is the only proof.
+ The capability gets `['event' => the decoded JSON body]` and runs as the system, with full access
  (`$context->actorType()` is `webhook`). Declare `public $rules = array('event' => 'required');`.
+ Before trusting an amount for something valuable, ask Stripe again: `(new Caligrafy\Payment())->retrieveCheckout($id)`.

## Reference: `Caligrafy\Payment`

```php
// a checkout on a page hosted by Stripe
public function createCheckout($amount = 1000, $currency = 'usd', $quantity = 1, $productData = array(), $successUrl = '', $cancelUrl = '', $customerEmail = null, $locale = null, $paymentType = null, $payment_intent_data = array(), $vendor = array())
public function retrieveCheckout($sessionId)        // its status: data->payment_status is 'paid' once paid

// a payment intent, for your own payment page (the Payment Element)
public function createPaymentIntent($amount, $currency, $metadata = array(), $receipt_email = null, $description = '', $transfer = array())
public function retrieveIntent($intentId)

// a charge from card data (only for Stripe accounts allowed to send raw card numbers)
public function createTransaction($amount, $currency, $card, $receipt_email = null, $metadata = null, $description = '', $transfer = array(), $save = false)

public function getPublicKey()                       // the publishable key of the current APP_ENV
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `$amount` | in cents (`500` is 5.00) |
| `$currency` | `'usd'`, `'eur'`... |
| `$productData` | `array('name' => ..., 'description' => ..., 'tax_code' => ...)` |
| `$successUrl` | where Stripe sends the customer after paying; `{CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` is replaced by the session id |
| `$cancelUrl` | where Stripe's back link goes |
| `$customerEmail`, `$locale` | fill in the email; the language of the page |
| `$paymentType` | leave `null`: the payment methods come from your Stripe dashboard |
| `$transfer`, `$payment_intent_data`, `$vendor` | Stripe Connect: `array('transfer_data' => ['destination' => 'acct_...'])`, `array('payment_intent_data' => ['application_fee_amount' => 200])`, `array('stripe_account' => 'acct_...')` |
| `$receipt_email`, `$metadata`, `$description` | a receipt address, your own key/value pairs, a description |

+ Every method returns `array('action_success' => true, 'data' => <Stripe object>)`, or
  `array('action_success' => false, 'error' => '<message>')`. `createCheckout()` adds `'url'`, the Stripe page;
  `createTransaction()` returns `'data' => array('confirmation' => <charge id>)`.
+ **Tax codes.** New Stripe accounts have Managed Payments on and refuse a product without a tax code. A
  `createCheckout()` without `tax_code` creates a classic Checkout (`managed_payments` off). To use Managed Payments,
  give the product its code (`txcd_10103001` SaaS for business use, `txcd_10000000` electronically supplied services);
  `'managed_payments' => array('enabled' => true|false)` in `$payment_intent_data` decides either way.
+ An empty `PAY_PRIVATE_KEY_*` makes `new Payment()` throw (`api_key cannot be the empty string`).

**Stripe Connect** (vendors paid out by Stripe):

```php
public function createAccount($email = null, $country = null, $type = 'express', $capabilities = array(), $accountInformation = array())
public function createAccountLink($accountId, $refreshUrl, $returnUrl, $type = 'account_onboarding')
public function createLoginLink($accountId)
public function updateAccount($accountId, $updates)
public function retrieve($accountId)
```

**ACH (bank) payments** go through Stripe Checkout: turn ACH on in your Stripe payment methods, and `createCheckout()`
offers it.
## <a name="cryptocurrency"></a>Cryptocurrency (Coinbase Business)

Caligrafy accepts USDC on Base through the **Coinbase Business Checkouts API**: Caligrafy creates a checkout and the
customer pays on a page hosted by Coinbase. Coinbase Commerce shut down on March 31, 2026, with its `CRYPTO_PAY_KEY`
setting; Coinbase Business serves merchants in the countries it supports (the United States and Singapore at the time
of writing).

**1. The keys.** Open a [Coinbase Business](https://www.coinbase.com/business) account, then create a secret API key for
the Business API in the Coinbase Developer Platform (Ed25519). In `.env`:

```text
# organizations/<org_id>/apiKeys/<key_id>
COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME=organizations/...
# the Ed25519 secret in base64, or a legacy ECDSA PEM written on one line with \n
COINBASE_API_KEY_SECRET=...
```

Each request is signed with a JWT built from them (valid 2 minutes); the secret never leaves your server.

**2. The capability.** Write `application/services/Payments/StartCryptoCheckout.php`:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\CryptoPayment;
use Caligrafy\Service;

#[Capability(
    name: 'start_crypto_checkout',
    description: 'Starts a Coinbase checkout for a 5 USD membership and returns the address of the payment page.',
    scope: 'payments:write'
)]
class StartCryptoCheckout extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('site' => '');
    public $descriptions = array('site' => 'The address of this site, for the way back from Coinbase. APP_URL wins over it');

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $site = rtrim((string) (getenv('APP_URL') ?: ($input['site'] ?? '')), '/');
        $result = (new CryptoPayment())->createTransaction(5, 'USD',
            array('name' => 'Bookshelf membership', 'description' => 'A year of Bookshelf'),
            array('user' => (string) $context->userId()),
            $site . '/membership/done', $site . '/membership');
        if (!$result['action_success']) {
            throw new \RuntimeException('Coinbase refused the checkout: ' . $result['error']);
        }
        return array('url' => $result['url']);
    }
}
```

**3. The route and the button.**

```php
    Route::form('/membership/crypto', 'start_crypto_checkout', [
        'inputs' => fn () => ['site' => session('home')],
        'success' => fn ($result) => $result['url'],
        'back' => '/membership',
    ]);
```

```pug
    form(method='POST', action=$home . 'membership/crypto')
      =csrf()
      button.btn.btn-secondary(type='submit') Pay with USDC
```

Coinbase needs `https://` addresses for both return links: try it on a server with HTTPS. Each checkout can be paid
once and expires after 24 hours by default.

```php
public function createTransaction($amount, $currency, $charge = array(), $metadata = array(), $redirectUrl = '', $cancelUrl = '', $expiresAt = null)
// ['action_success' => true, 'url' => <hosted payment page>, 'data' => <checkout>]
public function getCharge($chargeId)            // a checkout by id
public function getChargeStatus($chargeId)      // ACTIVE, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, EXPIRED, FAILED, DEACTIVATED, REFUNDED, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, or 'unknown'
public function getCharges($filters = array())  // filters: status, startTime, endTime, descriptionQuery, pageSize, pageToken
public function cancelTransaction($id)          // deactivates an active checkout
public function refundTransaction($id, $amount = null, $currency = 'USDC', $reason = '') // full refund when $amount is null
```

`new CryptoPayment($keyName, $keySecret)` uses another account. Every method but `getChargeStatus()` returns
`array('action_success' => ..., 'data' => ...)` or `array('action_success' => false, 'error' => ...)`.
## Other ways

**The Payment Element on your own page.** For a payment form on your own page (cards, wallets, 3D Secure), opening the
page creates a payment intent and hands its client secret to the page Caligrafy ships, `default/pages/payment.pug` (with
`public/js/services/stripe_client.js`, the Payment Element and `stripe.confirmPayment`). A `GET` that changes something is
not a `Route::page`: it is a web-only capability, `application/services/Payments/PayPage.php`:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Payment;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\Web;

#[Capability(name: 'pay_page', description: 'The payment page of a 5 USD membership.', webOnly: true)]
class PayPage extends Service
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $payment = new Payment();
        $result = $payment->createPaymentIntent(500, 'usd');
        $secret = $result['action_success'] ? $result['data']->client_secret : null;
        return Web::view('default/pages/payment', array('clientSecret' => $secret, 'publicKey' => $payment->getPublicKey()));
    }
}
```

with `Route::action('/pay', 'pay_page', ['comeBack' => true]);` (no `public: true`: a visitor signs in first and comes
back). Record the payment from the webhook (`payment_intent.succeeded`), as above.

**A controller around Checkout.** Projects made before 2.19.0 create the checkout in a controller and show
`default/pages/checkout.pug` with its `checkoutUrl`. They keep working; `StartCheckout` and `Route::form` replace them.

**A charge from card numbers** (`createTransaction()` with `'tok_visa'` in test mode, or raw card data): only for Stripe
accounts allowed to handle raw card data. Prefer Checkout.
## Common mistakes

+ **Every event answers 500.** `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is empty, or holds the API key instead of the endpoint's
  `whsec_...`.
+ **Every event answers 400 online.** A test-mode endpoint checked with the live secret, or the reverse (see
  [Going live](#going-live)).
+ **A payment recorded twice.** Stripe retries: check that the session is not recorded yet, as `RecordPayment` does.
+ **Anyone can record a payment.** A webhook capability is also a REST capability: refuse callers whose
  `$context->actorType()` is not `webhook`.
+ **`the product tax code is missing`.** A product with Managed Payments on and no tax code: give a `tax_code`, or leave
  it out to get a classic Checkout.
+ **The way back breaks on a test server.** Build the return addresses from `APP_URL` or from `session('home')` given by
  the route's `inputs`, never a fixed `https://` address.
+ **A payment created in `Route::page`.** Pages take read-only capabilities: use `Route::form`, or `Route::action` when
  opening the address must create it.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition -->

**FaceDetect** finds faces in a camera, a video or a picture, and recognizes whose face it is, in the browser. It is a
JavaScript class, `FaceDetector` (`public/js/services/detect.js`), built on
[@vladmandic/face-api](https://github.com/vladmandic/face-api) 1.7.15 (the maintained successor of face-api.js) and
its TensorFlow.js models, which ship with Caligrafy in `public/resources/models`. The pictures never leave the browser
unless your code sends them. `FaceDetector` also gives face prints and a liveness check, which the server-side class
`Caligrafy\FaceLogin` uses for [face sign-in](#face-login).

In the Bookshelf example, a page checks that the photo of a library card shows exactly one face.
> #### ![](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/public/images/resources/play.png) [Detecting and Recognizing human faces with Caligrafy](https://youtu.be/uUcr6JM00S4)
>
> The video shows how the FaceDetect library detects and recognizes faces.
## With Claude

```text
/caligrafy-quill:new-app facedetect faces
```

Claude checks the name, runs `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php facedetect faces`, and gives you the address of the app
(`/apps/faces`). Then describe what the app should do: *"a page that checks that a library card photo has exactly one
face"*, or *"face sign-in with liveness and passkeys"*, for which Claude follows the plugin's face login recipe.

**Check**
- The detector is created with `Vue.markRaw(new FaceDetector('detection'))` in a Vue app.
- The markup keeps `#detector`, the media with `id="detection"`, `#apps` and `#infobar`.
- A blocked or missing camera is told to the person (`{ autoStart: false }` and `startStream()` in a `try`).
- Face sign-in is never one face print: it uses the server challenge, `liveness()` and `FaceLogin::verify()`, and
  offers a passkey.
## By hand

Run the commands in the project folder of the [Quickstart](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Quickstart).
Without Docker (Composer with MAMP, XAMPP or LAMP), run the same commands without `docker compose exec dev-box` and
open your own address.

### Step 1: Create the app

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php facedetect faces
```

Expected:

```text
 Project created in the public folder.
 Type cd public/faces to access it anytime
```

It copies `framework/plugins/facedetect` to `public/faces`: `index.php` (the markup), `scripts/main.js` (a Vue app),
`css/styles.css` and `recognition/Flash/1.png` to `6.png` (pictures for the recognition example). No route to add: the
generic route of `web.php` serves every client app:

```php
Route::get('/apps/{appName}', 'Caligrafy\\Controllers\\ClientController'); // you can specify any path as long as it ends with appName
```

`Route::page('/apps/{appName}', 'Client/app', ['query' => ['app' => 'index']]);` is the same line, declared.

### Step 2: Try it

Open `http://localhost:8080/apps/faces` and allow the camera (the camera needs `https` or `localhost`). The camera
fills the screen, with six buttons at the bottom: **Detect**, **Full Detection** (box, landmarks, gender, age,
expression), **Recognize** (finds Flash), **Puppeteer** (a line drawing of the face without the video),
**Custom continuous** and **Custom callback** (they print to the browser console). When the camera is blocked, the
top of the screen says *The camera is blocked: allow it in the address bar, then reload the page.*

### Step 3: A page of your own: the library card photo

A client app can have several pages: `?app=<file>` opens `public/faces/<file>.php`. Create
**`public/faces/cardphoto.php`**:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
        <title>Card photo</title>
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/tokens.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/layout.css';?>">
        <link rel="stylesheet" href="<?php echo session('public').'css/look.css';?>">
    </head>
    <body class="cq-site">
        <section class="cq-hero cq-hero--page">
            <h1 class="cq-display">Library card photo</h1>
        </section>
        <section class="cq-band cq-band--tight">
            <div class="cq-inner cq-inner--narrow">
                <form id="photo" method="POST">
                    <div class="cq-field">
                        <label for="file">Your photo</label>
                        <input id="file" class="form-control" type="file" name="file" accept="image/png,image/jpeg">
                    </div>
                </form>
                <p id="result" class="cq-lead" role="status">Loading the face models...</p>
                <img id="detection" alt="Your photo" width="320" hidden>
            </div>
        </section>

        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
        <script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'face-api.min.js'; ?>"></script>
        <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'detect.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/detect.js'); ?>"></script>
        <script>loadVue({ scripts: ['cardphoto'] });</script>
    </body>
</html>
```

`loadVue({ scripts: [...] })` adds `public/faces/scripts/<name>.js` to the page (with or without Vue). Create
**`public/faces/scripts/cardphoto.js`**:

```js
// Checks that a library card photo shows exactly one face, in the browser: the photo is not sent anywhere
const detector = new FaceDetector('detection');   // an <img>: no camera
const image = document.getElementById('detection');
const result = document.getElementById('result');

detector.ready.then(() => { result.textContent = 'Choose a photo of your face.'; });

document.getElementById('file').addEventListener('change', (event) => {
    const file = event.target.files[0];
    if (!file) return;
    result.textContent = 'Checking...';
    image.onload = async () => {
        image.hidden = false;
        try {
            const print = await detector.faceprint(image);
            result.textContent = 'Good photo: one face, ' + Math.round(print.detection.score * 100) + '% sure.';
        } catch (error) {
            // 'No face found' or 'More than one face found'
            result.textContent = error.message + ': choose another photo.';
        }
    };
    image.src = URL.createObjectURL(file);
});
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/apps/faces?app=cardphoto`. The text changes to *Choose a photo of your face.* when the
models are loaded. Choose a portrait: *Good photo: one face, 99% sure.* Choose a picture with no face: *No face found:
choose another photo.*

### Step 4: Recognize your own people

1. Create one folder per person in `public/faces/recognition/`, named after them, with PNG pictures named `1.png`,
   `2.png`... (the same number for every person): `public/faces/recognition/Ada/1.png` to `4.png`.
2. In `public/faces/scripts/main.js`, change the **Recognize** app:

```js
this.loadApp({
    name: 'Recognize',
    method: this.detector.recognize,
    models: {
        labels: ['Flash', 'Ada'],   // the folder names
        sampleSize: 4               // pictures per person
    },
    options: {
        welcome: 'Show your face',
        recognition: true
    },
    algorithm: faceapi.SsdMobilenetv1Options
});
```

Reload `/apps/faces` and click **Recognize**: a box with the name and the distance (`Ada (0.41)`) follows each known
face, `unknown` the others. A picture in which no face is found is skipped, so use clear, front-facing portraits.

**Check**
- `/apps/faces` shows the six buttons and the camera (or the blocked-camera message).
- `?app=cardphoto` answers *Good photo* for one face and *No face found* / *More than one face found* otherwise.
- The browser console has no errors once the models are loaded.
## Reference

### The app's files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `public/<app>/index.php` | the markup (opened by `/apps/<app>`); `?app=<file>` opens `public/<app>/<file>.php` |
| `public/<app>/scripts/main.js` | the Vue app that creates the detector and loads the apps |
| `public/<app>/css/styles.css` | the app's styles, after `public/css/camera.css` and `look.css` |
| `public/<app>/recognition/<Name>/<n>.png` | the pictures of each person to recognize |
| `public/js/services/detect.js` | `FaceDetector` and `LivenessTracker` |
| `public/js/services/face-api.min.js` | @vladmandic/face-api 1.7.15 (TensorFlow.js 4 included) |
| `public/resources/models/` | the models (`*-weights_manifest.json` + `*.bin`): SSD MobileNet v1, Tiny Face Detector, 68 landmarks, age and gender, recognition, expressions |

## FaceDetect markup components

### The screen: the camera fills it

```html
<body class="cq-camera-body">
    <div id="app" class="cq-camera">
        <section id="detector" class="cq-camera-media">
            <video id="detection" width="640" height="480" class="show" autoplay="autoplay" muted playsinline></video>
        </section>
        <header class="cq-camera-top">
            <h1 class="cq-camera-title">Face Detect</h1>
            <section id="infobar" class="cq-camera-status"></section>
        </header>
        <section class="controls cq-camera-bottom">
            <div id="apps" class="cq-camera-actions"></div>
        </section>
    </div>
```

| Part | Role |
|---|---|
| `#detector` | the block the detector draws in: its canvas (`#detectfaces`) is added there |
| `#detection` | the media: a `<video>` without `src` (the camera), a `<video src="...">` or an `<img>`. Its `width` and `height` only size it on the page: the canvas takes the size of the picture itself (the camera's resolution, `detector.mediaSize()`, 2.19.2), so the drawings stay on the faces whatever shape the camera sends |
| `#apps` | where `loadApp()` adds one button per app |
| `#infobar` | where `display()` writes messages (the `welcome` text, camera errors) |

`public/css/camera.css` (2.11.0+) gives the full-screen camera: `cq-camera-mirror` on `.cq-camera-media` for a selfie
camera, `.cq-camera-oval` (`.is-scanning`, `.is-success`, `.is-failed`) to guide a face, `.cq-camera-sheet` over a
`.cq-camera-backdrop` for a form over the camera, `button.cq-camera-button.is-primary` for the main action. A
[design style](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Design-Styles) restyles it through the `--cq-camera-*` tokens.

### Scripts

```html
<script src="<?php echo scripts('vue'); ?>"></script>          <!-- with Vue only -->
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>"></script>
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'face-api.min.js'; ?>"></script>
<script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'detect.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/detect.js'); ?>"></script>
<script>loadEnvironment(`<?php echo $env; ?>`);</script>
<script>loadVue({ scripts: ['main'] });</script>
```

`loadEnvironment()` defines `env` (with `env.home`, `env.appName`, `env.app_resources`, from which the models load).

### `new FaceDetector(media, options = {})`

`media` is the id of the `<video>`, `<img>` or `<canvas>`. The models start loading at once; `detector.ready` is a
promise that resolves when they are loaded. With `options.autoStart` (default `true`) and a `<video>` without a
source, the camera starts once the models are loaded. In a Vue 3 app, wrap it in `Vue.markRaw()` before putting it in
`data`: otherwise Vue wraps the canvases, streams and models in reactive proxies, which slows or breaks the detections.

```js
var detector = Vue.markRaw(new FaceDetector('detection'));
```

### Controlling the camera

To tell the person when the camera is blocked or missing, create the detector with `{ autoStart: false }` and start
the camera yourself. `startStream()` rejects with the browser's error: `NotAllowedError` (blocked), `NotFoundError`
(no camera); the error is also in `detector.streamError`.

```js
var detector = Vue.markRaw(new FaceDetector('detection', { autoStart: false }));

// in a Vue method: the promise waits for as long as the person takes to answer the permission prompt
async startCamera() {
    try {
        await detector.startStream({ video: { facingMode: 'user' }, audio: false });  // getUserMedia constraints
    } catch (error) {
        this.message = error.name === 'NotAllowedError' ? 'Allow camera access, then retry' : 'No camera found';
    }
}

detector.stopStream(); // turns the camera off
```

The buttons of `loadApp()` appear at once and work as soon as the models are loaded.

### `loadApp(settings)`

Without settings it adds **Detect** (boxes around faces). Otherwise:

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `name` | the button's text |
| `method` | `detector.draw` (draws the options below), `detector.recognize` (names the faces), or your function, which gets the detector |
| `custom` | `false` (default): `method` runs at every detection, every 100 ms, with `detector.app.detections`. `true`: `method` runs once when the button is clicked, with the canvas ready and no detection started |
| `algorithm` | `faceapi.TinyFaceDetectorOptions` (default, faster) or `faceapi.SsdMobilenetv1Options` (more accurate) |
| `options.welcome` | the message shown in the infobar |
| `options.detection` | draws a box around each face |
| `options.landmarks` | draws the 68 landmarks |
| `options.puppeteer` | hides the video and draws only the landmarks |
| `options.gender`, `options.age` | writes the estimated gender and age |
| `options.expression` | writes the most likely expression (neutral, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised) when above 90% |
| `options.recognition` | loads the `models` for `recognize` |
| `models.labels` | the people: the folder names in `recognition/` |
| `models.sampleSize` | pictures per person (required: 0 loads nothing) |
| `models.images` | picture URLs to use instead of the folders (one list, or one list per label) |

### Face prints

`faceprint(media = null, minConfidence = 0.6)` returns the face print of the only face in the media:
`{ descriptor: [128 numbers], detection }` (the detection has `score` and `box`). It rejects with `No face found` or
`More than one face found`. Two prints of the same person are usually closer than 0.5
(`faceapi.euclideanDistance(a, b)`), prints of different people further than 0.6.

```js
await detector.ready;
const print = await detector.faceprint();            // the detector's media
const other = await detector.faceprint(someImage);   // any <img>, <video> or <canvas>
faceapi.euclideanDistance(print.descriptor, other.descriptor) < 0.5;  // probably the same person
```

A single face print is not a sign-in: a photo held to the camera gives one, and a print sent once can be sent again.

### Liveness

`liveness(options)` asks the person to do challenges in front of the camera and captures face prints while they move.
It follows the head turn (yaw) and the `happy` expression frame by frame: a turn starts facing the camera, a smile
starts neutral, so a photo fails.

```js
const result = await detector.liveness({
    challenges: ['turn-left', 'smile'],   // in this order; left and right are the person's own
    timeout: 20000,                       // ms for the whole check
    prints: 4,                            // face prints to capture
    onProgress: (p) => console.log(`${p.index + 1}/${p.total}: ${p.challenge}`)
});
// { passed: true, reason: null, challenges: [{ name, passed, at }], prints: [{ descriptor, challenge, at }], frames, duration }
```

| Option | Default |
|---|---|
| `challenges` | `['turn-left', 'smile']` (also `turn-right`; there is no `blink`) |
| `timeout` | `20000` ms |
| `prints` | `4`; the check passes with at least 3 (or `prints` when lower), the minimum of `FaceLogin::verify()` |
| `printInterval` | `350` ms between prints |
| `onProgress` | called with `{ challenge, index, total, passed }` when a challenge starts or passes |
| `thresholds` | overrides of `FaceDetector.LIVENESS_THRESHOLDS` = `{ frontalYaw: 0.15, turnYaw: 0.3, neutral: 0.3, smile: 0.8 }` |

It does not reject when the check fails: `passed` is `false` and `reason` says why (`Challenge not completed: smile`,
`More than one face found`, `Not enough face prints`). It rejects only when the models or the media cannot be used.
With a server challenge, keep `timeout` within its `expires_in`.

### Other methods and properties

| Member | What it is |
|---|---|
| `detector.app.detections` | the faces of the last detection (resized to the canvas): `detection.box`, `landmarks`, `descriptor`, `age`, `gender`, `expressions` |
| `detector.app.recognitions` | the matches, once `recognize` runs |
| `detector.app.canvas`, `detector.app.options` | the drawing canvas and the app's options |
| `detector.media` | the media element (`width`, `height`) |
| `detector.options` | `{ autoStart: true }` by default |
| `detector.streamError` | the last camera error, or `null` |
| `loadRecognition({ labels, images, sampleSize })` | promise of the `LabeledFaceDescriptors` of each person |
| `recognize(detector)`, `draw(detector)` | the drawing methods used by `loadApp()` |
| `detect(callback, recognize = false, fetchRate = 100)` | calls `callback` with the detections (or recognitions) every `fetchRate` ms |
| `detectFaces(app, detector)` | returns the function that starts the detection loop of an app |
| `prepareCanva(options)` | a new canvas over the media (stops the running app), fitted on the page the way the media is (`object-fit`) |
| `mediaSize()` | the size of the picture the media holds: `{width, height}` of the camera's resolution (`videoWidth` x `videoHeight`), an image's natural size, else its attributes (2.19.2). The canvas and `detector.app.detections` use it |
| `fetchImage(canvas, media)` | a data URL of the whole media drawn at the canvas's size |
| `display(message, output)`, `clearDisplay()` | write in the infobar, clear it |
| `FaceDetector.headYaw(points)`, `FaceDetector.frameSummary(points, expressions, at)`, `LivenessTracker` | the pure logic of the liveness check |

The face-api functions are available as `faceapi.*`: `detectAllFaces(media, options)` and `detectSingleFace()` (then
`.withFaceLandmarks()`, `.withFaceDescriptors()`, `.withAgeAndGender()`, `.withFaceExpressions()`),
`FaceMatcher(labeledDescriptors, 0.6)`, `LabeledFaceDescriptors(label, descriptors)`, `euclideanDistance(a, b)`,
`draw.drawDetections(canvas, detections)`, `draw.DrawBox(box, {label, boxColor})`,
`draw.DrawFaceLandmarks(landmarks, settings)`, `draw.DrawTextField(lines, anchor)`, `matchDimensions()`,
`resizeResults()`, `createCanvasFromMedia()`, `fetchImage(url)`. See the [face-api documentation](https://github.com/vladmandic/face-api).
## Face login

Face sign-in uses the browser for the camera and the server for every decision. **`Route::auth` has no face option**:
face sign-in is a set of web-only capabilities served by `Route::action`, because they keep a nonce in the session and sign
people in, and this is the template to use. The challenges come from the server, so a recording
of an earlier sign-in does not do them in the right order:

1. `POST /facelogin/start`: `FaceLogin::challenge($username)` returns a single-use nonce and 2 of the 3 challenges in a
   random order, kept in the session for 60 seconds.
2. The browser runs `detector.liveness({ challenges })` and sends `{ nonce, liveness, prints }`.
3. `POST /facelogin/login`: `FaceLogin::verify()` uses up the nonce (once, even when the check fails), requires the
   liveness result for the requested challenges in that order, and 3 to 12 prints of the same face that are **not
   identical** (identical prints are a replayed print, not a live camera). `FaceLogin::match()` then finds the account;
   prints already used by an earlier sign-in are refused.

**Honest limits.** Liveness in the browser stops photos, replayed requests and replayed prints. It does not stop a
determined attacker: a deepfake video through a virtual camera, or a modified page that sends made-up prints, can pass.
Use face sign-in as a convenience and require a [passkey](#passkeys) for sensitive accounts.

The steps need sign-in ([`Auth::authentication('User', 'users')`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication)
and its `users` table).

**1. The tables.** Create **`application/models/FaceLogin/create_db.sql`**:

```sql
-- Face login and passkeys for the users of the authentication module (users table). Safe to run more than once.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS face_prints (
  id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  descriptor TEXT NOT NULL,                      -- encryptDecrypt('encrypt', json) with APP_KEY, never plain
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT fk_face_prints_user_id FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

-- hashes of the prints of accepted logins: the same prints sent again with a new nonce are refused
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS face_login_used_prints (
  id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  print_hash CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT uq_face_login_used_prints_hash UNIQUE (print_hash),
  CONSTRAINT fk_face_login_used_prints_user_id FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

-- failures live in their own table, not on users: a change to the users row signs its owner out
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS face_login_attempts (
  id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  attempt_key VARCHAR(191) NOT NULL,             -- client IP + username ('*' for 1:N)
  failures INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  locked_until DATETIME NULL,
  modified_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT uq_face_login_attempts_key UNIQUE (attempt_key)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;

-- passkeys (Caligrafy\Passkey)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS passkeys (
  id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INT NOT NULL,
  credential_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,           -- base64url
  public_key TEXT NOT NULL,                      -- PEM
  sign_count INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  name VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Passkey',
  transports VARCHAR(255) NULL,
  aaguid CHAR(32) NULL,
  created_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  last_used_at DATETIME NULL,
  CONSTRAINT uq_passkeys_credential_id UNIQUE (credential_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_passkeys_user_id FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php sql application/models/FaceLogin/create_db.sql
```

Expected: `application/models/FaceLogin/create_db.sql run on <your database>`.

**2. The routes**, in **`application/config/routing/web.php`** (the page is the generic `/apps/facelogin`):

```php
Route::action('/facelogin/password', 'facelogin_password', ['method' => 'POST']);   // password sign-in from the page (before enrolment)
Route::action('/facelogin/register', 'facelogin_register', ['method' => 'POST']);   // new account from the page
Route::action('/facelogin/start', 'facelogin_start', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/facelogin/enroll', 'facelogin_enroll', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/facelogin/login', 'facelogin_login', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/facelogin/me', 'facelogin_me');
Route::action('/facelogin/logout', 'facelogin_logout', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/passkey/register/options', 'facepasskey_register_options', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/passkey/register', 'facepasskey_register', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/passkey/login/options', 'facepasskey_login_options', ['method' => 'POST']);
Route::action('/passkey/login', 'facepasskey_login', ['method' => 'POST']);
```

These passkey routes replace `Route::auth(['passkeys' => true])`: do not declare both. Each line serves a
[web-only capability](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#webonly): nothing but these routes reaches them. The page sends the
`X-CSRF-Token` header (`apiHeaders()`), which `Route::action` requires of every JSON call.

**3. The capabilities.** **`application/services/FaceLogin/FaceLoginCapabilities.php`**:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Auth;
use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Database;
use Caligrafy\FaceLogin;
use Caligrafy\FaceLoginException;
use Caligrafy\Passkey;
use Caligrafy\Service;
use Caligrafy\Web;

/**
 * Face login with a liveness check (FaceDetector.liveness() + Caligrafy\FaceLogin) for the users of the authentication
 * module. Enrolment: a password sign-in (or a new account) first, then a liveness check. Login: a liveness check (the
 * challenges chosen by facelogin_start), then the face is matched.
 * Web-only capabilities: they keep a nonce in the session and sign people in, so only Route::action reaches them.
 */
abstract class FaceLoginAction extends Service
{
    const MAX_FAILURES = 5;
    const LOCK_SECONDS = 60;
    // what face login does for accounts that have a passkey:
    //   'face'    face alone logs in (convenience)
    //   'step-up' face, then the passkey (2 factors) - recommended for sensitive accounts
    //   'passkey' face login refused: the account logs in with its passkey only
    const PASSKEY_POLICY = 'step-up';
    const PENDING = '__face_pending';      // face checked, passkey expected

    protected function fail($code, $message) { return Web::json(['error' => $message], $code); }

    // lockout after MAX_FAILURES (kept outside users): [locked?, function($code, $message) recording a failure]
    protected function guard($key) {
        $now = gmdate('Y-m-d H:i:s');
        $attempt = Database::toArray(Database::execute('SELECT * FROM face_login_attempts WHERE attempt_key = ?', [$key]))[0] ?? null;
        $locked = $attempt && $attempt['locked_until'] && $attempt['locked_until'] > $now;
        $failed = function ($code, $message) use ($attempt, $key, $now) {
            $failures = ($attempt && (!$attempt['locked_until'] || $attempt['locked_until'] <= $now) ? (int)$attempt['failures'] : 0) + 1;
            $lock = $failures >= self::MAX_FAILURES ? gmdate('Y-m-d H:i:s', time() + self::LOCK_SECONDS) : null;
            Database::execute('INSERT INTO face_login_attempts (attempt_key, failures, locked_until, modified_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
                               ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE failures = VALUES(failures), locked_until = VALUES(locked_until), modified_at = VALUES(modified_at)',
                              [$key, $lock ? 0 : $failures, $lock, $now]);
            return $this->fail($code, $message);
        };
        return [$locked, $failed];
    }

    // a new session id on every sign-in (fixation). The page stays open, so its CSRF token stays: not AuthRoutes::signIn()
    protected function mayChangeSignIn() {   // a face alone does not prove a person: a photo can pass
        return in_array(\Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::signedInBy(), ['password', 'passkey', 'face+passkey'], true);
    }

    protected function signIn($user, $factors, $status = 200) {
        session_regenerate_id(true);
        Auth::authorize($user);
        \Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::rememberSignIn(implode('+', $factors));   // what mayChangeSignIn() reads
        return Web::json(['user' => ['username' => $user->username], 'factors' => $factors, 'enrolled' => count($this->enrolled((int)$user->id)) > 0], $status);
    }

    protected function username($input) {
        $username = trim((string)($input['username'] ?? ''));
        return $username === '' || preg_match('/^[A-Za-z0-9._@-]{1,100}$/', $username) ? $username : null;
    }

    protected function enrolled($userId = null) {    // [['user' => id, 'descriptor' => [128]], ...]
        $sql = 'SELECT user_id, descriptor FROM face_prints' . ($userId ? ' WHERE user_id = ?' : '');
        $rows = Database::toArray(Database::execute($sql, $userId ? [$userId] : [])) ?: [];
        return array_map(fn($r) => ['user' => (int)$r['user_id'], 'descriptor' => json_decode(encryptDecrypt('decrypt', $r['descriptor']), true)], $rows);
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/start { username?, enroll? } -> { nonce, challenges, expires_in }
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_start', description: 'Starts a face scan: a single-use nonce and the liveness challenges.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginStart extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public $rules = ['username' => '', 'enroll' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        if (!empty($input['enroll'])) {                           // enrolment: the signed-in account
            return $this->mayChangeSignIn() ? Web::json(FaceLogin::challenge(user()->username)) : $this->fail(401, 'Log in with your password first');
        }
        $username = $this->username($input);
        if ($username === null) { return $this->fail(422, 'Invalid username'); }
        return Web::json(FaceLogin::challenge($username));
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/enroll { nonce, liveness, prints } - signed-in people only
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_enroll', description: 'Enrols the face of the signed-in person, after a liveness check.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginEnroll extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public $rules = ['nonce' => '', 'liveness' => '', 'prints' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        if (!$this->mayChangeSignIn()) { return $this->fail(401, 'Log in with your password first'); }
        $user = user();
        try {
            $prints = FaceLogin::verify($input, $user->username);
        } catch (FaceLoginException $e) {
            return $this->fail($e->getCode(), $e->getMessage());
        }
        if (FaceLogin::enrolledElsewhere($prints, $this->enrolled(), $user->id) !== null) {
            return $this->fail(409, 'This face is already enrolled on another account');
        }
        Database::execute('DELETE FROM face_prints WHERE user_id = ?', [$user->id]);
        foreach (array_slice($prints, 0, 5) as $print) {
            Database::execute('INSERT INTO face_prints (user_id, descriptor) VALUES (?, ?)', [$user->id, encryptDecrypt('encrypt', json_encode($print))]);
        }
        return Web::json(['enrolled' => min(5, count($prints))], 201);
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/password { username, password } - password sign-in before enrolment
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_password', description: 'Signs in with a username and a password, before enrolling a face.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginPassword extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public $rules = ['username' => '', 'password' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        $username = $this->username($input);
        if (!$username) { return $this->fail(422, 'Enter a valid username'); }
        $key = 'pw|' . ($_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'] ?? '') . '|' . strtolower($username);
        [$locked, $failed] = $this->guard($key);
        if ($locked) { return $this->fail(429, 'Too many failed attempts: wait a minute'); }
        $user = (new User('users'))->findByUsername($username);
        if (!$user) {
            // same work as a real check so that response times do not reveal which usernames exist
            password_verify((string)($input['password'] ?? ''), '$2y$10$B0NLUgDUK3CbImwrVfa/FuOtSOKrb7DZTGG3USPSF4Comn4cy5RtG');
        }
        if (!$user || !$user->verifyPassword((string)($input['password'] ?? ''))) {
            return $failed(401, 'Invalid username or password');
        }
        Database::execute('DELETE FROM face_login_attempts WHERE attempt_key = ?', [$key]);
        return $this->signIn($user, ['password']);
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/register { username, password } - creates the account and signs it in, ready to enrol
// (the rules of the authentication module's /register: letters and digits, passwords of 8 to 72 characters)
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_register', description: 'Creates an account and signs it in, ready to enrol a face.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginRegister extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public $rules = ['username' => '', 'password' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        $username = trim((string)($input['username'] ?? ''));
        $password = (string)($input['password'] ?? '');
        if (!preg_match('/^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,100}$/', $username)) { return $this->fail(422, 'Usernames use letters and digits (up to 100)'); }
        if (strlen($password) < 8 || strlen($password) > 72) { return $this->fail(422, 'Passwords need 8 to 72 characters'); }
        $users = new User('users');
        if ($users->findByUsername($username)) { return $this->fail(409, 'This username is taken'); }
        Database::execute('INSERT INTO users (username, passcode) VALUES (?, ?)', [$username, User::hashPassword($password)]);
        return $this->signIn($users->findByUsername($username), ['password'], 201);
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/login { username?, nonce, liveness, prints }
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_login', description: 'Signs in the account whose enrolled face matches the prints.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginLogin extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public $rules = ['username' => '', 'nonce' => '', 'liveness' => '', 'prints' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        $username = $this->username($input);
        if ($username === null) { return $this->fail(422, 'Invalid username'); }
        $key = ($_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'] ?? '') . '|' . ($username !== '' ? strtolower($username) : '*');
        [$locked, $failed] = $this->guard($key);
        if ($locked) { return $this->fail(429, 'Too many failed attempts: wait a minute'); }

        try {
            $prints = FaceLogin::verify($input, $username);       // nonce (single use), liveness, prints
        } catch (FaceLoginException $e) {
            return $failed($e->getCode(), $e->getMessage());
        }
        $users = new User('users');
        $target = $username !== '' ? $users->findByUsername($username) : null;
        $match = $username === '' || $target ? FaceLogin::match($prints, $this->enrolled($target ? (int)$target->id : null)) : null;
        if (!$match) {
            return $failed(401, 'Face not recognized');           // same message whether or not the username exists
        }
        $hashes = array_map([FaceLogin::class, 'printHash'], $prints);
        $seen = Database::toArray(Database::execute('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM face_login_used_prints WHERE print_hash IN (' . implode(',', array_fill(0, count($hashes), '?')) . ')', $hashes));
        if ((int)($seen[0]['n'] ?? 0) > 0) {
            return $failed(401, 'These face prints were already used: replay refused');
        }
        foreach ($hashes as $h) {
            Database::execute('INSERT IGNORE INTO face_login_used_prints (user_id, print_hash) VALUES (?, ?)', [$match['user'], $h]);
        }
        Database::execute('DELETE FROM face_login_attempts WHERE attempt_key = ?', [$key]);

        $user = $users->find($match['user']);
        $passkey = new Passkey();
        if (self::PASSKEY_POLICY !== 'face' && $passkey->credentials($user->id)) {
            if (self::PASSKEY_POLICY === 'passkey') { return $this->fail(403, 'This account logs in with its passkey'); }
            $_SESSION[self::PENDING] = ['user' => (string)$user->id, 'expires' => time() + 120];
            return Web::json(['step' => 'passkey', 'options' => $passkey->authenticationOptions($user->id)]);
        }
        return $this->signIn($user, ['face']);
    }
}

// GET /facelogin/me
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_me', description: 'Who is signed in, and whether their face is enrolled.', readOnly: true, public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginMe extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        if (!authorized()) { return $this->fail(401, 'Not logged in'); }
        return Web::json(['user' => ['username' => user()->username ?? null], 'enrolled' => count($this->enrolled((int)user()->id)) > 0]);
    }
}

// POST /facelogin/logout
#[Capability(name: 'facelogin_logout', description: 'Signs out.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FaceLoginLogout extends FaceLoginAction
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        Auth::unauthorize();
        session_regenerate_id(true);
        return Web::json(['loggedOut' => true]);
    }
}
```

**`application/services/FaceLogin/PasskeyCapabilities.php`**:

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Auth;
use Caligrafy\Capability;
use Caligrafy\Context;
use Caligrafy\Passkey;
use Caligrafy\PasskeyException;
use Caligrafy\Web;

/**
 * Passkeys (Caligrafy\Passkey): registration for signed-in people, sign-in alone or after face login (step-up)
 */
abstract class FacePasskeyAction extends FaceLoginAction
{
    // the user whose face was just recognized, waiting for the passkey (FaceLoginAction::PENDING)
    protected function pending() {
        $p = $_SESSION[self::PENDING] ?? null;
        return is_array($p) && $p['expires'] >= time() ? $p['user'] : null;
    }
}

// POST /passkey/register/options
#[Capability(name: 'facepasskey_register_options', description: 'The options to register a passkey.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FacePasskeyRegisterOptions extends FacePasskeyAction
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        if (!in_array(\Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::signedInBy(), ['password', 'passkey', 'face+passkey'], true)) { return $this->fail(401, 'Log in with your password first'); }
        $user = user();
        return Web::json((new Passkey())->registrationOptions($user->id, $user->username));
    }
}

// POST /passkey/register { id, clientDataJSON, attestationObject, transports, name? }
#[Capability(name: 'facepasskey_register', description: 'Registers a passkey for the signed-in person.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FacePasskeyRegister extends FacePasskeyAction
{
    public $rules = ['id' => '', 'clientDataJSON' => '', 'attestationObject' => '', 'transports' => '', 'name' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        if (!in_array(\Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::signedInBy(), ['password', 'passkey', 'face+passkey'], true)) { return $this->fail(401, 'Log in with your password first'); }
        try {
            $credential = (new Passkey())->register($input, user()->id, $input['name'] ?? null);
        } catch (PasskeyException $e) {
            return $this->fail($e->getCode(), $e->getMessage());
        }
        return Web::json(['passkey' => ['name' => $credential['name']]], 201);
    }
}

// POST /passkey/login/options: after face login only this user's passkeys, else any passkey of the site
#[Capability(name: 'facepasskey_login_options', description: 'The options to sign in with a passkey.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FacePasskeyLoginOptions extends FacePasskeyAction
{
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        return Web::json((new Passkey())->authenticationOptions($this->pending()));
    }
}

// POST /passkey/login { id, clientDataJSON, authenticatorData, signature, userHandle }
#[Capability(name: 'facepasskey_login', description: 'Signs in with a passkey, alone or after the face.', public: true, webOnly: true)]
class FacePasskeyLogin extends FacePasskeyAction
{
    public $rules = ['id' => '', 'clientDataJSON' => '', 'authenticatorData' => '', 'signature' => '', 'userHandle' => ''];

    public function handle(array $input, Context $context) {
        $pending = $this->pending();
        unset($_SESSION[self::PENDING]);
        try {
            $userId = (new Passkey())->authenticate($input);
        } catch (PasskeyException $e) {
            return $this->fail($e->getCode(), $e->getMessage());
        }
        if ($pending !== null && $pending !== $userId) { return $this->fail(401, 'This passkey belongs to another account'); }
        $user = (new User('users'))->find($userId);
        if (!$user) { return $this->fail(401, 'Unknown account'); }
        session_regenerate_id(true);
        Auth::authorize($user);
        \Caligrafy\AuthRoutes::rememberSignIn($pending !== null ? 'face+passkey' : 'passkey');
        return Web::json(['user' => ['username' => $user->username], 'factors' => $pending !== null ? ['face', 'passkey'] : ['passkey']]);
    }
}
```

**4. The client.** Create the app with `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php facedetect facelogin`, then replace its `index.php`,
`css/styles.css` and `scripts/main.js` with the ones of section 5 of the face login recipe,
[`claude-plugin/skills/caligrafy/reference/recipes-face-login.md`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/claude-plugin/skills/caligrafy/reference/recipes-face-login.md#5-client-facedetect-app).
It has a **Sign in** tab (an oval guide with hints such as *Move a little closer*; the liveness check starts by itself
when the face is in the oval, with the prompts on the video) and an **Enrol your face** tab (sign in with a password or
create an account, scan the face, then try it or add a passkey). The browser calls the routes with
`{ headers: apiHeaders() }`.

**Check** (from the command line, before the camera)
- `POST /facelogin/start` with `{"username": "<a user>"}` answers `{"nonce": "<64 hex>", "challenges": [2 of turn-left, turn-right, smile], "expires_in": 60}`.
- `POST /facelogin/login` with a made-up nonce answers `401`, *Unknown or already used challenge: start again*.
- Four identical prints answer `422`, *Identical face prints: they must come from a live camera*; the prints of an
  accepted sign-in sent again with a new nonce answer `401`, *These face prints were already used: replay refused*.

### `Caligrafy\FaceLogin` (static)

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `challenge($username = null, $count = null, $ttl = null)` | `['nonce' => 64 hex, 'challenges' => [...], 'expires_in' => 60]`, kept in the session (a new one replaces the old) |
| `verify($response, $username)` | uses up the nonce, checks the liveness result and the prints; returns the prints (`[[128 numbers], ...]`) or throws `FaceLoginException` (401 nonce, 422 liveness or prints) |
| `match($prints, $enrolled)` | `$enrolled` = `[['user' => id, 'descriptor' => [...]], ...]`; returns `['user', 'distance']` (mean below 0.5, none at 0.6 or more) or `null` |
| `checkPrints($prints)`, `enrolledElsewhere($prints, $enrolled, $user)`, `printHash($descriptor)`, `descriptor($d)`, `distance($a, $b)`, `consume($nonce, $username)` | helpers |
| `CHALLENGES` | `['turn-left', 'turn-right', 'smile']` |
| `$count` 2, `$ttl` 60, `$minPrints` 3, `$maxPrints` 12, `$distinct` 0.001, `$spread` 0.6, `$match` 0.5 | the settings |

### Passkeys

A passkey (WebAuthn) is a key pair kept by the person's device (Touch ID, Windows Hello, Android, a security key or a
password manager) and unlocked with its biometrics or PIN. The private key never leaves the device and a passkey works
only on the domain it was made for: it cannot be phished or replayed. `Caligrafy\Passkey` (on
[lbuchs/webauthn](https://github.com/lbuchs/WebAuthn)) checks them on the server, `PasskeyClient`
(`public/js/services/passkey.js`) runs them in the browser.

**Passkeys alone** (without face sign-in): create the `passkeys` table (the last statement of the SQL above) and add
`'passkeys' => true` to [`Route::auth`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes#auth):

```php
Route::auth(['home' => '/', 'passkeys' => true]);
```

It declares `POST /passkey/register/options`, `/passkey/register` (signed in), `/passkey/login/options` and
`/passkey/login`. With face sign-in, the passkey capabilities above take these routes instead, because they
know whose face was just recognized.

```js
// <script src="<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'passkey.js'; ?>"></script>
const config = { headers: apiHeaders() };   // the session and its X-CSRF-Token
const options = (await axios.post(env.home + 'passkey/register/options', {}, config)).data;
await axios.post(env.home + 'passkey/register', await PasskeyClient.create(options), config);

const login = (await axios.post(env.home + 'passkey/login/options', {}, config)).data;
await axios.post(env.home + 'passkey/login', await PasskeyClient.get(login), config);
```

+ `new Passkey($rpName = APP_NAME, $rpId = PASSKEY_RP_ID or the request host, $origin = PASSKEY_ORIGIN or APP_PROTOCOL://host, $table = 'passkeys')`;
  `registrationOptions($userId, $userName, $displayName = null)`, `register($response, $userId, $name = null)`,
  `authenticationOptions($userId = null)` (null: any passkey of the site), `authenticate($response)` (the user id),
  `remove($userId, $credentialId)`. To store them elsewhere, extend `Passkey` and override `credentials()`,
  `findCredential()`, `saveCredential()` and `touchCredential()`.
+ The challenge of each ceremony is kept in the session, used once, and expires after `$timeout` (120 s).
  `userVerification` and `residentKey` are `required`.
+ In production set `PASSKEY_RP_ID` (the domain, `example.com`) and `PASSKEY_ORIGIN` (`https://www.example.com`) in
  `.env` (they are not in `.env.example`). Passkeys need `https`, except on `localhost`.

| Setup | How | For |
|---|---|---|
| Face only | face sign-in with liveness (`FaceLoginAction::PASSKEY_POLICY = 'face'`) | low-risk apps, as a convenience |
| Face, then passkey | `'step-up'` (the default): accounts with a passkey confirm with it | most apps |
| Passkey only | `'passkey'`: face sign-in refused for accounts with a passkey | administrators, payments, health data |
| Passkey as fallback | the sign-in page always offers a passkey | every setup: the camera can be missing or blocked |

Enrol faces and passkeys only for people who are signed in with a password or a passkey, so that nobody can attach a face
or a passkey to someone else's account. `mayChangeSignIn()` checks it with
[`AuthRoutes::signedInBy()`](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#signedinby) (2.21.3): a session
opened with a face alone cannot replace the face or add a passkey, because a good photo can pass.

### Testing without a camera or a device

+ **A fake camera:** draw a picture on a canvas and give its stream to the page before the detector starts:
  `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia = async () => canvas.captureStream(15);`. `faceprint()` works on it and
  `liveness()` must fail: this is the photo test.
+ **Virtual passkeys:** Chrome DevTools > More tools > WebAuthn > *Enable virtual authenticator environment*, then add
  an authenticator (internal, resident keys, user verification).
## Common mistakes

+ **A detector in Vue `data` without `Vue.markRaw()`.** The detections slow down or stop.
+ **Recognition pictures that differ in number**, or `sampleSize` missing: `sampleSize` 0 loads nothing.
+ **The camera on `http://` with another host than `localhost`.** Browsers allow the camera only on `https` or `localhost`.
+ **Calling a face route with no `X-CSRF-Token`**: `401` `[ERROR 1004]`, signed in or not. Send `apiHeaders()`.
+ **`AuthRoutes::signIn()` in a face capability**: it gives the session a new CSRF token, and the open page's next call is
  refused. The recipe uses `session_regenerate_id(true); Auth::authorize($user);`.
+ **Usernames that are email addresses** ([Signing in with an email](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.1-Authentication#emailsignin)): `facelogin_register` checks its username itself: replace its letters-and-digits test with `filter_var($username, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` and store it in lower case.
+ **A face print as a password.** Use the server challenge, `liveness()`, `FaceLogin::verify()`, and a passkey.
+ **`blink` in the challenges.** It was removed: `liveness()` refuses it.
+ **Both `Route::auth(['passkeys' => true])` and the passkey routes of the face login.** Keep one.
+ **An app folder with a reserved name**: `app`, `bot`, `__bots__`, `css`, `facedetect`, `fonts`, `images`, `js`, `ml`,
  `resources`, `uploads`.
