<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.5-Security-and-Upgrading -->

This page has two parts: the settings an application needs before it goes online, with what the framework protects by
itself, and how to bring an existing project to a new release of Caligrafy Quill (`php caligrafer.php update`).
## With Claude

| You want | Ask |
|---|---|
| to know whether the project is ready for production | `/caligrafy-quill:deploy` (a read-only check: Dockerfile, `composer.lock`, scripts safe to run again, no secrets in git, `APP_DEBUG=false` online) |
| a review of your code for security mistakes | "review my code" (the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent: SQL built from input, CSRF, uploads, exposed secrets...) |
| the latest release | `/caligrafy-quill:update` (or `/caligrafy-quill:update 2.19.0`) |

`/caligrafy-quill:update` runs `php caligrafer.php update --check`, shows you what it changes, runs
`php caligrafer.php update`, merges each `<file>.caligrafy-new` into your version, then runs `version`, `doctor`,
`upgrade --local` and `platform install`, and checks the sign-in flows and the forms. It commits only with your OK.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php version` prints the new version.
+ `find . -name '*.caligrafy-new' -not -path './vendor/*' -not -path './backups/*'` prints nothing.
+ `php caligrafer.php doctor` has no `FAIL`.
+ Sign in, sign out, sign up and one form work from a private window.
## By hand: the production settings

**1. The production `.env`.** Online, the app reads its own `.env` (on Caligrafy Cloud the database settings and keys
are written for you; set the rest with `php caligrafer.php cloud secret set <app> KEY=value`). Give it:

```text
APP_ROOT=
APP_ENV=production
APP_PROTOCOL=https
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_URL=https://bookshelf.example.com
LEGACY_API_KEY=false
DB_ACTIVATE=true
```

and its own `APP_KEY` and `API_KEY`: `php caligrafer.php generatekeys` prints a new pair. Never reuse your computer's
keys, never commit a `.env`.

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| `APP_ENV=production` | the live Stripe keys, Google Analytics, the class map's production checks |
| `APP_DEBUG=false` | errors show no details to visitors, and Phug's debug mode is off: pages about three times faster (2.19.0) |
| `APP_PROTOCOL=https` | the links the app builds start with `https://` |
| `APP_URL` | the links of emails sent by jobs, the return addresses of payments, `og:url` |
| `LEGACY_API_KEY=false` | only personal access tokens open the API (Caligrafy Cloud sets it) |

**2. Leave the speed settings as they are.** They are on by default; each has a setting that turns it off, for when
something breaks:

| On by default | What it does | Turned off by |
|---|---|---|
| the views cache | each Pug view is compiled to PHP once, again only when it or a file it includes changes (2.17.0) | `VIEW_CACHE=false` |
| the Phug Optimizer | a compiled view runs without building Phug's compiler (2.19.0) | `VIEW_OPTIMIZER=false` |
| lazy sessions | a `GET` without a session cookie gets a session only when it needs one (2.19.0) | `SESSION_LAZY=false` |
| the class map | each class of `application/` is loaded when first used (2.18.0) | `CLASS_MAP=false` |
| `.env.php` | the settings are read from `.env.php` instead of parsing `.env` (2.19.0) | `php caligrafer.php env clear` |

**3. Compile `.env`.** With the production image (Caligrafy Cloud, Coolify, Docker), the deploy step does it at every
start: nothing to do. On a server without the image, run after each change to `.env`:

```bash
php caligrafer.php env cache
```
```text
 .env compiled to .env.php: pages read it without parsing .env (php caligrafer.php env clear removes it)
```

`.env.php` is used only while `.env` is exactly what it was compiled from: an edited `.env` is read as it is (slower,
still right) until the next `env cache`. `.gitignore` lists `.env.php`: never commit it.

**4. Check the server.** Run, with your address:

```bash
curl -I https://bookshelf.example.com/.env
curl -I https://bookshelf.example.com/caligrafer.php
```

Both must answer `403` or `404`. Then run `php caligrafer.php doctor` on the server (or `php caligrafer.php doctor
--env .env.production` on your computer): no `FAIL`, Stripe in live mode when the app takes payments.

**Check**

+ `APP_DEBUG=false`, `APP_ENV=production` and keys of their own in the production `.env`.
+ `.env`, `.env.php` and `caligrafer.php` are not served.
+ `git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)\.env($|\.)' | grep -v '\.env\.example$' | grep -v '^framework/settings/'` prints nothing.
## <a name="upgrading"></a>By hand: upgrading an existing project

A project made with the current release has nothing to do. Updating moves the `framework/` folder and the release's
other files to the new version; the `application/` folder, copied from `framework/settings/application` when the
project was made, is **yours**, and `upgrade` brings its untouched files up to date.

The commands run in the Docker server of your project; without Docker, drop `docker compose exec dev-box`.

**1. Start from a clean state.** Run `git status --short`: commit what is there first, so that the update is one change
you can review.

**2. See what changes.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update --check
```

It lists what it would replace, add and keep, the new settings and packages. Up to date, it prints
` Caligrafy Quill 2.21.6 is the latest: nothing to update. php caligrafer.php upgrade checks application/.`

**3. Update.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update            # the latest release
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php update 2.21.6     # or a given one
```

Run it whole (not through `| tail`: it exits with `1` when something did not finish, and its last lines run
`upgrade --apply`). Everything it replaces is copied first to `backups/caligrafy-update-<from>-to-<to>-<time>/`.

**4. Merge every `.caligrafy-new`.** A file you changed is kept, with the release's version next to it:

```bash
find . -name '*.caligrafy-new' -not -path './vendor/*' -not -path './backups/*'
```

For each one, compare (`diff <file> <file>.caligrafy-new`), write the merged result into `<file>` (your changes plus the
release's new lines and fixes), then delete the `.caligrafy-new`.

**5. Check.**

```bash
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php version            # Caligrafy Quill <the new version>
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php platform install   # the framework tables of the new release; safe to run again
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php upgrade --local    # nothing outdated left in application/
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php doctor             # no FAIL
docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php test               # when tests/ has tests
```

Then open the main pages, sign in, sign out and sign up, and send each form from a private window (no session cookie).
Read the release notes of every version you passed
(`https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-<version>`) and do what they ask of projects.

**6. Commit and deploy.** Commit (`Caligrafy Quill <from> to <to>`), push, then `docker compose exec dev-box php caligrafer.php cloud deploy <app>`
(or the deploy of your own server). Delete `backups/` once you are done: git ignores it, the production image leaves
it out, and since 2.19.1 the root `.htaccess` refuses it too.

**Check**

+ `php caligrafer.php version` is the new version, here and online.
+ No `.caligrafy-new` file is left.
+ The sign-in flows and the forms work from a fresh session.

**From 2.24.1 to 2.25.0.** A Snap card no longer shows a whole page (G163): give the main lists and records card views (`/caligrafy-quill:assistant` writes them in `application/views/snap/`; `php caligrafer.php snap views` lists them). Until then those cards are designed from their data. Nothing else changes.

**From 2.24.0 to 2.24.1.** Nothing to change; tests that fake the planner pass again (G162).

**From 2.23.0 to 2.24.0.** Nothing to change: `server` and `quickstart` print the ports of your `docker-compose.override.yml`, and `php caligrafer.php server start` works by hand.

**From 2.22.1 to 2.23.0.** `update` adds `anthropic-ai/sdk` to `composer.json`; run `php caligrafer.php platform install` for Snap's tables (a deploy does it too). Nothing else changes until you add `Route::snap();` ([Snap Cards and the assistant](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Snap-Cards-and-the-Assistant)).

**From 2.22.0 to 2.22.1.** Nothing to change for builds: the new `Dockerfile` runs Composer without plugins. To turn it off for `composer install` on your computer too, set `"nodejs-php-fallback/nodejs-php-fallback": false` in `composer.json` (under `config.allow-plugins`): `update` does not change it for you, because it runs the updater of the release you come from and keeps a value the project already has.

**From 2.21.9 to 2.22.0.** stripe-php 23: only code of your own that calls `Stripe::setAccountId()` or serializes Stripe objects changes (see the [release notes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-2.22.0)).

**From 2.21.8 to 2.21.9.** Nothing to change in a project. `cloud create` no longer needs `--repo` in the `dev-box` when the project has a GitHub `origin`.

**From 2.21.7 to 2.21.8.** A number field now answers 422 to a list or `true`; a token needs a user that exists.

**From 2.21.6 to 2.21.7.** A `GET` route variable is never replaced by the query string, in controllers too; send a value in the query string under another name.

**From 2.21.5 to 2.21.6.** In a client app made earlier, load `app.js` with a version so a deploy reaches every browser:
`<?php echo APP_SERVICE_ROOT.'app.js?v='.@filemtime(PUBLIC_PATH.'js/services/app.js'); ?>`.

**From 2.21.4 to 2.21.5.** Nothing to change: client apps' scripts now carry a version that changes at each deploy.

**From 2.21.3 to 2.21.4.** Nothing to change.

**From 2.21.2 to 2.21.3.** Nothing to change. If you built face sign-in from the recipe, add its `mayChangeSignIn()` check:
without it, a session opened with a face alone (a photo can pass) can replace the enrolled face.

**From 2.21.1 to 2.21.2.** On a `GET`, `Route::action` and `Route::capability` now keep the route variable when the query
string has the same name (`/books/3?id=9` is the book 3). A passkey sign-in follows `Route::auth`'s `level`.

**From 2.21.0 to 2.21.1.** A JSON call to `Route::action` needs the page's `X-CSRF-Token` or an API token, signed in or
not. Nothing to change if your pages send it.

**From 2.20.0 to 2.21.0.** Nothing to change: `Route::action`, web-only capabilities and `Route::bots` are new, and
existing controllers keep working. Moving one is optional:
[Controllers](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/8.-Controllers#controllerstartup).

**From 2.19.8 to 2.20.0.** Nothing to change: new options on `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::redirect`, and
`Route::auth` follows `/login?return=<a page of this site>` after signing in.

**From 2.19.7 to 2.19.8.** The session cookie is `HttpOnly`, and `Secure` on HTTPS (directly or behind a load balancer
that sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`). Nothing to change, unless JavaScript of yours read the session cookie: use
`X-CSRF-Token` and the session instead.

**From 2.19.0 to 2.19.1.** No new tables. `update` replaces an untouched root `.htaccess` (it now refuses `backups/`)
and adds the new `.gitignore` lines (every `.env.*` file but `.env.example`). Vue apps get `env.request` without the
session cookie or the `Authorization` header (`request()->forClient()`). A Vite SPA made before 2.19.1 keeps its own
`src/common/app.js` and `src/main.js`: remove its `VITE_API_KEY`, as
[the SPA pages](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.8.1---Setting-up-the-Vue-application) show.

**From 2.18 to 2.19.** No new tables. Sessions start only when used: a page with a form must print `=csrf()`, and code
that reads `$_SESSION['token']` on a `GET` reads `session('token')`. A model that declares its own `find()` keeps it for
`$book->find()`, but `Book::find()` then fails: use `Book::query()->find()`. Pug errors show their line only with
`APP_DEBUG=true` (set it on your computer). Moving controllers to declared routes is optional.
## <a name="checklist"></a>Reference: the production checklist

+ **Server files are not served.** `curl -I https://<your-host>/.env` answers `403` or `404`. The `.htaccess` files of
  Caligrafy deny dotfiles (`.env`, `.env.php`, `.git`...), the server-side folders and the tooling files, and prevent
  scripts in `public/uploads` from running. Keep them (they need `mod_rewrite` and `AllowOverride FileInfo` or `All`),
  or write the same rules for nginx.
+ **`APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`**, keys of their own (`generatekeys`), no `.env` or `.env.php` in git
  (the `.gitignore` of the project also leaves out `.env.production`, `.env.testing` and every other `.env.*` but
  `.env.example`, 2.19.1).
  Changing the `APP_KEY` revokes every legacy API key and signs every user out.
+ **Personal access tokens, not the API key.** Give each program or agent its own token with the scopes it needs
  (`php caligrafer.php token create`), let browser apps use the session (the JS client, or `apiHeaders()` for `Route::action` and controller
  routes, the session and `X-CSRF-Token` for the Vite SPA template since 2.19.1), then set `LEGACY_API_KEY=false`. The
  `API_KEY` is not a secret in the browser: Caligrafy gives it to the Vue apps it serves (`env.apiKey`, `null` with
  `LEGACY_API_KEY=false`).
+ **AI agents (MCP):** `Route::mcp()` accepts tokens only (a `POST /mcp` without one, session cookie or not, answers
  `401` with `WWW-Authenticate` and a JSON-RPC error, 2.19.1) and shows each agent the capabilities its scopes allow; mark
  capabilities that delete data `destructive: true`, and read `php caligrafer.php audit`.
+ **Administrators:** new users have `permissions` 0; promote administrators in the database.
+ **Queries:** the [query builder](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) binds every value. Elsewhere
  use `?` placeholders (`Database::execute($sql, [$value])`, `all()` with `bindings`); never put request data in SQL.
+ **Uploads:** the `file` rule of a capability (`'cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'`), or
  `uploadFile($file, ['png', 'jpg'])`. Scripts, HTML and SVG files are always refused.
+ **Forms:** every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE` form prints `=csrf()`, `Route::form` and `Route::action` included. Never write
  data in a closure route: use `Route::form`, `Route::action` or a capability route.
+ **Web-only capabilities:** they may read the session, sign people in and change data on a `GET`, so only `Route::action`
  reaches them. A `GET` has no CSRF token: keep what it changes harmless, and use `'method' => 'POST'` and a form for the
  rest. After signing in on a redirect, give a new session id and CSRF token with `AuthRoutes::signIn($user)`; a page that
  stays open at least calls `session_regenerate_id(true)` before `Auth::authorize($user)`. Never trust `{id}` alone to say which row someone may open: check it against the person
  (`$context`).
+ **What a weak sign-in may do:** `AuthRoutes::signedInBy()` says how a session signed in (`password` and `passkey` through
  `Route::auth`; `AuthRoutes::signIn($user, null, 'face')` for your own). A face without a liveness check does not prove a
  person: refuse anything that changes how the account signs in unless it answers `password` or `passkey`.
+ **Sign-in:** `Route::auth` limits failed sign-ins and gives a new session id at sign-in. Behind a proxy every visitor
  has the proxy's address: the limit is then per username.
+ **Webhooks:** `Route::webhook` needs `verify`; with `'stripe'`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is the live endpoint's
  `whsec_...`. The capability refuses other callers and is safe to run twice.
+ **Jobs:** capabilities run by the queue, the scheduler or a webhook have full access: refuse other callers
  (`$context->actorType()`), and check who may ask before pushing a job.
+ **Example routes:** the OpenAI routes of the template call a paid API for anyone who reaches them: protect or remove
  them.
+ **Face login:** never sign in with a single face print; use `FaceLogin::verify()` and a passkey for sensitive accounts,
  with `PASSKEY_RP_ID` and `PASSKEY_ORIGIN` set ([face login](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition#face-login)).
+ **Database changes:** `php caligrafer.php migrate status` shows no `changed` migration; the deploy step runs the
  pending ones.
+ **Health check:** `php caligrafer.php doctor` (or `--env .env.production`): every configured service `OK`, Stripe in
  live mode.

## <a name="protections"></a>Reference: what the framework does for you

| Threat | Protection |
| - | - |
| Downloading `.env`, `.git` or source files | `.htaccess` denies dotfiles, `application`, `framework`, `vendor`, `tests`, `qa`, `docker`, `claude-plugin`, `archives`, `backups` (2.19.1), `node_modules`, `caligrafer.php`, `composer.*`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `package(-lock).json` and `.sql`/`.log`/`.bak`/`.ini`/`.sh`/`.env` files |
| Uploading and running a PHP file | `uploadFile()` and the `file` rule accept an allow-list of extensions; `public/uploads/.htaccess` denies scripts |
| SQL injection | The query builder, `find()`, `create()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `search()`, the relationships and `all()` with `bindings` bind every value; column and table names are checked |
| Cross-site request forgery | Forms must carry the session's `_token` (`=csrf()`); JSON writes with the session need `X-CSRF-Token` (`Route::form`, `Route::auth`, capability routes); every JSON call to `Route::action`, `GET` included, needs it or a token that grants `*` (2.21.1); webhooks have no session: their signature is checked instead |
| Guessing passwords, session fixation | `Route::auth` counts failed sign-ins per username and address (429 after 5 in 15 minutes), answers unknown usernames as slowly as known ones, and gives a new session id and CSRF token at sign-in and sign-out |
| A spreadsheet running a formula from a download | `Route::download` puts `'` before cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` |
| Cross-site scripting through Vue apps | The `env` given to Vue apps is escaped: URL parameters cannot inject code |
| A script of the page reading the session | The session cookie is `HttpOnly`, and `Secure` on HTTPS (2.19.8). `env.request` of a Vue app is `request()->forClient()` (2.19.1): the method, host, address, route, its values and the query string; never the `Cookie` (the session id) or `Authorization` headers, nor a `POST` body |
| A query string replacing a route variable | `Route::page`, `Route::form`, `Route::action` and `Route::capability` keep the route variable: `/books/3?id=9` is the book 3 (2.21.2) |
| Open redirects after signing in | `/login?return=` follows a path of this site only; another site, `//...` or a backslash is ignored |
| A form choosing what only the server should | The `inputs` option of `Route::form` writes those values over anything the form sent |
| A browser-only capability reached by a program or an agent | `webOnly: true`: nothing but `Route::action` reaches it, and it is listed nowhere |
| Loading arbitrary files through client apps | `?app=` and the app folder accept letters, digits, `-` and `_` only, and only files of `public/<app>/` are served |
| A stolen password database | The authentication module stores `password_hash()` hashes |
| Signing in with a photo or a replayed face print | `FaceLogin` issues single-use liveness challenges and refuses identical or reused prints; `Passkey` (WebAuthn) checks a device signature bound to the domain |
| Choosing a secret through a form | The OpenAI example controller accepts only the documented commands and types |

## <a name="update-command"></a>Reference: `php caligrafer.php update`

```bash
php caligrafer.php update --check [<version>]   # what it would change
php caligrafer.php update [<version>] [--yes] [--no-composer]
```

1. `framework/` and `claude-plugin/` are replaced whole.
2. Every other file of the release (`caligrafer.php`, `.bin/`, `Dockerfile`, `index.php`, `public/css`, `public/js`...):
   an untouched copy is replaced, a missing one added, a changed one kept with the new version next to it as
   `<file>.caligrafy-new`. Your documents (`README.md`, `LICENSE`...) are left alone.
3. `composer.json` gets the new packages (then `composer update` for them) and, 2.22.1+, the release's `allow-plugins` the project did not change, `.gitignore` the new lines, `.env` the new
   settings with their defaults (existing values never change).
4. `php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply`, from the new release, brings `application/` up to date.

`application/`, the values of `.env`, `public/uploads` and `vendor/` are never replaced. `upgrade` checks for a newer
release too: when there is one, `upgrade` and `upgrade --apply` do what `update --check` and `update` do. Projects before
2.9.0 have no `update` command: see [Caligrafer: update](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Caligrafer#update).

## <a name="upgrade-command"></a>Reference: `php caligrafer.php upgrade`

```bash
php caligrafer.php upgrade            # dry run: prints the plan, changes nothing
php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply    # applies it
php caligrafer.php upgrade --local    # compares application/ with the templates of the release the project runs
php caligrafer.php upgrade --force application/views/Auth/login.pug          # replaces one customized file
php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply --keep application/views/default/index.pug   # keeps a default page that is now yours
```

Every file of `framework/settings/application` is reported as:

| Status | Meaning | With `--apply` |
| - | - | - |
| `missing` | new in the framework | copied into `application/` |
| `identical` | already up to date | nothing |
| `outdated` | an older template that you never changed | replaced |
| `kept` | an older template that you keep with `--keep` (remembered in the manifest) | **kept**; the new version is written next to it as `<file>.caligrafy-new` |
| `customized` | you changed it | **kept**; the new version is written next to it as `<file>.caligrafy-new` (or replace it with `--force`) |
| `held` | new files that would clash with how your project works (the user capabilities), the files that need them, and `AuthController` or `AdminController` in a project that signs in with `Route::auth` or whose routes no longer name them (2.19.3, 2.19.6, 2.19.7) | **not added**, with the reason; add one with `--force application/<path>` |
| `routes` | `config/routing/web.php` holds your routes | never replaced (except with `--force application/config/routing/web.php`) |

+ Every replaced file is first copied to `backups/caligrafy-upgrade-<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>/`. `.env`, `public/uploads`,
  `vendor` and the files you created in `application/` are never touched.
+ `initialize` and `upgrade --apply` write `application/.caligrafy-manifest.json` (the hash of each template as
  copied): commit it, it is how the next upgrade tells untouched files from yours. Projects without one are compared
  with the templates of the previous releases (`framework/settings/template-history.json`).
+ **Read the `outdated` list before `--apply`.** An untouched default page can be a page of your site: keep it with
  `--keep application/<path>`.
+ The settings of `framework/settings/.env.example` that your `.env` lacks are listed as `new`, obsolete ones as
  `obsolete` with what replaces them. Views and client apps that still use Bootstrap 3 classes are listed.
+ Client apps made with `php caligrafer.php app|bot|facedetect|ml` are listed with the files that differ from
  `framework/plugins/<type>`; they are never changed.
+ **Upgrading to 2.5.0** (the user capabilities): `upgrade --apply` adds `application/services/Users/` and replaces
  `AdminController` and `AuthController` when you never changed them. They are **held** when your `AdminController` is
  customized (set `CaligrafyUsers::ADMIN_LEVEL` to your level, then add the files with `--force`), or when
  `application/` already declares one of those capabilities or class names (rename yours first).
## <a name="changes"></a>Reference: behavior changes

| Area | Before | Now |
| - | - | - |
| `create()`, `update()`, `save()` | `0`, `''` and `false` were silently dropped | They are saved. Only `null` is skipped, and only the columns of the table are written (helper properties of a model are ignored) |
| `all()` | Raw clauses only | Raw clauses plus `bindings` for `?` placeholders |
| `search()` | Keywords inserted in the SQL | Keywords bound. Invalid column names throw an exception |
| `belongsToMany()` | Pivot creation failed with `INT UNSIGNED` ids or with a second pivot | Pivot columns copy the id type and constraint names are unique |
| `DB_PORT` | Ignored | Used, unless `DB_HOST` contains `;port=` |
| `session()`, `scripts()`, `keywords()`, `copyright()`, `metadata()` | Ignored `0`, `''` and `false` | Store them |
| `endWith()` | Only compared the last character | Compares the whole needle |
| `httpRequest()` | Only sent a body for `POST` | Sends it for every method except `GET` |
| `uploadFile()` | Accepted any extension | Allow-list (`DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXTENSIONS` or your own list) |
| CSRF | An empty `APPROVED_AGENTS` approved requests without a User-Agent | Empty entries are ignored |
| `Payment::createCheckout()` | Crashed with a locale or a customer email | Works |
| `OpenAI` `COMPLETE` | Dropped the text after `[insert]` | Sends it |
| `GPT4OMINI`, `ASSISTANT_GPT4OMINI` | `gpt-4o mini` (invalid) | `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `Assistant::run()` | Always sent an empty model and no tools, disabling `file_search` | Only sends the overrides that are given |
| `Assistant::retrieveResponse()` | Could wait forever | Gives up after `$timeout` seconds (120) |
| `caligrafer initialize` | Generated new keys on every run | Keeps the keys of a signed project |
| Authentication | Reversible passcodes, any user could manage users | Hashed passwords (8 to 72 characters), administrators need `permissions >= 1` |
| `APP_DEBUG=false` | Still turned the SMTP debug output on (`.env` values are strings) | Parsed as a boolean |
| Bot app | Loaded the latest Vue from a CDN | Pinned Vue 2.7.16; since the library upgrade, a Vue 3 chat on `scripts('vue')` (Vue 3.5.44) |
| Error responses | HTTP `200` for every error, including PHP fatal errors, with `[ERROR ...]` text | Real status codes: `401` (1004, access denied: since 2.7.0 the message ends with the reason), `403` (3000, CSRF), `404` (1001, controller or action), `405` (1000: the address answers other methods, with an `Allow` header, 2.16.0), `500` (other errors; for PHP fatal errors and uncaught exceptions the message is only shown with `APP_DEBUG=true`). API calls get `{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}}`. **Clients that expected `200` on errors must check the status** (axios and `fetch().ok` now treat them as failures) |
| Controller names | The example controllers of `application/controllers/core/` were global classes: a controller of yours named `AIController`, `AdminController`, `AuthController`, `ClientController` or `WatsonController` was a fatal error (`Cannot redeclare class`) on every page | They are in `Caligrafy\Controllers`. Routes accept fully qualified controllers (`'Shop\OrderController@show'`, leading `\` allowed); a short name that is not a declared class falls back to `Caligrafy\Controllers`, so old routes keep working and your own class of the same name wins. If your code referenced an example class directly (`new AuthController()`, `extends AIController`), use `Caligrafy\Controllers\...` |
| Relationships with namespaced models | The default foreign key of `hasOne`, `hasMany`, `belongsToMany` included the namespace | Uses the short class name (`Shop\Order` gives `order_id`) |
| Client apps (`?app=`) | Any path, including sub-folders and `../` | A file name of `public/<app>/` only (letters, digits, `-`, `_`): no sub-folders, no symbolic links pointing outside the app |
| Pug views (2.17.0) | Compiled on every request | Compiled once and kept in a private folder of the temporary directory, again when a view or a file it includes changes (`VIEW_CACHE=false` turns it off) |
| Classes of `application/` (2.18.0) | Every PHP file loaded on the first unknown class of each request | Each class loaded when first used, from a class map; a file with functions or top-level code is still loaded at start (`CLASS_MAP=false` restores the old way) |
| `tests/` (2.18.0) | Every PHP file loaded on each request | Your app's PHPUnit tests (`php caligrafer.php test`), never loaded on a page |
| Capabilities (2.18.0) | Built with `new` | Built by the container: their constructors get what they ask for (`application/config/container.php`) |
| Sessions (2.19.0) | Started on every request | Started when used. A request with a session cookie, and every `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE`, starts it as before. A `GET` or `HEAD` without one (a first visit, an API client, an agent) gets a session only when it reads the CSRF token (`session('token')`, `csrf()`), writes the session after `config.php`, or prints a page that carries the token. Code that reads `$_SESSION['token']` directly on such a request should call `session('token')`. `SESSION_LAZY=false` starts every session, as before |
| Pug debug mode (2.19.0) | Always on | Only with `APP_DEBUG=true` (Pug line numbers in errors); cached views run through Phug's Optimizer (`VIEW_OPTIMIZER=false` turns it off) |
| Output buffer (2.19.0) | 1 MB reserved for every request | Grows with the page; errors still get their status code |
| Database rows (2.19.0) | Encoded to JSON and back (a row with invalid UTF-8 became `null`) | Fetched as arrays: the same arrays, faster, and such a row is kept |
| `Model::find()` (2.19.0) | A declared method | Provided through `__call()` (`$book->find(1)`, as before) and `__callStatic()` (`Book::find(1)`, the query builder). A model that declares its own `find()` keeps it for instances, but `Book::find()` then fails: use `Book::query()->find(1)`. `method_exists($model, 'find')` is now `false` |
| `.env` (2.19.0) | Parsed on every request | Read from `.env.php` when the deploy step or `php caligrafer.php env cache` compiled it and `.env` has not changed since (`env clear` removes it) |
| `Auth::logout()`, `terminateSession()` (2.19.0) | Always touched the session | Only when one is active |
## <a name="libraries"></a>Reference: upgrading to the current libraries (October 2026)

This release moves Caligrafy to current versions of every library and service. As with the security fixes, **new projects get everything automatically**; existing projects follow the steps below. The [Release notes: October 2026](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Release-notes:-October-2026) give the same steps as a checklist, with every other change of October 2026.

**1. Requirements:** PHP 8.3 or higher (the Docker image uses PHP 8.5), MySQL 8.4, Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ for the Vue SPA template. Run `composer update` after pulling the framework.

**2. `.env`:** add the new settings when you use the matching module (see `framework/settings/.env.example`):

| Setting | Module |
| - | - |
| `COINBASE_API_KEY_NAME`, `COINBASE_API_KEY_SECRET` (replace `CRYPTO_PAY_KEY`) | Crypto payments (Coinbase Business) |
| `WATSON_URL` (required), `WATSON_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `WATSON_API_VERSION` | Watson bots |
| `OPEN_AI_MODEL`, `OPEN_AI_IMAGE_MODEL` (optional) | OpenAI and Assistants |
| `GROQ_MODEL`, `GROQ_VISION_MODEL` (optional) | Groq agents |
| `PWA_SERVICE_WORKER` (optional, `false` by default) | Offline page of installed apps ([Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)) |
| `PASSKEY_RP_ID`, `PASSKEY_ORIGIN` (in production; not in `.env.example`, the request host is used without them) | Passkeys ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.2-Face-Detection-and-Face-Recognition#passkeys)) |
| `AGENT_PROVIDER`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY`, `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `AGENT_API_KEY`, `AGENT_API_BASE`, `AGENT_MODEL`, `AGENT_VISION_MODEL` (optional) | Open source agents on another provider than Groq ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.6-Open-Source-Agents-(llama,-Mistral-etc.))) |

**3. Views (Bootstrap 5):** the layout now loads Bootstrap 5.3 instead of Bootstrap 3.3.7, and no jQuery. Copy the new views of `framework/settings/application/views` (at least `default/master/layoutblocks.pug`, `default/modules/messaging.pug`, `default/modules/cryptopayment.pug`, `default/pages/payment.pug`, `default/pages/checkout.pug` and the `Auth` views) and delete `default/modules/gestures.pug`. Replace `default/modules/install.pug` (add-to-homescreen) with the new one and add `default/modules/serviceworker.pug` (`php caligrafer.php upgrade --apply` does both when you never changed them). If you customized `layoutblocks.pug`, add `meta(name='theme-color', content='#ffffff')` and `link(rel='manifest', href="{$home}public/manifest.webmanifest")` to the headers, and `include ../modules/serviceworker` then `if $install` / `include ../modules/install` after `include ../modules/standalone` (see [install to home screen](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)). If you customized the root `.htaccess`, copy its `Service-Worker-Allowed` lines and the `AddType application/manifest+json .webmanifest` block. Update `public/css/theme.css` too: its end keeps the Caligrafy black and white look on Bootstrap 5 (14px text, cards, black `btn-primary`, white `btn-secondary` with black text, black focus rings, readable `a.btn` links). It also keeps the Bootstrap 3 layout: full-width page container, header title centered in the header, grids centered in their wrapper, Caligrafy card borders and colors, Bootstrap 3 text color and button metrics. If you customized `theme.css`, copy everything from the "Bootstrap 5 compatibility layer" comment to the end of the file. Its heading margins apply to `body.caligrafy-layout` (and `body#gesturize`, so older copies of `default/master/layout.pug` keep their look): add `class='caligrafy-layout'` to the body of your own layouts. Client apps that reuse the Caligrafy header can replace a custom `margin: 20px 0 10px` on the header title with the class `caligrafy-header` on the header. In your own views, wrap Bootstrap columns in a `.row` and move them one breakpoint up (`col-sm-6` becomes `col-md-6`, `col-md-4` becomes `col-lg-4`, see [Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views)). Single page apps created before October 2026 load Bootstrap 3 and jQuery from their `index.html`: replace those three tags with `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css` and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js` and update the columns of their components the same way. To keep Bootstrap 3 in a project for now, add to `application/config/config.php`:
```php
scripts('bootstrap_css', 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@3.4.1/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css');
scripts('bootstrap_script', 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@3.4.1/dist/js/bootstrap.min.js');
scripts('bootstrap_jquery', 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jquery@3.7.1/dist/jquery.min.js');
```

**4. Client apps in `public/`:** apps created with Caligrafer are copies. Update their markup to `scripts('vue')` and `scripts('axios')` (pinned versions), and re-create or compare the bot, FaceDetect and ML apps with `framework/plugins`. The shared services (`public/js/services/detect.js`, `mlcore.js`, `face-api.min.js`, `stripe_client.js`, `passkey.js`) and the models in `public/resources/models` are updated with the framework.

**5. Code that calls the changed APIs:** see the table below.

| Area | Before | Now |
| - | - | - |
| PHP | 7.2+ | 8.3+; deprecation notices are never printed into pages |
| Composer | `dev-master` branches | Stable releases: stripe-php 22, Phug 2, Pug-php 3.6, PHPMailer 7, phpdotenv 5.8, GUMP 2.3, SimpleImage 4.4, groq-php 1.4, lbuchs/webauthn 2.2 (passkeys); PHPUnit 12 for the unit tests (development) |
| Bootstrap / jQuery | Bootstrap 3.3.7 + jQuery 1.12 | Bootstrap 5.3.8, no jQuery (jQuery 4 only for Summernote) |
| Add to home screen | add-to-homescreen.js 3.2.3 (`$install`, `add_to_home` scripts keys) | Web app manifest `public/manifest.webmanifest` linked by the layout, `'install' => true` shows an Install button (`beforeinstallprompt`) or the iOS Share hint, optional offline service worker `PWA_SERVICE_WORKER=true` ([Views](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/7.-Views#install)) |
| Hammer.js gestures | Included in the layout | Removed |
| OpenAI text | `gpt-3.5-turbo` (shut down) with temperature/max_tokens defaults | `gpt-6-luna`, only the model is sent by default |
| OpenAI images | DALL.E (shut down), URLs | `gpt-image-2`, base64 in `b64_json` |
| `Assistant` | Assistants API (shut down Aug 26, 2026) | Responses + Conversations APIs, same methods, vector stores for files ([details](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.5-Open-AI:-Assistants#migrating)) |
| Stripe Checkout | `sessionId` + `redirectToCheckout` (removed) | Redirect to `$result['url']` |
| Stripe card form | Card Element | Payment Element (`stripe.confirmPayment`) |
| `createCheckout()` | `payment_method_types` = `['card']` | Payment methods from the Stripe dashboard (current API versions reject the parameter) |
| `CryptoPayment` | Coinbase Commerce (shut down Mar 31, 2026) | Coinbase Business Checkouts with CDP keys; `$transaction['url']` |
| Groq `Agent` | Llama 3.x defaults (retired), Groq only | `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` (vision), `whisper-large-v3`; `AGENT_PROVIDER` selects Together AI, Fireworks AI, OpenRouter (Llama), Ollama (local Llama) or a custom endpoint; `configure()` parameters are now sent ([migrating from the Groq Llama models](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/9.9.6-Open-Source-Agents-(llama,-Mistral-etc.)#migrating)) |
| Watson | URL of a fixed instance, version 2021-11-27 | `WATSON_URL`, optional environment, version 2024-08-25 |
| Bot client | BotUI + Vue 2 | Vue 3 chat; `pause` actions call `window.executeBotAction(context)` |
| FaceDetect | face-api.js 0.22 (abandoned) | @vladmandic/face-api 1.7.15; MTCNN removed; `detector.ready` promise; `{ autoStart: false }` + `startStream()` (rejects with camera errors, `streamError`), `stopStream()`, `faceprint()` |
| ML Core | ml5 0.12 (poseNet, uNet) + p5 0.9 | ml5 1.4 (bodyPose, bodySegmentation) + p5 2.3; callbacks receive `(results, error)`; the previous pose shape is kept |
| Vue SPA template | Vite 7, Vuex, ESLint 9 legacy config | Vite 8, Vue Router 5, Pinia, ESLint 10 flat config |
| Docker | php:8.2.2, mysql:latest, phpmyadmin:latest | php:8.5-apache, mysql:8.4, phpmyadmin:5.2.3 |
## <a name="qa"></a>Testing the framework

> Contributors: [Testing Caligrafy](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Caligrafy) explains every phase of the QA suite, the unit tests, how to add a test and the release process.

Caligrafy comes with a QA suite that runs the framework, HTTP and tooling tests in an isolated Docker stack (the first free ports from 8090 and 3316, so it never clashes with your development servers). From a clean checkout of the framework:
```bash
composer install
./qa/run.sh
```
The suite refuses to run when an `application` folder or a `.env` file that it did not create is present. Its stack includes stripe-mock, and the OpenAI, Coinbase, Groq and Watson integrations are tested against local mock servers, so no API key is needed.

If the Docker image cannot be built on your network (see the Docker troubleshooting below), build or obtain the `quillqa-web` image once and run the suite with `QA_NO_BUILD=1 ./qa/run.sh`: it reuses the existing image instead of rebuilding it.

The suite also runs the PHPUnit unit tests of the framework core (`qa/unit`: routing, errors, requests, models, validation, upgrade and doctor helpers, face login checks and passkeys, capabilities, tokens, deploy, the scheduler, the view cache, the class map, migrations, the container, the cache, the query builder, lazy sessions and the declarative routes). They need no web server, database or `.env`, so you can run them on their own with the development dependencies installed:
```bash
composer install
vendor/bin/phpunit
```

**`.env` comments:** write comments on their own line (`# ...`). Some tools and the QA suite read `.env` with PHP's `parse_ini_file`, which fails on text after `true`/`false` (`FLAG=false # comment`) and on parentheses in unquoted values; the QA tooling phase checks the templates.

**Docker image build killed during `apt-get` on slow or proxied networks:** on some corporate networks `apt-get install` in `docker/Dockerfile` grows to several GB while it retries slow downloads and the build fails with "Killed" / "cannot allocate memory". Give Docker Desktop more memory (Settings, Resources), close other containers and retry, or build on another network; for the QA suite, reuse an existing image with `QA_NO_BUILD=1`.
## Other ways

### The manual upgrade

Without `update` (a project you cannot run it in), the steps it does by hand:

**1. Update the framework**
```bash
git pull   # or: composer update / download the new release
```

**2. Copy the root and uploads `.htaccess` files** from the new release (keep your own additions). Then check that `.env` is no longer served: `curl -I http://<your-host>/.env`.

**3. Update the files of your `application` folder** that you have not customized, from `framework/settings/application` (`php caligrafer.php upgrade` does this step for you):

| File | Why |
| - | - |
| `views/Client/app.pug` | Path traversal through `?app=` and script injection through URL parameters (**required** if you use Vue, bot, FaceDetect or ML apps) |
| `controllers/core/AI/ClientController.php` | Validates the `?app=` parameter |
| `controllers/core/AI/AIController.php` | The previous version let a form select any PHP constant, including your `.env` secrets (**required** if the `/ai` routes are enabled) |
| `controllers/core/Auth/AuthController.php` and `AdminController.php` | Password hashing, exact username lookup (the previous login accepted `%` as a username), admin pages restricted to `permissions >= 1` |
| `models/Auth/User.php` | `findByUsername()`, `hashPassword()`, `verifyPassword()`, `needsRehash()` used by the controllers above |
| `views/Auth/login.pug`, `register.pug`, `manageusers.pug` | Passwords of up to 72 characters |
| `models/Auth/create_db.sql` | No longer drops the `users` table |
| `controllers/core/AI/*.php`, `controllers/core/Auth/*.php` | The example controllers are declared in the `Caligrafy\Controllers` namespace, so a controller of yours with the same name (`AIController`...) no longer collides with them. Your routes do not need to change: short names such as `'ClientController'` fall back to `Caligrafy\Controllers` |
| `config/routing/web.php` | The `catch` at the end calls `Errors::handle($e);` instead of `echo $e->getMessage();` (add `use Caligrafy\Errors;`), so API clients get JSON errors. Without this change the framework errors (401, 403, 404) still get their status code, but other exceptions (database errors, your own) still answer `200`, and every body stays plain text |

If you customized these files, apply the same changes to your versions: compare them with the new files of `framework/settings/application`.

**4. Upgrade the `users` table** (authentication module):
```sql
ALTER TABLE users MODIFY passcode varchar(255) NOT NULL;
```
Since 2.18.0, put such a change in a [migration](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Migrations) (`php caligrafer.php migrate make users_passcode_255`) so that every server gets it.
Existing users keep logging in with their passwords: their passcode is converted to a hash on their next login. Keep the same `APP_KEY` until they have all logged in once.

**5. Promote your administrators**: `UPDATE users SET permissions = 1 WHERE username = '...';`

**6. Review the [behavior changes](#changes)** in your own code.
## Common mistakes

+ **Pages are slow online.** `APP_DEBUG=true`: Phug's debug mode makes every page about three times slower.
+ **A setting changed on your own server is ignored.** It is not: an edited `.env` is read as it is until the next
  `php caligrafer.php env cache`. A value that still looks old comes from a `.env.php` compiled from another `.env`:
  run `env cache` again, or `env clear`.
+ **`.env.php` in git.** It holds every secret of `.env`: remove it from git, change the keys, and keep the
  `.gitignore` line.
+ **A form answers `[ERROR 3000]` after the update to 2.19.** Its page does not print `=csrf()`, or code reads
  `$_SESSION['token']` before the session started: use `session('token')`. `SESSION_LAZY=false` brings the old sessions
  back while you fix it.
+ **`update` piped into `tail`.** The pipe hides its exit code and its last lines (`upgrade --apply`): run it whole.
+ **`.caligrafy-new` files committed.** Merge them into your files and delete them before committing.
+ **`backups/` online.** It can hold views and SQL scripts. Before 2.19.1 the root `.htaccess` did not refuse it: take
  the 2.19.1 `.htaccess` (`backups` in its folder rule), delete the folder, or keep it out of the server (the
  production image leaves it out).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Caligrafy -->

This page is for contributors to Caligrafy Quill: how the framework is tested, how to run all or part of the tests, how to add a test, and how a release is prepared. You do not need any of it to build an application with Caligrafy. How the framework itself is built (the request lifecycle, capabilities, the `Context`, the design decisions) is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/master/ARCHITECTURE.md).

Run every command from the root of a **clean checkout of the framework** (`git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.git`), not from one of your projects.
## <a name="overview"></a>Two kinds of tests

| | Unit tests | QA suite |
| - | - | - |
| Where | `qa/unit` | `qa/run.sh`, `qa/tests`, `qa/fixtures` |
| What | The core classes, one at a time | The whole framework: database, HTTP requests through Apache, Caligrafer, client apps, the Claude plugin |
| Needs | PHP 8.3+ and `composer install` | Docker, PHP with curl on the host, Node.js and `composer install` |
| Time | A few seconds (333 tests) | Several minutes (the first run builds a Docker image) |
| Command | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | `./qa/run.sh` |

Run the unit tests while you work, and the QA suite before you open a pull request. When you change `framework/` or `framework/settings/application`, add a test for the change.
## <a name="qa"></a>The QA suite

```bash
composer install
./qa/run.sh            # builds the stack, runs every phase, removes everything
./qa/run.sh --keep     # leaves the stack and the generated files in place, for debugging
```

`qa/run.sh` starts its own Docker stack (`qa/docker-compose.yml`, compose project `quillqa`): the web server built from `docker/Dockerfile` (stage `dev-php`, with the checkout mounted into it) on the first free port from `8090`, MySQL 8.4 on the first free port from `3316`, and Stripe's official mock (`stripe/stripe-mock`). The ports never clash with your development server (`8080`, `3306`); set them with `QA_WEB_PORT` and `QA_DB_PORT`. No API key is needed: OpenAI, Groq and the other Agent providers, Coinbase, Watson and SMTP are replaced by small mock servers from `qa/fixtures`.

Before the phases, it generates what a project needs and removes it at the end: a `.env` from `framework/settings/.env.example` (marked `# QA-GENERATED`, with `DB_HOST=mysql` and the database `quillqa`), an `application` folder copied from the templates (marked with `application/.qa-generated`) plus the fixtures of `qa/fixtures/application` and `qa/fixtures/facelogin`, the QA routes added to `web.php` (with every commented route of the template turned on, and the 2.19 declarative routes), the client apps `public/qaapp`, `public/qabot`, `public/qafacedetect` and `public/qafacelogin`, and the tables of `models/Auth/create_db.sql`, `qa/fixtures/books.sql`, the face login fixture and `platform install`. Inside the web container it also serves the Watson mock (port `8769`) and the push service mock (port `8770`).

> **The suite refuses to run** when an `application` folder or a `.env` file that it did not create is present: move them aside or use a clean checkout. Note that every Caligrafer command except `version` and `doctor` creates `.env` from the template when it is missing: delete that copy before you run the suite.

### Phases

| Phase | Runs | Covers |
| - | - | - |
| Database scripts | `mysql` in the `mysql` container | `models/Auth/create_db.sql` can be run again without deleting users; `platform install` can be run again |
| Framework tests | `qa/tests/cli_tests.php` in the web container | Models (CRUD with falsy values, SQL injection, relationships and pivots), validation, the database connection, helpers, OpenAI request building, the Assistant on the Responses and Conversations APIs, Stripe against stripe-mock, Coinbase Business with real JWT signatures, the Groq Agent and the other Agent providers, Watson |
| Unit tests | `vendor/bin/phpunit --colors=never --do-not-cache-result` in the web container | The PHPUnit tests of `qa/unit` (see [below](#unit)) |
| HTTP tests | `qa/tests/http_tests.php` on the host, against `http://localhost:8090` (or the next free port) | The front controller, the web app manifest and service worker, server files that must not be served, client apps (`?app=`), CSRF and API access, the REST API example of the wiki, uploads, the authentication module, the AI controller, face login with liveness and passkeys, the [declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes) (2.19.0: `Route::auth`, `Route::form`, file inputs, `Route::webhook`, `Route::download`; 2.19.1: the `POST /logout` form), MCP without a token (`401`, 2.19.1), `backups/` denied (2.19.1), HTTP status codes |
| Doctor tests | `qa/tests/doctor_tests.sh` | `php caligrafer.php doctor` against the mocks: good and wrong keys, unknown models, leading spaces, DNS errors, Agent providers, masked secrets |
| FileInfo hosts | `qa/run.sh` itself | The `.htaccess` rules on a host that only allows `AllowOverride FileInfo`: pages still load, server files and uploaded scripts answer `403`, `sw.js` keeps `Service-Worker-Allowed` and the manifest its type |
| Tooling tests | `qa/tests/tooling_tests.sh` on the host | `php -l` on the framework, `caligrafer initialize` and `upgrade` on an older project, the client app scaffolds, the liveness logic (`node qa/tests/liveness_tests.js`), front-end libraries (pinned and reachable CDN URLs, no jQuery, no Bootstrap 3), the Bootstrap 5 compatibility layer of `theme.css`, `.env` templates, the web app manifest, the Vue SPA template (build, ESLint, `npm audit`; since 2.19.1 relative paths, hash history, no API key in the bundle, `dist/` kept in git), the project's `.gitignore` (every `.env.*` but `.env.example`) and `migrate --env <file>` (2.19.1), the Claude plugin |

The suite exits with `0` when every phase passes. Each check prints `PASS` or `FAIL` with the reason.

### Running part of the suite

| To run | Command |
| - | - |
| The unit tests only | `vendor/bin/phpunit` (no Docker) |
| The tooling tests only | `sh qa/tests/tooling_tests.sh` (no Docker; add `QA_SKIP_SPA=1` to skip the Vue SPA build, which needs npm and the network). It ends with `<n> passed, <n> failed` |
| The liveness and passkey client tests | `node qa/tests/liveness_tests.js` |
| A phase that needs the stack | `./qa/run.sh --keep` once, then for example `docker compose -f qa/docker-compose.yml exec -T web php qa/tests/cli_tests.php` or `php qa/tests/http_tests.php`; clean up with `docker compose -f qa/docker-compose.yml down -v` and remove the generated files |

### Options

| Variable | Effect |
| - | - |
| `QA_WIKI=<wiki clone>` | The tooling phase also checks that the wiki mirrors of the Claude plugin are up to date with that clone (`sync-wiki.py --check`). Without it, the check is skipped |
| `QA_NO_BUILD=1` | Reuses the existing `quillqa-web` image instead of rebuilding it. Use it on networks where the image build fails |
| `QA_SKIP_SPA=1` | Skips the Vue SPA build of the tooling phase |
| `QA_WEB_PORT`, `QA_DB_PORT` | Ports of the stack (default: the first free ports from `8090` and `3316`) |

The tooling phase runs `claude plugin validate` only when the `claude` command is installed, and then also checks that Claude Code runs the plugin version of the checkout.

For example, before a release:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.wiki.git ../caligrafy-quill.wiki
QA_WIKI=../caligrafy-quill.wiki ./qa/run.sh
```

### One stack at a time

The stack always has the same compose project name (`quillqa`) and ports, and the suite writes `.env`, `application` and the `public/qa*` apps into the checkout. Two runs at the same time, even from two checkouts, share the same containers: one run tears down the stack of the other. Check that no QA stack is running before you start one:
```bash
docker ps --filter name=quillqa
```

### When the image cannot be built

On some slow or proxied networks, `apt-get install` in `docker/Dockerfile` grows to several GB while it retries and the build is killed ("Killed", "cannot allocate memory"). Give Docker more memory, close other containers, or build on another network. Once a `quillqa-web` image exists, run the suite with `QA_NO_BUILD=1 ./qa/run.sh`.
### <a name="buildonce"></a>Build once: the cross-channel tests
The HTTP phase proves that one capability behaves the same on every channel, with the Bookshelf capabilities of `qa/fixtures/application/services/Books`: a book created on a web page (`BookPageController`, `Controller::call()`) is the same through REST (`Route::capability`), the generic endpoint, MCP over HTTP and stdio, and the generated JS client run in Node; invalid input gets the same field errors everywhere; a token without the scope, or an owner without the level, is refused on REST and MCP alike; and the audit log names each channel. Tokens are created with `php caligrafer.php token create` inside the web container, like a user would.

## <a name="unit"></a>Unit tests (PHPUnit)

```bash
composer install                               # installs PHPUnit 12 (require-dev)
vendor/bin/phpunit                             # every test of qa/unit
vendor/bin/phpunit qa/unit/RouteTest.php       # one file
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter testBase64Url      # one test
```

The configuration is `phpunit.xml.dist`: test suite `unit` (the folder `qa/unit`), bootstrap `qa/unit/bootstrap.php`, and warnings or risky tests make the run fail.

### What each test file covers

| File | Covers |
| - | - |
| `RouteTest.php` | `Route::resolveController()`: a global class wins over the example namespace, namespaced controllers with or without a leading backslash, short names that fall back to `Caligrafy\Controllers`, unknown controllers |
| `ErrorsTest.php` | `Errors::status()` (404, 401, 403, 500), `Errors::raise()`, the JSON error body for API requests and the plain text for HTML requests |
| `RequestTest.php` | `Request::wantsJson()`, the API key check (`authorizeApiRequest()`) with valid, invalid and missing keys, the session check (`authorizeSessionRequest()`, the `X-CSRF-Token` header) and the reason of a refusal (`apiRefusal()`); `forClient()`, the `env.request` of client apps without the `Cookie`, the `Authorization` header or a `POST` body (2.19.1) |
| `ModelTest.php` | `prepareInputs()` keeps `0`, `''` and `false` and drops `null` and restricted properties; identifier quoting accepts safe names and rejects unsafe ones |
| `ControllerTest.php` | `validate()` and `filter()` (GUMP) |
| `UpgraderTest.php` | `caligrafer upgrade` in a temporary project: the classification of files, the template history, `--apply` only replaces untouched files and never touches `.env` |
| `DoctorTest.php` | `Doctor::mask()` and the key format checks (leading space, missing dash after the prefix) |
| `DoctorWebAppTest.php` | The install to home screen check of doctor: the framework manifest, missing or invalid manifests, missing icons, required sizes and fields, the service worker check only when `PWA_SERVICE_WORKER` is on |
| `AgentTest.php` | `Agent::settings()`: Groq is the default, the `GROQ_*` and `AGENT_*` settings, key precedence, the defaults of every provider, Ollama without a key, unknown providers |
| `FaceLoginTest.php` | `FaceLogin`: random challenges kept in the session, a nonce accepted once (even when the check fails), expiry, wrong nonce or account, challenge order, identical prints, prints of different faces, print format and count, account matching, print hashes |
| `PasskeyTest.php` | `Passkey` against a software authenticator: registration options, register and authenticate, excluded credentials, replayed assertions, single-use challenges, wrong origin, bad signature, sign counter going back, another user's passkey, user verification, relying party |
| `CapabilitiesTest.php` | The registry of capabilities: attributes, checks of scope and level, validation, the audit, `Capabilities::call()` |
| `ContextTest.php` | `Context`: the CLI, guests, users, tokens and system contexts, scopes and levels |
| `TokensTest.php` | Personal access tokens: format, hashing, scopes, expiry, revocation |
| `ClientTest.php`, `McpServerTest.php` | The generated JS client, and the MCP server (tools listed by scope, calls and errors; a `POST` without a token gets the JSON-RPC `401`, not the CSRF error, 2.19.1) |
| `DeployerTest.php` | `php caligrafer.php deploy`: which `create_db.sql` scripts run, the destructive ones never twice |
| `SchedulerTest.php` | Scheduled jobs: the declaration of `schedule.php`, cron, the listing Caligrafy Cloud reads |
| `NotifyTest.php` | Notifications without a database: message rules, channels, keys, the signed unsubscribe link |
| `CloudClientTest.php`, `UpdaterTest.php`, `QuickstartTest.php`, `PluginSourceTest.php`, `VersionTest.php`, `DesignsTest.php` | The `cloud`, `update`, `quickstart`, `plugin`, `version` and `design` commands |
| `DoctorFormsTest.php`, `DoctorPugTest.php` | Doctor's checks of forms without a method and of two Pug mistakes |
| `ViewTest.php` | The compiled view cache (2.17.0): a private folder, an edited view compiled again |
| `ClassMapTest.php` | The class map (2.18.0): declarations found, classes loaded when used, files that run at start, a new class found at once |
| `MigrationsTest.php` | Migrations (2.18.0): how a script is split, the order and names of the files, `make` |
| `ContainerTest.php` | The container (2.18.0): constructor injection, bindings, singletons, instances, clear errors |
| `CacheTest.php` | The cache (2.18.0): the default store, JSON values, expiry, `remember`, `off` |
| `ValidatorRulesTest.php` | The `exists`, `unique` and `current_year` rules (2.19.0): the ignored row of `unique`, names checked like the query builder, the app's own message, their use in services, a schema rule without its argument |
| `TestCaseTest.php` | `Caligrafy\Testing\TestCase`: each test starts without the queries of earlier tests (no N+1 warning carried over) |
| `QueryTest.php`, `QueryModelTest.php`, `QueryEagerTest.php`, `DatabaseQueryTest.php` | [Queries](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Queries) (2.19.0): the SQL and bindings of the query builder, validated names, writes without a `where`, `Book::query()` and the model forms, eager loading (`with`, `withCount`, pivots), and on an in-memory SQLite the transactions and the N+1 warning. `php qa/bench-query.php` (not part of the run) times 10,000 queries |
| `SessionLazyTest.php` | Sessions only when used (2.19.0): what starts a session, and when a request without a session cookie saves one |
| `FormRouteTest.php`, `UploadsTest.php`, `AuthRoutesTest.php`, `WebhookTest.php`, `DownloadTest.php` | The [declarative routes](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Declarative-Routes) (2.19.0): `Route::form` (redirects, errors, old input, flash), the `file` rule (`required_file` and `required\|file` refuse a missing file, 2.19.1), `Route::auth` (sign-in, lock, session regeneration, the `POST /logout` form, 2.19.1), `Route::webhook` (signatures), `Route::download` (CSV, file names) |

### How the bootstrap loads the framework

The unit tests run without a web server, a database or a `.env`. `qa/unit/bootstrap.php` does only what the tested classes need:

1. defines a test `APP_KEY` (constant and environment variable),
2. requires `vendor/autoload.php` and `framework/helpers/corehelpers.php`,
3. requires the core classes and interfaces under test one by one (the list is in `qa/unit/bootstrap.php`: `Errors`, `Route`, `Request`, `Model`... `ClassMap`, `View`, `Migrations`, `Container`, `Cache`, `Query`, `Form`, `Uploads`, `AuthRoutes`, `Webhook`, `Download`..., `Rest`, `Mcp/Server`, `Mcp/Http`, `Client` and `framework/database/Database.php`, with `DB_ACTIVATE=false`: the query tests give `Database::useConnection()` an in-memory SQLite),
4. requires the fixtures of `qa/unit/fixtures`: test controllers in the global, `Shop` and `Caligrafy\Controllers` namespaces, `QaSoftAuthenticator`, a software WebAuthn authenticator (EC P-256, "none" attestation) also used by the HTTP tests, the test capabilities of `services.php`, and `query.php` (an executor that records the queries of the query builder, and test models).

It never calls `Framework::init()`: no route is dispatched. Classes whose constructor needs the live request or the database are built without their constructor (`ReflectionClass::newInstanceWithoutConstructor()`), and the tests set the properties they need. `Passkey` keeps its credentials in memory by overriding its 4 storage methods. Tests that need files (`UpgraderTest`, `DoctorWebAppTest`) create a temporary project and delete it in `tearDown()`.

### Why `qa/unit` and not `tests/`

`tests/` belongs to the applications: since 2.18.0 it holds an app's own tests (`php caligrafer.php test`, [Testing your app](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/Testing-Your-App)), and projects keep it when they update. The framework's unit tests therefore live in `qa/unit`, which the framework never loads (and which `.htaccess` denies to browsers). Before 2.18.0 the framework also loaded every PHP file of `tests/` on every request.

### Adding a unit test

1. Create `qa/unit/<Something>Test.php` with a `final class <Something>Test extends TestCase` (`use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;`) and `public function test...(): void` methods.
2. If the class under test is not loaded yet, add it to the list of `qa/unit/bootstrap.php`.
3. Keep it independent of the network, the database and `.env`: build objects without their constructor when it reads the request or connects, restore every superglobal (`$_SERVER`, `$_SESSION`) and setting you change in `tearDown()`.
4. Run `vendor/bin/phpunit`.

```php
<?php

use Caligrafy\Errors;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class ErrorsExampleTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testCsrfErrorIsForbidden(): void
    {
        $this->assertSame(403, Errors::status(3000));
    }
}
```
## <a name="fixtures"></a>Mocks and fixtures (`qa/fixtures`)

| Fixture | Used for |
| - | - |
| `openai_mock.php` | OpenAI Responses, Conversations, Files, Vector Stores and models endpoints (Assistant, doctor). Every request is logged to `qa_openai_mock.log` in the temporary folder, so a test can check what was sent |
| `groq_mock.php` | The OpenAI-compatible endpoints of `Agent` and doctor. The first path segment picks the provider: `/openai/v1` (Groq), `/together/v1`, `/fireworks/inference/v1`, `/openrouter/api/v1`, `/ollama/v1`, `/ollama-empty/v1` (no model pulled), `/custom/v1` |
| `coinbase_mock.php` | Coinbase Business Checkouts API. It logs each request with its `Authorization` header to `qa_coinbase_mock.log`, and `cli_tests.php` verifies the JWT signatures |
| `watson_mock.php` | watsonx Assistant v2 (sessions and messages) |
| `smtp_mock.php` | An SMTP greeter for the doctor `mail` check |
| `push_mock.php` | A web push service for the notifications tests: `/ok/*` accepts (201), `/gone/*` answers 410, `/fail/*` 500; each accepted push is logged with its headers |
| `echo.php` | Answers with the request it received (method, URI, body, `Authorization` header) to inspect outgoing calls such as `httpRequest()` |
| `application/` | QA code copied into the generated `application`: `QaController` (errors, uploads, the install module), `BookController` and `Book` (the REST API example of the wiki), `BookPageController` (a page calling a capability), a project `AIController` (a name that collides with an example controller), `Shop/OrderController` (namespaced controller), the Bookshelf capabilities of `services/Books`, the jobs of `services/QaJobs`, the capabilities of the declarative routes in `services/QaRoutes`, and the `Qa` views |
| `books.sql` | Tables of the REST API example |
| `facelogin/` | The face login example of the recipe, with the controllers `FaceLoginController` and `PasskeyController` (the recipe itself now declares these addresses with `Route::action`), the tables (`create_db.sql`) and the client app |
| `docs/` | The components example of the Vue pages of the wiki |
| `outside/` | A file outside the plugin, for the `php -l` hook test |

The mocks are plain PHP scripts served with `php -S` inside the web container (for example `php -S 127.0.0.1:8766 qa/fixtures/openai_mock.php`), and the tests point the framework to them with the base URL settings (`OPENAI_API_BASE`, `GROQ_API_BASE`, `AGENT_API_BASE`, `STRIPE_API_BASE`, `COINBASE_API_BASE`, `WATSON_URL`).
## <a name="addcheck"></a>Adding a QA check

Choose the phase by what the check needs:

+ **Framework code that needs the database or a mock** (models, payments, AI request building): add a `qa_test()` to `qa/tests/cli_tests.php`, in the right `qa_section()`. The helpers of `qa/tests/lib.php` are `qa_test($name, $fn)`, `qa_assert($condition, $message)`, `qa_equals($expected, $actual)`, `qa_contains($needle, $haystack)` and `qa_not_contains()`.
    ```php
    qa_test('endWith() compares the whole needle', function () {
        qa_assert(endWith('caligrafy.php', '.php'));
        qa_assert(!endWith('caligrafy.php', 'xphp'));
    });
    ```
+ **Behavior seen by a browser or an API client** (status codes, headers, routes): add a `qa_test()` to `qa/tests/http_tests.php`. If it needs a route, add it to the routes that `qa/run.sh` inserts into `web.php`, and its controller to `qa/fixtures/application/controllers`.
+ **Files, Caligrafer commands, scaffolds, front-end libraries, the plugin**: add an `ok`/`ko` check to `qa/tests/tooling_tests.sh`. It runs on the host and works in `qa/tmp`.
+ **doctor**: add a variant `.env` and a check to `qa/tests/doctor_tests.sh`.

Make the check fail first (break the code it protects), then make it pass. Never print a secret in a check message.
## <a name="release"></a>Release process

With [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) in the framework repository, the `caligrafy-contributor` skill (`.claude/skills/caligrafy-contributor/SKILL.md`) follows this process after every framework change, then asks whether to review the [course](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill-course) and whether to update and deploy caligrafy.com and Caligrafy Cloud, and ends with a report (plugin, README and wiki, course, and an inventory of every Caligrafy folder with its versions). It is for contributors only: releases leave it out (`.gitattributes`), `php caligrafer.php update` never adds it to a project, and `php caligrafer.php initialize` deletes it from a clone.

The wiki clone is `../caligrafy-quill.wiki`, next to the framework checkout (`git clone https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill.wiki.git ../caligrafy-quill.wiki`).

1. **Claude plugin.** Update what the change touches in `claude-plugin/`: `skills/caligrafy/reference/api-reference.md` and `gotchas.md` (written by hand from the source: a new behavior goes in the API reference, a pitfall found becomes the next `G<n>`, and the range `G1-G<n>` of `skills/caligrafy/SKILL.md` follows), `ui-guidelines.md` when the look changes, every other skill and the `caligrafy-reviewer` agent, read in full against the change.
2. **README and root documents.** `README.md` (keep its banner), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `llms.txt` and `context7.json` (the index for coding agents and Context7: its rules, its links), `claude-plugin/README.md`: change what the change makes wrong or incomplete.
3. **Wiki.** Every page the change affects, read in full. A minor or major release gets a page `Release-notes:-X.Y.0.md`, linked in `_Sidebar.md`; a patch release gets a short `Release-notes:-X.Y.Z.md` too (`php caligrafer.php update` links to the release notes of the exact version it installs). The banner image is only on `Home.md`. Then refresh the plugin's mirrors of the wiki:
    ```bash
    python3 claude-plugin/scripts/sync-wiki.py ../caligrafy-quill.wiki            # rewrite the mirrors
    python3 claude-plugin/scripts/sync-wiki.py ../caligrafy-quill.wiki --check    # exit 1 when a mirror is stale
    ```
    A new wiki page needs a line in the `PAGES` table of `sync-wiki.py` and a row in the reference map of `skills/caligrafy/SKILL.md`.
    Then rebuild `llms-full.txt` (every wiki page but the release notes, in the order of the sidebar, for coding agents):
    ```bash
    php qa/build-llms-full.php ../caligrafy-quill.wiki            # rewrite it
    php qa/build-llms-full.php ../caligrafy-quill.wiki --check    # exit 1 when it is stale (the suite runs this with QA_WIKI)
    ```
4. **Plugin version.** Bump `version` in `claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (minor with a framework minor, patch otherwise), add a line at the top of the changelog of `claude-plugin/README.md`, update the "Current version" line of the [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/10.-Claude-Code-Plugin) page, and validate:
    ```bash
    claude plugin validate ./claude-plugin --strict
    claude plugin validate . --strict             # the marketplace
    php caligrafer.php plugin                     # refreshes Claude Code's copy of the plugin in this checkout
    ```
    The tooling phase fails while Claude Code runs an older copy than the checkout's plugin.
5. **Framework version.** Set `Caligrafy\Framework::VERSION` in `framework/core/Framework.php` ([semantic versioning](https://semver.org): major when projects can break, minor for features, patch for fixes) and add its section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. The `VersionTest` unit test checks the format and the changelog.
6. **Templates changed?** When a file of `framework/settings/application` changed, rebuild the template history:
    ```bash
    php qa/build-template-history.php
    ```
    `framework/settings/template-history.json` holds the sha256 of every version each template file had in the git history (and the working tree). `php caligrafer.php upgrade` uses it to recognize untouched copies in projects that have no `application/.caligrafy-manifest.json`. The tooling phase fails when a current template version is missing from it.
7. **Run the whole suite** with the wiki clone:
    ```bash
    QA_WIKI=../caligrafy-quill.wiki ./qa/run.sh
    ```
    Before the release is tagged, the only expected failure is `caligrafer version` (it compares the version with the tag on the commit). After the tag, `sh qa/tests/tooling_tests.sh` must pass entirely.
8. **Commit, tag and push.** Commit only the files of the change (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`), then tag the release and push `master`, the tag and the wiki. Packagist picks the tag up:
    ```bash
    git tag -a v2.19.0 -m "Caligrafy Quill 2.19.0"
    git push origin master v2.19.0
    git -C ../caligrafy-quill.wiki push
    ```
9. **GitHub release.** Create it from the tag with its `CHANGELOG.md` section as its notes (it is public: the maintainer decides). Until it exists, `php caligrafer.php update` without a version does not offer the release:
    ```bash
    gh release create v2.19.0 --title "Caligrafy Quill 2.19.0" --notes-file <its CHANGELOG section> --latest
    ```
